summary: Review TRIDENT fork code and comparison/baseline/optimization methodology across 8 dimensions, adversarially verify each finding, rank by threat to thesis claims

report.headline: No imputation-side threat survived verification at high severity. The pipeline arithmetic that decides decoder-vs-baseline is correct, and the RQ1 direction is robust: the model is below every plain baseline on 8-9 of 9 tables (Wilcoxon over tables p=0.012; Holm p=0.0156, the floor at n=9), and every adopted ADR direction (0013, 0014, 0015, 0018) holds at table level. What does not hold is the headline as stated. 'Below the bar on 19 of 21' counts seed means. Under the project's own verdict rule it is 16 better / 4 no difference / 1 worse (E35) and 14/5/2 (E34, bar of 5). Against missForest it is 12/8/1, and against the best of all six baselines 9/9/3 (11 with ADR 0018). It is also read against baselines that never got a tuning budget: one alternative hgb recipe already flips kr-vs-kp_40nan to 'baseline better'. It sits on cells every default was chosen on, and at 80nan it rests on ADR 0015's non-deployable checkpoint (wins over mean/mode: 0/3 under H, 2/3 under K). The fixes are mostly reporting plus three runs: an equal validation-only baseline budget, a deployable checkpoint readout, and one frozen confirmation pass on the 14 variants on disk that no run has touched. Classification: the 3-fold sweep cannot be set against Table 3, and classification Optuna still ranks on test macro-F1.

top_threats.title: The RQ1 headline is a count of seed means against the weakest opponent set, read from three inconsistent bar and readout definitions
top_threats.status: new; the bar-of-4 part is known-open (2026-10-07 review finding 6)
top_threats.what: ADR 0017 and the report scripts count a variant as a win when the 3-seed model mean is below the bar mean. The paired 15-fold-pair rule (CI excludes 0, three seeds agree in sign) is never applied to model minus bar. Under that rule the counts are 16/4/1 on E35 (seeds 42/7/13, bar of 4), 14/5/2 on E34 (101/202/303, bar of 5), 12/8/1 against missForest and 9/9/3 against the best of six (11/7/3 with ADR 0018). The means count itself is 19 on E35 but 17 on E34. Three bar definitions coexist: the store's per-run minimum, ADR 0017's pooled min-of-means (softer by up to 0.008), and the reports' min over four names without lgbm. On E34/E35 (decode_checkpoint=loss) the store's headline and gap keys are H, not K, so a store-native query returns 16, not 19, and flips kc2_20nan, credit-g_60nan and kr-vs-kp_80nan.
top_threats.touches: ADR 0017 Outcome :167-176, ADR 0016 :268, the E34-E36 secondary counts in EXPERIMENTATION_LOG, wiki fork-experiments.md:96 (the E30 means count), any thesis 'N of 21' sentence. No ADR decision rests on these counts.
top_threats.direction: Favours the model. Means to verdict costs about 3 variants. Adding missForest to the opponent set costs 7-10.
top_threats.cheap_check: Done read-only (fair_probe_verdicts.py, meansonlyskeptic_probe.py, repro_q3.py). For the store, the pooled 15-pair CI of gap_to_best_baseline and gap_to_missforest rebuilds exactly from each run's mean/std/fold_count; this was verified to 1e-17 on E38.
top_threats.fix: For each opponent (bar of 5, missForest, best of six), report the verdict tally better / no difference / worse on both seed sets. Add the table-level test (8/9 tables, Wilcoxon p≈0.01, Holm 0.0156) and the median relative gap (about -4%) with a seed-level CI. Read everything through one shared helper that selects K vs H by the decode_checkpoint tag and takes the bar from summary.OUTSIDE_THE_BAR. Name the bar definition in ADR 0017's table header.

top_threats.title: Baselines get no tuning budget while the model was configured over E24-E38 on the same variants
top_threats.status: new as a weakness; the fixed bar is a documented decision (ADR 0007 d5, ADR 0016 d7) never reviewed for its effect
top_threats.what: KNN runs at k in {5,10}, and hgb, lgbm and missForest run at library or R defaults. The bar's min-over-baselines step is chosen on test means, but its identity is stable across all six seeds, so it gives the model about 0.000 of cushion. Scoring-only, one alternative hgb recipe (lr 0.05, 200 iterations, depth 3) lowers the bar by 0.010-0.035 on 4 of 6 variants. Under it, kr-vs-kp_40nan becomes 'baseline better' (+0.0136 [+0.0054, +0.0219], all seeds), the kr-vs-kp_60nan and spambase_20nan wins become no verdict, and k=50 flips credit-g_60nan by mean. Caveat: that recipe was picked after seeing seed-42 test, so this is proof that a stronger bar exists, not a measurement of it. The estimated cost is 15 down to 12-14 verdict wins and 19 down to 16-18 by means. Large margins are out of reach of such a grid (vehicle, biodeg, kc2_60nan, and letter/pendigits at about -8% under ADR 0018). Baselines also fit on 70% of rows while the model selects on the validation 10%; this is minor.
top_threats.touches: RQ1 per-variant claims on spambase_20nan, kr-vs-kp_20/40/60nan and credit-g_40/60nan. At 60-80nan the bar is mean/mode (model 0.976-0.992), so a regularised or shrunk booster could land in between. ADR 0007 d5.
top_threats.cheap_check: CPU-only scoring on the cached E35 or E39-D folds. Choose per fold on the validation rows' induced gaps, never on test: KNN k in {5,10,20,50}; an hgb/lgbm grid over lr x max_iter x depth/leaves x min_samples_leaf (about 12 configs); a shrink-toward-mean alpha for 60-80nan. Recompute the verdicts. budgetskeptic_*.py is the template.
top_threats.fix: Write an ADR amending ADR 0007 d5: a declared, validation-only budget per baseline family, the same selection signal as the model, a refit on train plus validation, and the chosen settings logged. Keep the untuned bar as a secondary row. Fix hgb's early-stopping split by original row only; early_stopping=False is harmful (electricity vicprice 0.461 to 1.363).

top_threats.title: No untouched confirmation: every default, file and seed set was chosen on the same 21 variants and one MCAR draw each

The induced cells are fixed per CSV and a seed only re-partitions them, and both seed triples are now spent. Selection optimism on these tables is bounded small. Each adoption has z between -2.8 and -5.9 and keeps its sign on every disjoint 2-fold subset, which bounds optimism at about 0.005 against a gap of -0.0335. M was also confirmed on 17 variants it had never seen, and letter sat outside E37's screen. Generalisation to new tables and new draws is untested. Four margins sit within about one E12 seed SD: credit-g_40nan 0.008, credit-g_60nan 0.008, kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.006-0.014, spambase_80nan 0.013. Fourteen variants exist on disk with zero imputation runs: pendigits/letter/electricity at 40/60/80nan and vehicle/biodeg/kc2 at 40/80nan (electricity_40nan has 2 FAILED runs).

top_threats.title: ADR 0015's default checkpoint uses true values of real gaps: the 80nan wins exist only under it, and no deployed or RQ2/RQ4 run can use it
top_threats.status: new; the mechanism is declared in ADR 0015 but not its consequences (one skeptic known-open)
top_threats.what: DECODE_CHECKPOINT=induced keeps the epoch whose validation gaps score best against the _00nan truth. This is not test leakage, because only validation rows are used. It is selection that no baseline gets and that natural data cannot support: the runner falls back to loss, prints that it did, and tags the run. Below-bar counts by means go 15 to 17 (E34) and 16 to 19 (E35), and verdict wins against the bar of 4 go 13 to 15 and 14 to 16. Wins over mean/mode at 80nan are 0/3 under H and 2/3 under K (kr-vs-kp_80nan, spambase_80nan) on both seed sets. K also improves the masked test cells it never selected on (kr-vs-kp_80nan -0.028 to -0.037), so part of the gain is a better stopping rule that a deployable criterion might recover. That is untested. Under the default, H's test score is no longer produced.
top_threats.touches: ADR 0015; '80% beats mean/mode'. RQ2/RQ4: on natural gaps the run is a different system; under controlled MNAR, K would select epochs on the shifted truth. E39 compounds this, since objective and checkpoint use the same cells. CONSOLIDATED.md:76 ('sibling touched only after best_state') is stale at HEAD.
top_threats.direction: Favours the model: about -0.007 to -0.010 on the mean, plus 2-3 marginal variants. The bar's own test-side min selection partly offsets this, except where mean/mode is the bar.
top_threats.cheap_check: Done read-only for H vs K vs the bar on the 126 E34/E35 parents (adr0015skeptic_q.py, oracleckpt_skeptic_mm.py). Next: one small pre-registered arm on the three 80nan variants using a deployable per-epoch criterion on masked validation cells.
top_threats.fix: Add DECODE_CHECKPOINT=masked: lambda-free impute_score on the fixed hidden_validation mask, using decoding.py:345-352 as machinery and _ValidationGapScore as template. Put it behind a flag and tag, with an ADR. Under the induced default, also score H on test. Report the deployable readout wherever a claim must transfer, and K as an oracle upper bound. Say in the thesis that the default needs labelled gaps.

top_threats.title: The metric pair decides the missForest and categorical verdicts; heavy tails decide kc2/biodeg
top_threats.severity: medium (one skeptic low on the central-tendency half)
top_threats.status: new for the measured flips; the root (§3.5 residue, F-03-2/F-03-4: macro_f1_cat 'used by nothing', commensurability) is known-open
top_threats.affects: imputation (RQ1 vs missForest, categorical and heavy-tailed variants)
top_threats.what: impute_score is a cell-weighted RMSE ratio plus a 0/1-error ratio. mae_num_z and macro_f1_cat are computed but nothing reads them. Against missForest, RMSE+accuracy gives 14/1/6 and MAE+accuracy 9/6/6: missForest wins five variants by 2-8% in MAE, and those are five of ADR 0017's six declared 'ties'. Against the bar, MAE helps the model (17/2/2) and macro-F1 hurts it (12/4/5), but macro-F1 is inflated by rare-label noise (a marginal sampler scores 0.282 on credit-g_80nan, hgb 0.288). Balanced accuracy is the cleaner check. It puts the model at chance on credit-g_80nan and above the mode on kr-vs-kp_80nan, where hgb still beats the model on macro-F1 (+0.071). On kc2/biodeg the top 1% of cells hold 87-98% of SSE in outlier folds, and the same row recurs in every seed. kc2_20nan is undecided under RMSE but worse than knn5 under MAE on both seed sets (+0.054/+0.048). Cell-count weighting hides electricity's day loss (categorical ratio 0.81 vs hgb 0.71). Numeric guesses are not over-shrunk (the sd ratio is above the conditional-mean bound and the slope is 0.77-0.94), but K lowers categorical macro-F1 at 80nan. There is no signed-bias term, which RQ2/RQ4's MNAR arm requires.
top_threats.touches: Any 'beats or matches missForest on N' sentence (gap_to_missforest, ADR 0016/0017); categorical claims at 60-80nan; kc2 and biodeg per-variant claims; the MNAR scoring plan. ADR 0018 holds under RMSE and MAE. ADR 0015's net direction holds, but its 'worse on none' fails on one variant per alternative metric.
top_threats.direction: Mixed. The current pair favours the model against missForest and on categoricals; MAE favours it against the bar.
top_threats.cheap_check: Done (metric_probeB.py, metric_probeB4.py, metricskeptic_e35.py). Extend with balanced accuracy and a column-normalised numeric ratio, computed from raw_fold_metrics.csv and per_column_imputation.csv. Every baseline's per-column errors are already logged.
top_threats.fix: Keep impute_score as the pre-registered primary and add the secondary panel described in methodology_recommendations. Log ratio_num, ratio_cat, the naive denominators and per-column signed bias in score_cells. Claim a result only where primary and per-kind readings agree, and flag kc2_20nan, electricity and the missForest-under-MAE variants explicitly.

top_threats.title: Per-variant inference: 15 dependent fold pairs, no multiplicity control, no smallest effect of interest, and no stated target
top_threats.status: known-open (F-08-4 overlap half, CONSOLIDATED.md:974-990; the pairing half is fixed)
top_threats.what: All 14 report scripts use one Student t over 15 pooled fold pairs (df=14). Seed means vary less than iid predicts (median ANOVA F 0.65; 1.5% at p<0.05 over 272 contrasts), so for 'these rows, this draw' the rule is roughly calibrated. But counts change two- to five-fold across defensible tests (E32 G-M: 11 naive, 8 seed random-effects, 2 N&B), and the set of variants with a verdict changes too. Under a seed random effect, the E31 and E32 heavy-gate readings become 'mixed' and E35 becomes 'safe but weaker'. Family-wise error over 21 null tests is about 0.62, and the sign-agreement rule only takes the per-test rate from 0.05 to 0.044. 13% of verdicts have |Δ|<0.005, though those are large relative to their own variant's seed SD. No ADR outcome flips: 0013 8/9 tables p=0.012, 0014 9/9 p=0.0039, 0015 8-9/9, 0018 robust under every test.
top_threats.touches: Wiki thesis-goals.md:86, trident.md:57, fork-experiments.md:76-82 (counts quoted with no test named); the E31/E32/E35 pre-registered labels; per-variant RQ1 claims.
top_threats.direction: No fixed direction; it overstates certainty.
top_threats.fix: Name the target and the test beside every count. Make the table-level test the primary for method claims. Add a seed random-effects column as sensitivity (N&B is over-conservative for paired arms). Use Holm on veto-direction verdicts. Pre-register a SESOI of about 1% relative and read vetoes as equivalence tests.

top_threats.title: Search and promotion protocol: single-split studies, and E39's rule promotes T where T cannot be told apart from the defaults
top_threats.severity: medium (the overlap and shared-cell parts low)
top_threats.status: known-open (T08, T09; F-07-1, F-07-6/F-08-3 sharpened by the induced objective)
top_threats.affects: imputation (per-variant files, any ADR amending ADR 0005)
top_threats.what: Trials train once on the fixed predefined split, because the trial namespace never sets cv_folds. E39 is complete (30/30 FINISHED). Under the pre-registered tally, credit-g_40nan and kr-vs-kp_40nan read 'promote T' only because the stale F loses to both T and D, while T-D is null (-0.0046 [-0.0146,+0.0054] and -0.0024 [-0.0117,+0.0068]). spambase_40nan reads 'remove file' (D-F -0.0044), spambase_20nan has D better than T (+0.0096 [+0.0015,+0.0177], all seeds), and kr-vs-kp_20nan keeps F. Under the induced objective, about 10% of each CV test fold's induced cells (5.8-12.9%) are the cells that ranked the trials, which voids CONSOLIDATED.md:687-688's dampeners. The bound is 0.0002-0.0023, a direct ledger recompute shows no bias in the predicted direction, and no verdict is within reach. The objective's optimism varies with LR_DECODE, but on spambase that is a validation-to-test shift also seen on masked cells, so only kr-vs-kp_20nan isolates the shared-cell mechanism.
top_threats.touches: The E39 outcome and its ADR; 'tuned' labels in thesis text. The five stale E02 files lack PRETRAIN_GAP_TOKEN and ENCODER_FINAL_NORM (review item 12; inert today). ADR 0008 does not mention the overlap.
top_threats.direction: Favours the 'tuned' label; negligible effect on model-vs-baseline.
top_threats.fix: Apply the pre-registered rule, but state in the ADR that T is indistinguishable from D on both promoted variants, and never call the files 'tuned above the defaults'. The owner decides whether to deviate toward D, which means fewer per-variant knobs. Record the overlap in ADR 0008 and the E39 ticket, and correct the ticket's 'common to every trial' sentence (:148-150). Future searches: use disjoint cells for checkpoint and objective (T08), repeated inner validation (T09), and a promotion gate in code that requires beating D on unseen seeds.

top_threats.title: Exact duplicate rows fall on both sides of every fold (kc2 32%, spambase 11%, letter 9% of test cells)
top_threats.affects: both (absolute numbers; kNN bar; classification CV)
top_threats.what: kc2 has 186 of 522 rows in duplicated feature vectors (6 groups with conflicting labels), spambase 577 of 4601 and letter 2177 of 20000, already present in the raw OpenML files. StratifiedKFold has no grouping, so kNN copies the twin (knn5 on kc2_20nan: 0.113 on twin cells vs 0.646 elsewhere). At HEAD the bias works against the model: removing twins widens its lead (kc2_20nan 0.569 vs 0.559 becomes 0.586 vs 0.598; letter's lead goes from 0.038 to 0.043). ADR 0018's letter gain is the same on non-twin cells (-6.1% vs -5.9%). The kc2_60nan 'loss by 0.012' is stale ADR 0007 data; it is now 0.572 vs 0.717. Every method's absolute impute_score is inflated by 1-4% on kc2, letter and spambase.
top_threats.touches: Thesis sentences of the 'recovers X% of the mean-fill error' kind; 'kNN holds the bar on kc2'; the coming clinical tables (repeated patients).
top_threats.direction: Favours the baselines, chiefly kNN, so it is conservative for the model.
top_threats.cheap_check: dupskeptic_ledger.py and dupskeptic_twinsplit.py over the stored best/worst ledgers (done).

methodology_recommendations: 1. Development vs confirmation (threat 3). Call the 21 variants plus seed sets 42/7/13 and 101/202/303 the development benchmark, freeze the configuration after the E39 decision, and pre-register one confirmation read. It covers the 14 untouched on-disk variants (pendigits/letter/electricity 40/60/80nan, vehicle/biodeg/kc2 40/80nan), 2-3 new OpenML tables, an optional second MCAR draw per small table written to a new suffix (generate_splits.py:202 overwrites in place, so never regenerate into datasets/processed_datasets), and never-used seeds. Before reading it, fix the ADR 0018 inheritance rule for the 40-80nan rungs and add the context-free-row share. Read it once, for the headline.

2. Statistics (threats 1 and 6). Use paired per-fold model-minus-opponent differences on shared folds. The primary claim about the method is cross-table: Wilcoxon signed-rank or a Bayesian signed-rank test (Benavoli et al. 2016) over tables, with Holm across opponents, over 9 tables now and more with the confirmation tables. Report per-variant tallies better / no difference / worse under the project rule as descriptive results, with a seed random-effects column as sensitivity. Report both seed sets, name the test beside every count, and drop 'N of 21 by means'. Pre-register a SESOI of about 1% relative and read 'worse on none' vetoes as equivalence tests.

3. Equal tuning budgets (threat 2). Give each baseline family a declared validation-only selection equal in kind to the model's: KNN k in {5,10,20,50}; hgb/lgbm over about 12 configs of lr x max_iter x depth/leaves x min_samples_leaf; missForest mtry and trees; a mean-shrinkage alpha for the 60-80nan rungs. Select per fold on the same validation signal the model uses, refit on train plus validation, and log the chosen settings. The model gets no new tuning on the confirmation set. Keep the untuned bar as a secondary row so continuity with ADR 0007 stays visible.

4. Symmetric, deployable selection (threat 4). The headline arm for any claim that must transfer to natural or clinical data uses a checkpoint criterion that needs no gap truth: H, or a masked lambda-free per-epoch impute_score. Report K beside it as an oracle upper bound. If K stays the RQ1 headline, give baselines a validation-gap selection of equal strength. Every RQ2/RQ4 arm uses the deployable criterion.

5. Opponent set (threat 1). Report each claim against three opponents: the plain-imputer bar of 5, missForest with ADR 0016's ±0.016 inductive caveat, and the best of all six. The dedicated imputers RQ1 names (ReMasker, CACTI, DiffPuter, TabImpute) are the eventual primary comparison and should go through the same protocol.

6. Metric suite (threats 5 and 8). Keep impute_score as primary. The pre-registered secondary panel: per-kind RMSE ratio, per-kind MAE ratio, accuracy ratio, balanced-accuracy ratio (preferred over macro-F1, which rare-label noise inflates), column-normalised numeric ratio for heavy-tailed tables, per-column signed bias, dispersion ratio and 1-D Wasserstein for numerics, category-frequency total variation, a twin/no-twin split on kc2/letter/spambase, and downstream utility (classify on data imputed by each method vs the complete _00nan sibling). Claim only where the primary and per-kind readings agree; list disagreements.

7. MNAR arms (threat 5, mnar-blind-score). Report raw error and signed bias against the complete truth beside the ratio, plus an MCAR/MAR control sample at equal rate. Under MNAR the ratio stays honest only on the masked population. On the induced population an equally biased imputer moves toward 1, and an imputer that removes bias drops below its MCAR value while its absolute error can grow. Never select checkpoints on MNAR-shifted truth.

8. Search hygiene (threat 7). Use validation-only objectives for both tasks. Use disjoint validation cells for the checkpoint and the objective (T08) and inner repeats (T09). Promote a file only if it beats the no-file default (D) on seeds and rows the study never saw, and log that comparison in the ADR.

9. Cross-level and population readings (threat 9). State dose-response only within table or with table fixed effects, never read the masked population across levels, and complete the cheap ladders (vehicle, biodeg, kc2 at 40/80nan) if a level trend becomes a thesis claim.

10. Classification step zero (classification_notes). Run it on 80/10/10-shaped splits (--cv_folds 10), with an upstream 40/40 arm and a fork 300/150 arm. Tune on validation macro-F1 at the kept checkpoint with the baselines' budget. Pool across tables per missingness level with the seed-sign rule.

finding.title: The default decode checkpoint is chosen with the true values of real gaps; the baselines get no such selection, and real data cannot use it
finding.claim: The mechanism is declared in ADR 0015; its consequences are not. Under the imputation default DECODE_CHECKPOINT=induced, every fold picks its decode epoch (and its early-stopping reference) by the validation rows' own gaps, scored against the _00nan sibling's true values. A deployed imputer never has those values. Four consequences go unstated. (a) The baselines are fixed-hyperparameter imputers with no validation selection at all. The bar does select in the opposite direction: it takes the best of five baselines on CV *test* means. (b) Part of the headline advantage over the bar comes from this oracle criterion. (c) On any table without a complete sibling, which means every natural clinical table for RQ2/RQ4, the runner silently switches to the loss checkpoint. The benchmarked system and the system the thesis would apply are therefore different. (d) In a controlled-MNAR benchmark that has a complete table, the criterion would choose epochs using the MNAR-shifted true values, an oracle on exactly the mechanism under study.

finding.title: The masked companion population is still drawn by the training corruption helper; its realised rate drifts across the ladder and the comment explaining it is wrong
finding.claim: §3.1 is unchanged at HEAD. evaluation_mask still calls preprocess_table. That helper deflates the rate by each row's share of nulls and forces at least one hidden cell into every row that drew none. As a result the masked population's realised rate and composition change with the missingness level: on credit-g_80nan about 81% of its cells come from the per-row floor. The extra-rate segments carry no realised rate. The code comment still claims the rate 'falls as missingness rises', which is not monotone.
finding.evidence: src/training/data.py:163-179 (evaluation_mask wraps preprocess_table); src/utils.py:68-90 (p_base*(1-prop_nulls) and the per-row floor); src/training/decoding.py:217-222 (wrong comment; realised_rate for the primary rate only); src/training/decoding.py:227-243 (extra rates without a realised rate). Probe pipe_probe2.py: 541 masked cells on credit-g_20nan fold 1 against 203 on credit-g_80nan at the same nominal 0.2.
finding.impact: Paired within-variant contrasts are unaffected, because every arm shares the mask per (seed, fold). That covers ADR verdicts and E39's masked contrasts. Any cross-ladder reading of impute/masked, such as a thesis plot of performance against missingness level or ADR 0004's comparability sentence, cannot be interpreted. Induced is the only ladder-comparable population.
finding.cheap_check: Store query: cv/test/impute/masked/realised_rate/mean on parent runs across credit-g_20/40/60/80nan, compared with the configured EVAL_MASK_RATE 0.2.
finding.suggested_fix: Give evaluation its own draw: a flat Bernoulli over observed cells with no deflation and no per-row floor, behind a flag and a tag. Alternatively, strike the cross-ladder comparability claim and use only induced for ladder reads. Fix the comment at decoding.py:217-218 and log the realised rate for every rate segment.

finding.title: The diagnostic best and worst folds, the only folds whose cell ledgers reach the store, are chosen on the masked population while verdicts read induced
finding.claim: The imputation TaskSpec ranks folds on impute/masked/impute_score. _diagnostic_roles uses it to choose best_fold and worst_fold, and only those two child runs get their artifacts (cell ledgers, previews) mirrored into MLflow. The folds a reader opens to see why the headline is poor or good are therefore extremes of the companion population, not of the induced headline.
finding.evidence: src/training/types.py:141 (ranking_metric impute/masked/impute_score); src/training/summary.py:343-360 (_diagnostic_roles on task.ranking_metric); src/training/tracking.py:229-236 (_log_diagnostic_children replays only those roles); src/training/artifacts.py:117-122 (manifest ranking uses the same key).
finding.impact: No metric or verdict changes. Diagnostics can point at the wrong fold for an induced regression. Most induced-only ledgers sit only under the results/ tree.
finding.cheap_check: For a few E39 or E38 parents, compare argmin/argmax over folds of test/impute/masked/impute_score with the same for test/impute/induced/impute_score from the fold records in metrics.csv.
finding.suggested_fix: Rank imputation folds on impute/induced/impute_score when a sibling exists, falling back to masked. Alternatively, choose a second pair of diagnostic children on induced.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. Every link in the chain holds at HEAD b2b50fd, and nothing elsewhere in the code works around it.

1. The imputation TaskSpec ranks on masked. Its `ranking_metric` is `impute/masked/impute_score` (src/training/types.py:139-145).
2. `_diagnostic_roles` picks the best and worst fold on that key only (src/training/summary.py:344-360). `summarize_cross_validation` calls it with no population override (summary.py:77).
3. Only those two folds reach MLflow as child runs. `MlflowTracker.fold_run` yields a `BufferedFoldTracker` that buffers each fold's metrics and artifacts (tracking.py:158-164). `finalize_cross_validation` then replays only the folds named in `diagnostic_roles` (tracking.py:177-186, 229-262). Every fold writes its preview and cell ledger through the fold tracker (runner.py:204-215), so only the best and worst folds' ledgers reach the store.
4. The manifest uses the same key (artifacts.py:117-122).
5. The verdicts read induced. `architecture_size_report.py:58` (E38) and `retune_report.py:44,50` (E39) do, and `selection_replication_report.py:56` uses induced as its headline H. ADR 0004:251-254 names induced as the headline and then tells readers to "open the best_fold/worst_fold children for the preview and cell ledger", which is exactly the misdirection this finding describes. E39 also ranks its Optuna search on `validation/impute/induced` (retune_report.py:44) while fold ranking stays on masked.

**Cheap check.** A read-only script went over all 792 imputation diagnostic manifests in mlruns modified since 2026-10-01, covering E38 and E39. I deduplicated them by artifact source path and all 792 are unique. For each one I compared the manifest with that run's raw_fold_metrics.csv:
- The manifest roles match the masked argmin/argmax in 100% of runs, so the mechanism works as claimed.
- The masked-best fold is also the induced-best fold in only 26.5% of runs, and the masked-worst is the induced-worst in only 31.4%. Chance with 5 folds is 20%.
- Both picks differ from the induced picks in 51.5% of runs, and both agree in only 9.5%.
- In 115 of the 792 runs (14.5%), the child labelled `best_fold` is the induced-worst fold. In 107, `worst_fold` is the induced-best.
- The median per-run Spearman correlation between masked and induced fold scores is 0.20, ranging from 0.03 on pendigits to 0.39 on letter.

So for the headline population, the two diagnostic children are close to a random pick of folds.

**Mitigations, which keep this low.**
- The parent still logs raw_fold_metrics.csv for every fold, with the induced scores (tracking.py:219-227). A reader can therefore find the induced-worst fold.
- The parent also logs per_column_imputation.csv for every fold and every population, induced included (runner.py:230-234; artifacts.py:242-262).
- What is missing for the other folds is the cell ledger and preview, plus the loss histories. For server-run E38/E39 these exist only under the server's /scratch2 results tree; the manifest's retained_artifact_paths point there, and the local results/ tree stops at 2026-09-13.
- No metric, gap or verdict changes.

**Status.** Ranking folds on masked is a documented, deliberate choice: masked exists on every variant, including _00nan (docs/wayfinder/imputation-decoder/issues/05-loss-and-error-metrics.md:78-80; ADR 0014:66). The prior reviews note that only best/worst are replayed (CONSOLIDATED.md:463-466, 817-820) and that the search ranks on masked while the headline is induced (F-08-5, about the Optuna objective). Neither connects the masked fold ranking to which folds become diagnostic children, and ADR 0004:253 actively steers readers to those children. I therefore keep it as new rather than known. The suggested fix stays consistent with the design rationale: rank on induced when a complete sibling exists and fall back to masked on _00nan.

finding.title: The column-wise and [NULL]-path diagnostics now score a row shape the default decoder never trains on
finding.claim: Since ADR 0014 the decode stage shows every real gap as [MASK] in training. The column-wise diagnostic still shows the other gaps as [NULL], and its docstring claims that is 'the row shape the decode stage trains on'. The [NULL]-path diagnostic is likewise fully out of distribution for the default model. E31 measured column-wise before ADR 0014, so it was valid then. A column-wise or null_token readout under today's defaults would compare against a shape the model never saw.
finding.evidence: src/training/decoding.py:275-279 (docstring); :440-452 (other gaps as [NULL]); :261-264 ([NULL] path); src/training/decoding.py:88 and :128 with src/training/types.py:165 (training shows gaps as [MASK] by default); docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:60 (E31 ran under null-gap training).
finding.impact: Diagnostic only, so no headline moves. It could mislead a future token-shape study (T02, RQ3) run under the defaults.
finding.cheap_check: Store query for runs that carry impute/induced/column_wise/* or impute/induced/null_token/* with tag decode_gap_token=mask.
finding.suggested_fix: Under DECODE_GAP_TOKEN mask, show the other gaps as [MASK] in the column-wise path, or refuse the flags. Correct the docstring.

verdicts.reasoning:
Most of the finding holds at HEAD b2b50fd, but it is not new, and the [NULL]-path half is overstated.

What holds. Imputation defaults now set DECODE_GAP_TOKEN to mask (src/training/types.py:165). Under that default the decode stage passes every input through embedder.gaps_as_mask (src/training/decoding.py:88, :128; src/embedder.py:207-236), so a default model never sees [NULL] in decode training. The column-wise path hardcodes [NULL] for the other gaps (decoding.py:441, `shown = frame.mask(frame.isna(), "[NULL]")`) whatever the token setting is. train_and_evaluate_decoder honors score_column_wise without checking decode_gap_token (decoding.py:275-283). The comment at decoding.py:276-278 still says this is "the row shape the decode stage trains on", and so does the CLI help a user actually reads (src/training/config.py:477-479). Both are false under the default. The column-wise runner also passes no decode_gap_token (scripts/experiments/column_wise_run.py:33-45), so rerunning it today scores column-wise under mask. That is the 2026-10-07 code review item 7 (docs/reviews/2026-10-07-code-review-last-two-weeks.md:141-147), still unchecked.

Why this is known, not new. ADR 0014's Consequences already say that both token diagnostics "describe the old model": a mask-trained model never sees [NULL], and the diagnostics measure what they were built for only with --decode_gap_token null (docs/adr/0014-gaps-shown-as-mask-in-the-decode-stage.md:70-72). The owner accepted this as a documented limitation when the ADR landed (2026-10-03). Only the code text and the guard were never updated. Nothing at the point of use enforces it, so the status is known-open, not mitigated.

What is overstated.
(a) The [NULL]-path comment (decoding.py:261-264) never claimed it matches training. It says the head "was never trained at a null position, so this measures whether it transfers there", which is still accurate. It is a transfer diagnostic by design.
(b) [NULL] is not fully out of distribution for the default model. Pre-training still shows gaps as [NULL] (src/training/pretraining.py:103, DEFAULT_PRETRAIN_GAP_TOKEN = "null" at types.py:54), and E36 kept that setting (docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md, E36 row). Only the decode head never saw [NULL]. So the stale-text defect is limited to the column-wise path, and the null-path part should be dropped from the claim.

Why severity stays low. A read-only query of the store found zero contaminated runs. Every parent run with column_wise or null_token metrics is tagged decode_gap_token=null: E31's 126 active runs (column-wise-2026-10-02), the null-path-recheck-2026-09-30 runs and two from 2026-09-17. No run has the tag set to mask. E32's report pairs mask-trained arm G with arm M's null-trained column-wise score (scripts/experiments/gap_token_report.py:9-14, :135), which is valid. No stored number or headline moves. The risk is only to a future T02/RQ3 study run with the flags under the defaults.

Fix: under decode_gap_token == "mask", near decoding.py:275, either show the other gaps through shown()/gaps_as_mask or refuse the flag. Also correct the two text claims, and pin decode_gap_token="null" in column_wise_run.py, which closes review item 7 for that runner.

That is 126 active plus 15 deleted runs in column-wise-2026-10-02, 8 active plus 2 deleted in null-path-recheck-2026-09-30, and 2 untagged runs from 2026-09-17. No run has decode_gap_token=mask.

finding.title: C1 and C2 are still open; their measured effect on the model-vs-baseline comparison is negligible
finding.claim: The scaler and the categorical vocabularies are still fit on the whole variant frame before splitting (C1). The decoder's output space can therefore include categories seen only in test or validation rows, while every baseline's classes come from the training fold. I measured it on all 21 variants at seed 42 with 5 folds: only 8 induced cells (credit-g_80nan) and 5 (kr-vs-kp_80nan) have a true category that is in the vocabulary but absent from the training fold. Those classes are never decode targets, so their logits are only pushed down. C2: every categorical column of a gapped variant has a 'nan' vocabulary entry. It is excluded from the model's heads and from the baselines' classes, and it never reaches an input token, so the effect is symmetric.
finding.evidence: src/training/data.py:73 (scaler fit_transform on the whole frame); src/training/pretraining.py:54-56 (TabularEmbedder on feature_frame); src/models.py:12 and :156-173 (NON_CATEGORY_TOKENS excluded from the heads); src/training/imputation_baselines.py:33-34, :135, :221 (baseline classes from the training fold minus nan/[MASK]/[NULL]). Probe pipe_probe1.py: nan_in_vocab_cols=13/13 on credit-g and 36/36 on kr-vs-kp; vocab_not_in_train=8 and 5; impute_score is scale-invariant (CONSOLIDATED §3.11).
finding.impact: No verdict moves; under 0.08% of categorical cells. It still needs a sentence in the thesis because the pipeline is transductive (BACKLOG C1), and rmse_num_z is in a per-variant unit fit on the scored rows.
finding.cheap_check: Rerun pipe_probe1.py (read-only, about 1 minute) for the other seed sets 7, 13, 101, 202 and 303.
finding.suggested_fix: Leave the protected order alone. State C1 in the methods. If the stage is ever reworked, fit the vocabulary and scaler on the training fold behind a flag and a tag.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding and couldn't. It holds at HEAD b2b50fd, and the cited files have not changed since e2f4e47. Two of its wordings need tightening, but neither changes the conclusion.

What I confirmed:
- **C1 (scaler).** C1 is still open. The scaler is fit before any fold exists: StandardScaler.fit_transform runs on the whole variant frame inside prepare_dataset (data.py:73), and runner.py:93 builds the folds afterwards.
- **C1 (vocabulary).** The TabularEmbedder vocabulary is built from the whole feature frame (pretraining.py:50, :54-56; embedder.py:153-158). TridentDecoder's head output spaces are derived from that vocabulary (models.py:156-173), so the head space depends partly on test and validation rows.
- **Baselines.** Every baseline derives its classes from train_frame, the training indices only (decoding.py:60, :180-190), with nan/[MASK]/[NULL] removed. This covers kNN (imputation_baselines.py:135), HGB (:221), LightGBM (it inherits HGB's fit, lightgbm_baseline.py:30), missForest (missforest.py:110) and mean_mode (pandas mode drops NaN, imputation_metrics.py:136).
- **Decode targets.** The decode stage trains only on train_frame (decoding.py:89, :126-136). A class absent from the training fold is therefore never a target, and cross-entropy only pushes its logit down. Either way the model and the baselines miss that cell together.
- **No leak into the scaler.** It is fit on the gapped variant, not on the _00nan sibling, so induced truths never reach it.
- **C2.** C2 is real. "nan" sits in every categorical vocabulary of every gapped variant: 13/13 columns on credit-g, 36/36 on kr-vs-kp, 1/1 on electricity. Its harm path is closed, though. NON_CATEGORY_TOKENS (models.py:12) removes it from the heads, and _NOT_A_CLASS (imputation_baselines.py:34) removes it from the baselines. Every input path replaces nulls with [NULL] or [MASK] before encoding: preprocess_table (utils.py:47), EpochMasker (embedder.py:76), _clean (decoding.py:659-661), the induced scoring (decoding.py:404, :442, :503) and finetuning (finetuning.py:81-87).

The two wordings to tighten:
1. **"It never reaches an input token."** This is true for the transformer's input. The pre-training target frame, however, encodes the raw train_frame (pretraining.py:92-93), so "nan" ids (and NaN numerical values) do appear there. They never enter the loss, because draw_dynamic_mask never masks an already-null cell (utils.py:78) and the loss reads only masked positions (models.py:64-65).
2. **"impute_score is scale-invariant."** This holds per column, or for one scale shared by all columns. The numerical part of impute_score is a ratio of RMSEs pooled across columns (imputation_metrics.py:49-52, :82). Rescaling each column by its own factor therefore reweights the columns. Swapping the global sigma for a training-fold sigma moves each weight by about the sampling noise, a few percent at most (CONSOLIDATED §3.11 gives a 3% spread in credit-g duration sigma). The effect stays negligible, but "provably immune" overstates it for tables with several numerical columns.

The cheap check is done. I ran a read-only copy of the probe over seeds 42, 7, 13, 101, 202 and 303 and added the masked population.
- **Seed 42.** It reproduces the claimed counts exactly: 8/10400 induced categorical cells on credit-g_80nan and 5/92052 on kr-vs-kp_80nan.
- **Worst cases.** Across all six seeds the highest counts are 8/10400 on credit-g_80nan (0.077%) and 8/92052 on kr-vs-kp_80nan. The masked population has at most 1 such cell per variant and seed.
- **Coverage.** Only credit-g, kr-vs-kp and electricity have categorical columns. The other 13 of the 21 variants (spambase, vehicle, biodeg, kc2, pendigits, letter) have none, so the vocabulary half of C1 and all of C2 cannot touch them.

The "under 0.08%" and "no verdict moves" claims therefore hold on all six seeds.

dims.summary:
The plumbing of the model-vs-baselines comparison is fair. Baselines are fit on the training fold only and see exactly the observed cells the model sees: the same boolean mask, the same truths and the same training-fold mean/mode denominator. The model itself is inductive except for C1. The protocol is not fair on information and tuning, and every asymmetry favours the model.

The model's configuration was chosen across E24 to E38 on these same 21 variants, using both seed triples. A seed only re-partitions the same rows (data.py:218-222). Seven variants also carry per-variant files. Its decode checkpoint is picked with the _00nan truth of the validation rows' real gaps (ADR 0015). The baselines run at library defaults by design (ADR 0007 decision 5): KNN at k=5/10 only, although k=20 was measured stronger. They are fit on 70% of the rows, while the model also consumes the validation 10%.

Over that period the bar count went from 6/21 (ADR 0007 Outcome) to 19/21 (ADR 0017 Outcome) with the baselines essentially fixed. The 19/21 is a count of means. I re-read the 126 E34/E35 run CSVs and the 63 E38 CSVs read-only and applied the project's own verdict rule (15 fold pairs, CI excludes 0, three seeds agree). Model better than the bar of 5: 14/21 on seeds 101/202/303 and 16/21 on 42/7/13. Under the loss checkpoint, which is what real data allows, it is 12 and 14. Against missForest it is 12/21; against the best of all six baselines, 9/21 (11 with ADR 0018's encoder).

ADR 0007's argument that taking the min over baselines makes the bar conservative is true but worth about 0.000: the bar's identity is the same on all six seeds. So nothing offsets the model-side selection.
sound: Q4, same observed cells at impute time. score_baselines hides exactly the scored (row, column) cells and reads fills back at the same positions (src/training/imputation_baselines.py:352-371). Every imputer treats a cell already missing in the frame as hidden too (:93, :164, :296). The masked population's scored cells are exactly evaluation_mask's [MASK] positions (decoding.py:191-195, :201-212, :594-637). gaps_as_mask shows real gaps as [MASK] and leaves masked_positions alone (src/embedder.py:207-237), the same information as the NaN the baselines get. The induced cells are the frame's own gaps (decoding.py:404, :256).

Q2, inductive on both sides. Pre-training trains on train_frame only (src/training/pretraining.py:51, :92, :96, :110). The decode stage trains on train_frame (decoding.py:60, :89, :126). Test rows are first touched at decoding.py:179, after the checkpoint is restored at :174-176. The model is row-local at inference (attention over a row's columns). Every baseline is fit on train_frame (decoding.py:188-190; baseline_cache.py:135-140). KNN donors come from the training matrix only (imputation_baselines.py:144-146). missForest replays its fitted models on the test rows (ADR 0016 decision 2). Pre-training and decode never see test rows' observed values.

Q6, the denominator. mean_mode_baselines is computed on train_frame only, which excludes both validation and test rows (decoding.py:180-182; also :117 for the checkpoint score). Model and every baseline go through the same score_cells with the same mapping (imputation_metrics.py:31-57), and mean_mode scores exactly 1.0 by construction.

Q7, selection effect of the min over baselines. I fixed the bar's identity on seeds 42/7/13 and evaluated it on 101/202/303. Optimism of the per-seed min was 0.000 on every variant: the identity of the four-baseline bar is identical across all six seeds. With lgbm, hgb and lgbm alternate on 6 variants by at most 0.009. So ADR 0007:186's 'errs against the model' is correct in sign but gives no cushion; the min is chosen once per run on the CV mean, not per fold (summary.py:95-108).

The external and withdrawn baselines are kept out of the bar in one place, summary.OUTSIDE_THE_BAR (summary.py:88-92, :105). missForest's own gap uses the same paired arithmetic (:151-185). The percentage gap is a ratio of means, as ADR 0007 decision 9 argues.

The cache key excludes the model's guesses and includes the train and test frames, cell positions, truths and denominators (baseline_cache.py:142-156), so a cached baseline cannot depend on the model arm.

The baseline scores are identical between E34 and E38 cells of the same seed and variant (asserted to 1e-6 in the probe for all four ADR 0007 baselines on 63 cell pairs), confirming they depend only on the folds.

The 15 E38 CSVs with a pre-ADR 0017 missforest column are electricity, letter, pendigits and spambase_60/80nan: numerical tables, which ADR 0017's thread-order correction did not touch. So their missforest values are valid.

E39's double use of the validation gaps (objective plus checkpoint) is acknowledged in advance in docs/tickets/imputation-retune/01-retune-promoted-files.md:147-150; the test split is not used for trial ranking.

missForest's inductive weakening is quantified (ADR 0016:183-189) and carried into ADR 0017's claims as 'ties within 0.016'. The electricity_20nan 'tie' there is against missForest (0.618 vs 0.619), consistent with it losing to the bar (hgb 0.606).

finding.title: The headline uses a checkpoint chosen with ground truth that baselines and real data never get
finding.claim: Under ADR 0015 the decoder's epoch is the one whose validation rows' induced gaps score best against the _00nan sibling. That is supervised selection with the true values of real gaps. No baseline has any analogous access: each is a fixed recipe fit once on the training fold. Some 80nan 'wins over mean/mode' exist only because of this oracle. On real clinical data (RQ2/RQ4) there is no truth, and the run falls back to the loss criterion, so the MCAR headline is a configuration the thesis's own medical study cannot run.
finding.evidence: src/training/decoding.py:111-119 builds _ValidationGapScore from complete_sibling and fold.validation_indices; :161-167 keeps the best-gap epoch; :174-176 restores it. docs/adr/0015-decode-checkpoint-chosen-on-the-validation-gaps.md:26 says 'below the best baseline on 17 variants instead of 15'; :41 is the fallback to loss. docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md E35 counts 16 (H) vs 19 (K) by means. My read-only probe of the E34 and E35 CSVs plus E38 (lgbm/missForest), verdict rule over 15 pairs, seeds 101/202/303, bar of 5: K better on 14, H better on 12; seeds 42/7/13, bar of 4: K 16, H 14. kr-vs-kp_80nan: H 1.0104, above mean/mode, against K 0.9815 (win). spambase_80nan: H 0.9946 (no difference) against K 0.9846 (win). Against the best of all six baselines: K wins 9, H wins 7. E39 adds the induced validation objective on the same cells; this is acknowledged in docs/tickets/imputation-retune/01-retune-promoted-files.md:147-150.
finding.impact: It inflates 'beats the bar' and 'beats mean/mode at 80%' in the model's favour by about 2 verdicts out of 21. It also threatens the claim that the MCAR protocol transfers to RQ2/RQ4, where only the loss or masked-cell criterion is possible.
finding.cheap_check: Already measured read-only (scratchpad fair_probe_verdicts.py: H vs K vs bar from raw_fold_metrics.csv). A complementary check: give one baseline the same privilege on one fold, e.g. choose KNN k or an alpha shrinking hgb toward the mean on the validation rows' induced gaps, and see whether it also drops below 1.0 at 80nan.
finding.suggested_fix: Report the loss-checkpoint (H) or masked-checkpoint score as the deployable headline next to K. If K stays the headline, let every baseline select its own hyperparameters or shrinkage on the same validation gaps. State in the thesis that the default needs labelled gaps.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is in the code at HEAD exactly as the finding says, and the numbers it quotes reproduce to four decimals. Three parts of the finding are overstated, so I downgrade it from high to medium but do not refute it.

What holds:
1. Under DECODE_CHECKPOINT induced, the decode epoch is the argmin of the validation rows' induced impute_score, scored against the complete sibling's true values.
2. Without a sibling the run silently uses the loss criterion.
3. The privilege decides the 80nan story. Under H (loss checkpoint) the model beats mean/mode on none of the three 80nan variants, on either seed set. Under K it beats mean/mode on 2 of 3 (kr-vs-kp_80nan, spambase_80nan), on both seed sets. On those two variants the bar is mean_mode on every seed, and mean/mode has nothing to tune, so the asymmetry there is real.
4. Classification picks its epoch on validation labels, which a real training set always has. True values for real gaps never exist in deployment, so K is not a deployable selection rule.

What is overstated:
- "Inflates": there is no test leakage. The validation rows are disjoint from the test rows, and the baselines are fit on the training rows only. The test score is an unbiased estimate for a procedure that needs labelled validation gaps. The flaw is comparability and deployability, not a biased estimate.
- "No baseline has any analogous access": the bar has its own selection privilege, a worse one. Per run, it is the lowest cross-validated mean over 4 or 5 recipes, picked on the test folds, so the choice of knn5 vs knn10 vs hgb is made on test. This cancels the model's advantage only where the bar is not mean_mode; it does not at 80nan.
- RQ2/RQ4: "the medical study cannot run it" is too strong. With MNAR induced on a complete clinical table, truth exists and K runs. With natural gaps there is no imputation score at all, so no headline to compare. The real risk is different and arguably worse: under induced MNAR, K would pick epochs using the shifted true values of MNAR gaps, which no deployment ever has.

Size of the effect: the mean gain is small (H 0.7542 vs K 0.7446 on seeds 42/7/13). Verdicts against the bar of 4 are 16 for K vs 14 for H, about two of 21.

Status: new. ADR 0015 records the fallback and that the validation gaps are "spent on model selection", but only about how optimistic a search objective becomes. CONSOLIDATED section 3.3 even recommended using the validation induced gaps. The retune ticket's lines 147-150 cover only objective optimism. Nothing records the baseline-fairness or deployability problem.

Fix: report the H (or masked-criterion) score as the deployable headline next to K. Say in the thesis that the default needs labelled gaps. Do not claim "beats mean/mode at 80%" without that caveat.

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts in the finding hold up. The framing ("oracle", "no baseline has analogous access") and the high severity do not, so I'm keeping it but downgrading it from high to medium.

What holds:
(1) Under ADR 0015 the kept decode epoch is the one whose validation rows' induced gaps score best against the _00nan truth. The baselines are fixed recipes.
(2) On both seed sets, kr-vs-kp_80nan and spambase_80nan beat mean/mode by verdict only under K. Under H they show no difference. That is about 2 of 21 verdicts, and the mean over 21 variants moves by about 0.007 to 0.010.
(3) Under the induced default, the loss checkpoint's test score is never computed. So E36 to E39 have no deployable (truth-free) number next to K. This reporting gap is new and is the part worth acting on.

Why it is not high:
(a) The test split is never touched; selection happens on disjoint validation rows. H also selects on labelled validation cells, the self-masked ones. Under MCAR, the induced gaps and the masked cells come from the same mechanism, so K's advantage is mostly resolution (about 80 masked cells vs about 10x as many gaps) and alignment of the criterion with the headline metric. It is not access to a different kind of information.
(b) The key point: K's epoch is also better on the MASKED test population, which it never selected on. On E34, masked K-H is a verdict for kr-vs-kp_80nan (-0.037) and spambase_80nan (-0.024); on E35 both lean the same way. So the gain is a stopping-rule effect: at 80nan the loss criterion overtrained (epochs 25->12, 32->21, 92->61). It is not a fit to the specific gaps, and a truth-free criterion with more masked cells, or patience, could plausibly recover it. That is untested.
(c) The selection asymmetry between the model and the baselines predates K: Optuna, the promoted files and the ADR 0013/0014/0018 defaults were all chosen on truth-bearing variants. K is the newest and smallest step of it. On the other side, the bar is min-over-5 on TEST means (summary.py:95-108). That selection is inert at 80nan, where the bar is mean/mode on every variant that flips, but it favours the baselines at 20-60nan.
(d) The RQ2/RQ4 claim mixes two things. On natural clinical missingness there is no sibling, so the induced headline metric cannot be computed under any checkpoint rule; only the masked metric transfers. There, the pooled masked K-H bounds what the H fallback loses at about -0.028 (kr-vs-kp_80nan) to +0.009 (electricity_20nan). verdicts.reasoning:
Not refuted. Downgraded from high to medium, and its status changes from new to known-open.

WHAT HOLDS. (1) The mechanism is as the finding states. Under DECODE_CHECKPOINT induced, the decoder keeps the epoch whose validation rows' induced gaps score best against the _00nan sibling. The run falls back to the loss when there is no complete table. (2) My read-only re-run of the per-fold CSVs of E34 (seeds 101/202/303) and E35 (42/7/13) reproduces the flip exactly, on both seed sets:
- kr-vs-kp_80nan: H vs mean/mode has no verdict (1.0104 / 1.0100); K wins (0.9815 / 0.9759).
- spambase_80nan: H has no verdict (0.9946 / 0.9971); K wins (0.9846 / 0.9871).
On those variants the bar is mean/mode, so the same two verdicts flip against the bar of four. Counts of wins against the bar of four: 15 K vs 13 H on 101/202/303, 16 vs 14 on 42/7/13, consistent with the finding's numbers. (3) There is also a stale clearance to correct. CONSOLIDATED.md:76 clears the protocol because "the _00nan sibling is touched only after best_state is restored". The wiki repeats this. Under the ADR 0015 default that is no longer true at HEAD: the sibling's validation rows are read every epoch to choose the checkpoint. The test rows are still untouched.

WHY IT IS KNOWN, NOT NEW. ADR 0015 is a documented owner decision with exactly this design:
- Decision 1 selects on the gaps against the complete sibling.
- Decision 3 is the no-truth fallback the finding presents as a threat.
- Consequences says "the validation gaps are now spent on model selection".
- ADR 0015:26 itself cites the bar counts moving (15 to 17 variants below the best baseline) as a reason for adopting K.
- The ADR 0008 amendment and the retune ticket (:147-150) repeat that the same cells are shared.
- The 2026-10-07 code review cleared the ADR 0015 defaults as correct code.
What no review or ADR states: the fairness asymmetry with the baselines, and that two 80nan wins over mean/mode depend on K. Nothing mitigates either, so the status is known-open.

WHY MEDIUM, NOT HIGH.
(a) "No baseline has any analogous access" is overstated. The bar is the best of five baselines, chosen after seeing their cross-validated test means (summary.py:95-108). ADR 0007:185-187 says outright that this favours the baselines. So the comparison is a recipe chosen on test against an epoch chosen on validation. The asymmetry runs both ways. Only the individual recipes (knn k, hgb settings) are untuned, and that half of the claim stands. At 80nan the bar is mean/mode, which has no parameters, so a counterweight there would need a new shrinkage baseline. That is unmeasured.
(b) No test leakage. The gap score uses only fold.validation_indices, so K vs H is a paired held-out result. The 'oracle' is only that validation truth exists, which is the premise of the MCAR benchmark.
(c) The effect is small. It is 2 of 21 verdicts, on variants where K sits at 0.976-0.987, within about 2% of mean/mode. That is a weak claim to begin with.
(d) "The medical study cannot run it" depends on the design. The fallback fires only when complete_sibling is None. Two RQ2/RQ4 designs the owner is weighing, semi-synthetic MNAR and fill-then-delete, give a truth for the injected cells, so in principle they could supply a sibling. The code may need adapting for natural NaNs in that truth. Only a design that uses natural gaps alone forces the loss criterion. There, no method has an imputation score at all.

WHAT TO DO.
- Report H (the deployable loss checkpoint) next to K for the 80nan claims of beating mean/mode.
- State in the thesis that the default needs labelled gaps. It transfers to the semi-synthetic arms but not to an arm with natural gaps only.
- Correct the clearance in CONSOLIDATED.md:76.
- Note that default runs no longer produce H's test numbers. The induced_checkpoint diagnostic is scored only under loss (decoding.py:296), so H needs a second run with --decode_checkpoint loss.

finding.title: 39 rounds of model configuration on the same variants vs fixed baseline defaults
finding.claim: The bar compares a model configured per variant against 5 fixed recipes. The model got global defaults (ADRs 0011, 0013-0015) and per-variant files (5 promoted Optuna files, ADR 0018's two), each chosen by reading test-split scores of these same 21 variants. Both seed triples were spent on decisions, and a 'fresh' seed only re-partitions the same rows. The baselines were never tuned on anything (ADR 0007 decision 5). KNN at k=20 was measured stronger at ≥40% missingness and still left out of the bar. hgb, lgbm and missForest run at library defaults. ADR 0007's statement that the bar 'errs against the model' covers only the min-over-baselines step, which I measured at zero.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core claim holds at HEAD. The baselines are fixed recipes by design, while the model's defaults came out of a sequence of experiments, each scored on the CV test folds of the same 21 variants. All the cited lines check out. Several sub-claims are overstated, though, and the impact is narrower than stated, so I downgrade high to medium rather than refute.

Holds:
- ADR 0007 decision 5 makes the bar fixed by design. KNN_NEIGHBOURS=(5,10); hgb runs at sklearn defaults; lgbm runs at LightGBM defaults (ADR 0017 decision 3).
- The "errs against the model" sentence covers only the min-over-baselines step.
- Every adopted change (ADRs 0013, 0014, 0015, 0018) was decided on cv/test/impute/induced over 5-fold CV of these rows. Both seed triples were consumed. A new seed only re-partitions the same rows (KFold/StratifiedKFold with random_state=seed).
- The move from 6/21 to 19/21 is model-side: the 4-baseline and 5-baseline bars give the same count.

Overstated or wrong:
1. "39 rounds of configuration" and "configured per variant": 14 of 21 variants run global defaults. The decision levers are about four global choices, each pre-registered with a "no variant worse" rule, and three were replicated on the other seed triple with equal or larger effects (E33, E35, E38).
2. The 5 promoted Optuna files were chosen on the predefined validation objective, not on test scores. They have no demonstrated advantage: E03 found the reduced search did not beat the defaults (worse on 4 of 6 pairs), E12 put every tuned-vs-default gap inside seed noise, and E21 found the tuned model beats the bar nowhere. E39 is re-testing them now.
3. "Baselines never tuned on anything" is slightly wrong. knn10 was added after E20 measured it better on the same seed-42 test folds, so the KNN size set was itself chosen by reading test scores.
4. k=20 is immaterial on the documented numbers. Where it improves on k=10 (credit-g_20nan 0.938, spambase_20nan 0.925, kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.850), hgb/lgbm already sit lower (0.936, 0.865, 0.772 in the same table). On pendigits, a KNN-bar variant, k=20 was not lower. Distance weighting was worse on 21 of 27 variants.
5. ADR 0018 did not target "where knn10 had beaten the model". By E35 the model already beat knn10 on letter and pendigits with paired verdicts. The size rule was chosen before E38 ran, and the one post-hoc exclusion (electricity) changes no verdict.
6. "19/21" is a count of means (ADR 0017), not a verdict count, and the wiki's thesis-goals does not state it as a thesis claim.

Check I ran (read-only, fold artifacts plus store; lgbm approximated by a mean shift because its fold values are not in the CSV): under the paired verdict rule at HEAD's configuration, the model wins on 15/21 variants on seeds 42/7/13 (E35, K readout) and 15/21 on seeds 101/202/303 (E34, K readout), with letter and pendigits under ADR 0018 from E38. Most wins are 0.02 to 0.17 below the bar, far beyond what a plausible baseline grid recovers. Letter and pendigits under the bigger encoder win by 0.039 and 0.031. The finding's thin-margin list is partly moot:
- kr-vs-kp_40nan: no verdict on seeds 42/7/13; a marginal win on 101/202/303 (CI upper bound −0.0003).
- spambase_20nan: a win on 42/7/13 (upper bound −0.0045); no verdict on 101/202/303.
- kr-vs-kp_20nan: wins on both triples, upper bounds −0.0125 and −0.0077.
- kr-vs-kp_80nan and spambase_80nan: the bar there is mean/mode.
These are the variants where a validation-selected GBDT grid could plausibly flip a win, so the cheap check should focus on them.

The unaddressed risk is real but confined to about 3 to 5 variants. Thesis text should report verdict counts, not mean counts, and state that the baselines run at defaults. Status: the baseline-side asymmetry appears in no prior review or backlog item, so it is new. The model-side test-reuse half overlaps the known-open CONSOLIDATED §3.3 (F-07-2, F-07-6, F-08-3) and F-11-1 (untouched test split), with E39 a partial mitigation in progress.

verdicts.reasoning:
Part of the finding holds. The baselines run at library defaults and were never tuned. Both seed triples were spent on decisions. A new seed only re-partitions the same rows, and the induced cells are the variant's own gaps, so they are identical across seeds. Two parts are overstated: how the asymmetry arises and how large it is. It affects no ADR decision.

Sub-claims refuted:
(1) "Configured per variant via 5 promoted Optuna files chosen on test scores" is wrong on two counts. The files were chosen on the validation masked objective, not on test. They also did not help: E03 found the promoted files worse than the defaults on 4 of 6 pairs, and E17 found the credit-g files hurt. They are neutral or a handicap, and E39 is re-testing them now.
(2) "ADR 0018 targeted the two variants where knn10 beat the model" uses stale 09-28 numbers. In E35, before ADR 0018 and with the small encoder, the model already had paired verdicts below knn10 on both:
   - pendigits: gap -0.0176 [-0.0205, -0.0146];
   - letter: gap -0.0136 [-0.0162, -0.0110].
   The user fixed the table-size rule before E38 ran. After ADR 0018 the margins are 8.3% and 8.7%, with upper bounds of -0.028 and -0.036. The finding's "0.004 to 0.02" does not apply to letter or pendigits.
(3) knn20 was measured to help on credit-g_20nan, spambase_20nan and kr-vs-kp_40nan. On each, hgb or lgbm already sets the bar 0.02 to 0.09 lower, so knn20 would move no bar.
(4) The test-set reuse is not where the risk sits. The global defaults came from a few decisions, each pre-registered with its rule fixed in advance and replicated on the other seed triple. Their effects (for example E32/E33 G better on 11 and 13 of 21, mean -0.02 to -0.05; E30 M on pendigits/letter -0.05 to -0.07) are far above any selection optimism from choosing among 2 to 4 arms. None of these ADRs used the baselines in its rule: every comparison was model arm against model arm, paired.

What remains is a plain hyperparameter-tuning asymmetry on the headline count. I recomputed it read-only from the E35 K readout (today's default except the two ADR 0018 variants), fold values from raw_fold_metrics.csv, with lgbm folded in as a per-seed mean shift (an approximation, because lgbm fold values are not in the CSV):
   - mean below the bar on 19 of 21, which matches ADR 0017:167;
   - paired 15-fold verdicts under the protocol: MODEL better on 15, BAR better on 1 (credit-g_80nan), none on 5 (credit-g_40nan, credit-g_60nan, electricity_20nan, kc2_20nan, kr-vs-kp_40nan).

Wins at risk from a small baseline grid, judged by upper bound:
   - spambase_20nan: -0.0045, about 0.5% of the bar; likely to flip;
   - kr-vs-kp_20nan: -0.0125, about 2%; possible.
   - spambase_80nan (-0.0086) and kr-vs-kp_80nan (-0.018) have mean/mode as the bar. There a tuned GBDT would have to fall from 1.04-1.07 to below about 0.99, a bigger ask than the margin suggests.
   - Mean-only wins at risk: kr-vs-kp_40nan and credit-g_40nan, both about 0.8%.

Plausible gain scale from evidence in the repo: two different GBDT default recipes (hgb and lgbm) differ by up to 0.016 on single seeds, and lgbm moved the 5-baseline bar by at most 0.009 (ADR 0017:169). missForest, an iterated forest also at defaults, is an upper envelope for tree imputers, and the model is still lower than it on 20 of 21 by mean. My estimate is that tuning would cost 1 to 3 paired wins (15 down to 12-14) and 1 to 3 mean wins (19 down to 16-18). Every shift favours the model, and none reverses the comparison: more than 10 verdicts have margins of 2.4% to 20% that defaults-tuning cannot plausibly close.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core asymmetry survives a re-read and no prior review covers it. CONSOLIDATED.md (2026-09-11..18) is older than the baseline imputers (ADR 0007, 2026-09-24). The 2026-10-07 review's baseline items (#6, #10) are bookkeeping bugs, and BACKLOG has nothing on this (I3, ReMasker, is a different issue). The fixed bar is a deliberate, documented choice (ADR 0007 decision 5), but nobody has raised what it does to the "19/21" claim. Several pieces of the evidence are wrong or overstated, though, so I am downgrading high to medium.

What holds:
(1) The global imputation defaults were adopted from cv/test induced impute_score on the same 21 variants: ADR 0013 from E30, ADR 0014 from E32 and E33, ADR 0015 from E34 and E35. Both seed triples were used for these decisions.
(2) The induced population is the fixed gaps of each _XXnan file. A "fresh" seed re-partitions the rows and re-scores the same cells. Ticket 03's "Known limits" concedes it "replicates over seeds, not over datasets".
(3) The below-the-bar count climbed with each model-side decision: A 7, M 11 (E30), G 16 (E32), K 19 (E35). Meanwhile the baselines got no hyperparameter search at all: KNN_NEIGHBOURS=(5,10), and hgb runs at scikit-learn defaults.
(4) The "19 of 21" is a tally of point estimates, and several margins are 0.006 to 0.018.

What does not hold:
(a) The 5 promoted Optuna files were not "chosen by reading test-split scores". They were picked on a single predefined validation split. Those validation rows reappearing in the CV test folds is already known as F-08-3 (SOUND/medium, CONSOLIDATED §3.3:680, still open). The files also don't favour the model: tuned did not beat defaults in 11 of 12 comparisons (ADDENDUM §3). In E17 the credit-g files were worse than defaults, and the credit-g_20nan file was removed. ADR 0013's Consequences says the old arm A still led on 3 of the 5 promoted variants. So they are at best neutral for the model.
(b) ADR 0018 plays no part in the 19/21. ADR 0017's table comes from E35 (2026-10-04), three days before ADR 0018 (2026-10-07). With the small encoder the model was already below knn10 on pendigits (0.332 vs 0.350) and letter (0.459 vs 0.473). Those two flipped through the global defaults (E30: −0.068 and −0.054), not per-variant tuning. The finding's "exactly the two where knn10 had beaten the model" quotes the pre-default ADR 0007 numbers.
(c) Leaving out k=20 most likely changes no verdict. Every place k=20 was measured lower is a variant where hgb or lgbm holds the bar by a wide margin. On the variants where KNN is the bar, E20 reports no k=20 gain: kc2, where k=5 beats k=10, and pendigits/letter at 20nan.
(d) The bar was not entirely static. knn10, hgb and lgbm were each added after test results showed they were stronger. missForest, compared outside the bar, still trails the model on 20 of 21 induced variants. Six of those wins are ties within the 0.016 band.

What remains, at medium severity: the defaults were tuned on test, which cannot help the baselines and can only make the model look better, and the baselines got no hyperparameter search. Nothing has measured how big the selection optimism is or what a tuned baseline would score. Mitigating: the model decisions were few, global, pre-registered and replicated, with effects larger than these margins. The open exposure is the ~5 thin-margin variants and the 60–80nan variants where mean/mode is the bar. A regularised booster could edge just below 1.0 there. The cheap check the finding proposes (a baseline grid selected on validation, CPU only) is the right next step. So are a clean confirmatory pass on pendigits/letter at 40/60/80nan, which no decision has touched (ADR 0018 decision 3), and a third seed triple no study has used.

finding.title: The 'below the bar on 19 of 21' headline counts means, not the project's verdict rule
finding.claim: Every report and ADR outcome counts a variant as a win when the model's mean is below the bar's mean. The paired verdict rule (CI excludes 0 and three seeds agree in sign), which the project applies to every model-vs-model decision, is never applied to model vs baselines. Applied, the count falls by 3-5 variants, and kc2_20nan changes sign between seed triples.
finding.evidence: scripts/experiments/selection_replication_report.py:236-245 counts `below[arm] += mean < base`; ADR 0017:167 '19 of 21' and :170 '20 of 21' against missForest. Probe, seeds 101/202/303, today's default K (old encoder on pendigits/letter): against the bar of 5, 14 better / 5 no difference / 2 worse (credit-g_80nan, electricity_20nan). Seeds 42/7/13, bar of 4: 16/4/1. Against missForest: 12/8/1. kc2_20nan: knn5 0.5216 < model 0.5363 on 101/202/303, but model 0.541 < knn5 0.567 on 42/7/13.
finding.impact: The headline number in fork-experiments and in the thesis overstates the model's position, in its favour.
finding.cheap_check: Already computed read-only (scratchpad fair_probe_verdicts.py). Re-run it on the E39 D arm once it finishes.
finding.suggested_fix: Report the verdict-rule tally of better / no difference / worse against the bar, against missForest and against the best of all six, beside the means count. Use the parent's gap_to_best_baseline intervals pooled over seeds.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the core of the finding, but it needs three corrections, and those support a downgrade from high to medium.

What I confirmed at HEAD b2b50fd:
- Every report script that compares the model with baselines does it by means only, e.g. `below[arm] += mean < base`.
- None of them applies the 15-pair verdict (CI excludes 0 and all three seeds agree in sign) to model minus bar. The same scripts do apply that verdict to every model-vs-model contrast.
- My own read-only probe reproduced all of the finding's tallies (numbers in the evidence field).

Correction 1: "never applied" is too strong. ADR 0007, "How to compare", defines a paired win reading: `gap_to_best_baseline/impute_score` with `ci95_upper < 0`. ADR 0017 decision 2 adds `gap_to_missforest` with the same arithmetic. Both are logged on every parent with `ci95_*` keys. E19 read model vs bar with intervals ("never clearly"), and E21 and E24 used a disjoint-interval rule. What is missing is narrower: no report or ADR outcome pools these over seeds or applies the three-seed rule to the bar.

Correction 2: the impact claim puts the headline in the wrong place. "19 of 21" appears only in ADR 0017:167. It is not in `fork-experiments.md`, `thesis-goals.md` or `trident.md`, and no thesis text exists yet. What does spread is the means-count practice:
- `fork-experiments.md:96` carries E30's "11 for M, 7 for A".
- The log carries means counts for E34, E35 and E36.

The scripts label their line honestly ("variants whose mean is below the best baseline"), and ADR 0017's table header says the cells are seed means. ADR 0017 already marks six of its 20 wins over missForest as ties within the 0.016 band. Where it slips is ":167-169", where a means count borrows verdict wording ("moves no verdict").

Correction 3: the size of the drop. Against the bar, on the same population, the count falls by exactly 3 on both seed triples. "3-5" mixes a means count on 42/7/13 with a verdict count on 101/202/303. Against missForest the drop is larger than claimed: 19 to 12, that is 7.

One partial offset: the bar is picked per seed as the minimum test mean over the baselines, which biases it against the model (ADR 0007 says so). So the means count is not one-sidedly in the model's favour, though the noise effect dominates on the variants that flip.

Why medium rather than high:
- ADR 0017's numbers are correct as means.
- Nothing is published.
- No ADR decision rests on the 19. ADR 0017 decided where missForest sits, ADR 0018 decided encoder size.
- The paired per-run gap is already in the store, so the fix is a report line plus an ADR amendment.

The case for keeping it high is that RQ1's central claim will be exactly this count, and the error runs in the model's favour.

CONSOLIDATED F-08-4 (unpaired intervals) is the ancestor, and ADR 0007 decision 9 answered it per run, not pooled over seeds. No earlier review flags the baseline count itself.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is real. Since E30 the reports count a variant as "below the bar" when the pooled mean is below the bar's pooled mean, and ADR 0017's Outcome prints "19 of 21" and "20 of 21" in bold. Re-running the probe read-only gives the same numbers. The finding overstates how much this matters, though, and gets several details wrong.

1. **The drop is 3, not "3-5".** On the same seed triple the count falls by exactly 3 each time. E35 (42/7/13): 19 below on means, 16 better / 4 no difference / 1 worse by the rule. E34 (101/202/303): 17 below, 14 / 5 / 2. The "5" only appears when E35's 19 is set against E34's 14, which mixes seed triples. The three that move on E35 are credit-g_40nan, credit-g_60nan and kc2_20nan. All three become "no difference"; none becomes a loss.

2. **It isn't only in the model's favour.** The means count also inflates the losses: on E35 it shows 2 variants above the bar where the rule finds 1 worse, and on E34 it shows 4 above where the rule finds 2. No variant flips from better to worse. Both "worse" verdicts (credit-g_80nan, electricity_20nan) are ones the means count already puts above the bar. kc2_20nan changes sign between triples but is "no difference" in both, which is what a tie looks like on a small table.

3. **No decision rests on these counts.** ADR 0017 keeps missForest outside the bar because the owner wants the bar to show how the model sits among ordinary baselines (ADR 0017:12-20), not because of the tally. ADRs 0013-0018 were decided on model-vs-model paired verdicts. Pre-registrations label the below-the-bar count as Secondary. When beating the bar was the decision criterion (E21), the rule was stricter still: the model's upper bound had to be below the bar's lower bound. E19 reported "never with disjoint intervals".

4. **"Never applied" is overstated.** ADR 0007 defines `gap_to_best_baseline` as a paired per-fold difference whose `ci95_upper` below 0 is "the paired reading of a win". `summary._paired_gaps` logs it on every parent, and ADR 0017 decision 2 adds a paired `gap_to_missforest`. What is missing is only the pooled three-seed version of that verdict in the reports.

5. **ADR 0017 already qualifies the missForest count.** Right after "20 of 21" it says six of those wins fall within the 0.016 band ADR 0016 measured between the inductive and transductive versions, and calls them ties. That leaves about 14, close to the rule's 12 / 8 / 1 on the other triple.

6. **The impact statement is wrong today.** The wiki has no "19 of 21" or "20 of 21" baseline count anywhere. fork-experiments.md gives E19's "6 of 21, never clearly", E30's "11 variants" and a qualitative ADR 0016 line. No thesis text exists yet.

7. **Today's default doesn't change the picture.** On pendigits and letter the ADR 0018 encoder is clearly better than both the bar and missForest.

What remains is a reporting gap that could mislead later. A thesis sentence reading "19 of 21" should say "16 better, 4 no difference, 1 worse". The verdict-rule tally is cheap to add, and the suggested fix is sound. No prior review lists this: CONSOLIDATED F-08-4 is about unpaired intervals in the Optuna comparison, and finding 6 of the 2026-10-07 review is about which baselines make up the bar in this same count. So the status stays new, at low severity.
