verdicts.reasoning:
The core claim holds when the code is re-read and the probe re-run. From E30 on, the model-vs-bar tallies count a variant when its mean is below the bar's mean, and the three-seed, 15-pair verdict rule is never applied to them. Under that rule the count drops by 3 on the same seeds and the same bar. No prior review or backlog item files this. Code review #6 is about which baselines make up the bar (4 vs 6). The line-308 note ("Four --tally paths print counts without the ticket's pre-registered verdict") is about arm-vs-arm tallies that lack their ticket's "reading" line. CONSOLIDATED §3.7 F-08-4 asked for paired model-vs-model differences. So the status is new, with partial mitigation.

Three parts of the finding are overstated, so severity drops from high to medium:

(1) "Never applied to model vs baselines" is false. ADR 0007 decision 9 logs a paired per-fold gap with a CI on every parent, and its "How to compare" section calls ci95_upper<0 "the paired reading of a win". E19 reported "never with disjoint intervals". The optuna-full tickets 01-03 and imputation-pretraining/01 required disjoint intervals before saying "beats the bar". So this is a drop in rigour from E19, not a rule that was never applied.

(2) The impact claim is false at HEAD. The wiki's fork-experiments.md, thesis-goals.md and trident.md contain no "19 of 21" or "20 of 21". The thesis is not written yet. The overstatement lives only in the ADR 0016/0017 Outcome bullets, the EXPERIMENTATION_LOG secondary lines and the report scripts' stdout. Those tables are labelled as means over three seeds, and ADR 0016:279-280 points to the paired intervals in the store.

(3) Against missForest, the ADRs already discount near-ties. ADR 0016:274-278 and ADR 0017:172-175 call six wins inside the 0.016 inductive-vs-transductive band "ties, not wins". That leaves 14 on seeds 42/7/13 and 13 on 101/202/303, against 12 under the verdict rule. So the missForest half is largely mitigated. The bar half (19 vs 16) has no such discount.

kc2_20nan does not flip its verdict: the CI includes 0 on both seed triples. Only the mean changes sign, which argues for the fix rather than showing a defect in the verdict.

No decision rests on these counts. ADRs 0013-0018 decided on arm-vs-arm verdicts, the pre-registered tickets list best-baseline counts as Secondary, and the qualitative reading (the model beats the ordinary bar on most variants) survives. What remains is a reporting inconsistency in the model's favour, cheap to fix before it reaches RQ1. One small sign of the wording slipping: ADR 0017:168-169 says lgbm "moves no verdict" about a comparison of means.

finding.title: missForest is outside the bar by choice, and the wiki still describes the superseded ADR 0016 bar
finding.claim: ADR 0017 removed the strongest standard baseline from the bar because it would set the bar on most variants. That makes the headline bar weak by design. The missForest kept outside it is itself handicapped: R defaults, inductive and untuned. Against the best of all six baselines the model wins 9/21 by the verdict rule (11 with ADR 0018), not 19. The wiki hasn't absorbed ADR 0017: it says missForest is in the bar and lists the withdrawn LightGBM missForest as available.

Wiki projects/trident/trident.md:58 says 'missForest baselines ... added to the baseline bar'. projects/trident/fork-experiments.md:125 and :129 give ADR 0016's six-baseline bar and 476/873 with no ADR 0017. projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:141 says 'missForest (Random Forest and LightGBM, already in the fork, ADR 0016)'. Probe against the best of six: 9 better / 9 no difference / 3 worse (credit-g_40nan, credit-g_80nan, electricity_20nan).

finding.suggested_fix: Make 'best of all baselines including missForest' the thesis headline and the plain-imputer bar the secondary reading. Update trident.md, fork-experiments.md and thesis-goals.md for ADR 0017 (missforest_lgbm withdrawn, single-pass lgbm in the bar) and ADR 0018.

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts mostly check out at HEAD, but the framing is overstated in three places. I am downgrading the finding, not refuting it.

1. **Leaving missForest out of the bar was a documented decision, and missForest is still scored.** The bar is the best of mean_mode/knn5/knn10/hgb/lgbm. missForest is external and lgbm-missForest is withdrawn (summary.py:88-92, missforest.py:6-8). ADR 0017 lists "leave missForest in the bar" as a considered and rejected option, with its reason (:99-100). Every parent run still logs gap_to_missforest with paired fold gaps (ADR 0017 decision 2, :34-38). ADR 0017's Outcome reports the model against missForest next to the bar (:170-175). It also already treats six induced wins inside ADR 0016's 0.016 inductive-vs-transductive band as ties. So the bar is weaker on purpose, the weakness is stated in the ADR, and the stronger comparison is computed on every run. That is a choice about the thesis headline, not a hidden defect.

2. **"Handicapped missForest" is partly misattributed.** The R defaults (100 trees, mtry 1/3 or sqrt, leaf 5 or 1, R stopCriterion; ADR 0016 decision 4) are canonical missForest, not a weakened version. The inductive protocol matches how the model itself is scored. ADR 0016's Bias section measures the forest moving by at most 0.016 when fitted transductively, "in no consistent direction": better on five rows, worse on two (0016:183-185). The "up to 0.067" figure belongs to the withdrawn missforest_lgbm, not to the forest that stays. "Untuned" is true, but it applies to every baseline.

3. **"9/21 (11 with ADR 0018), not 19" mixes two counting rules.** The 19 is a comparison of 3-seed means on seeds 42/7/13 against the bar of 5 (ADR 0017:167). The 9 and 11 are verdict-rule tallies on seeds 101/202/303. I rebuilt them from the reviewer's own probe output (scratchpad barcheck_out.txt), comparing the model to whichever of the six baselines has the lowest mean (induced population):
   - Seeds 42/7/13, bar of 5, verdict rule: 16 better / 4 no difference / 1 worse.
   - Seeds 101/202/303, bar of 5: 14 / 5 / 2.
   - Same seeds, best of six: 11 / 7 / 3, with credit-g_40nan, credit-g_80nan and electricity_20nan worse. This reproduces the finding's 11 and its worse-list.

   So the drop from 19 to 11 splits into about 3 from switching means to the verdict rule, 2 from the change of seeds, and only 3 from adding missForest. On the masked population, best of six gives 12 / 8 / 1, against 15 / 6 / 0 for the bar of 5. Against missForest alone, the model is better on 14 of 21 induced and 17 of 21 masked by the verdict rule. Caveats: the best baseline is picked by 3-seed mean, not run by run; I did not check the variant without ADR 0018 that gives the "9".

4. **The wiki pages are stale, not wrong.** trident.md:51 and fork-experiments.md:166 pin their read to commit 41e7881 (2026-10-06 14:49). ADR 0017 (2295f50, 19:51 the same day) and ADR 0018 (acb8c99, 10-07) came after it. The reflog shows the local checkout stayed at 41e7881 until a pull on 2026-10-15 at 23:37. So trident.md:58, fork-experiments.md:125/:129 and thesis-goals.md:141 were accurate for the commit they cite. The uncommitted thesis-goals.md diff does not touch line 141. At HEAD the fork does contain a LightGBM imputer, the single-pass lgbm, so thesis-goals.md:141 is wrong only about which LightGBM. The "favours the model" impact needs a premise: a reader who applies the stale definition to HEAD-era "beats the bar" numbers. The stale pages themselves describe the stronger, six-baseline bar.

**What remains:** the wiki needs a refresh for ADRs 0017 and 0018 (new, low). The thesis should report missForest alongside the bar, ideally as best of six under the verdict rule, rather than the bar of 5 alone. That is a reporting recommendation, already enabled by gap_to_missforest.

**Adjacent issue, still open at HEAD:** 2026-10-07 review finding 6. The report scripts hardcode a four-baseline tuple and leave out both lgbm and missForest: architecture_size_report.py:44, selection_report.py:37, gap_token_report.py:37, pretrain_gap_token_report.py:38, and now E39's retune_report.py:41. So the fork's own experiment reports read a bar different from the one in the store.

finding.title: Baselines learn from 70% of the rows while the model also consumes the validation 10%
finding.claim: Both sides fit on the training fold. The model also uses the validation rows: pre-training validation loss, the decode loss mask and, under ADR 0015, the truth of the validation gaps. The baselines need no selection step, yet they never see those rows, so they get 14% fewer rows than the like-for-like budget.
finding.evidence: src/training/data.py:226 validation_ratio = 0.1/(1-1/cv_folds), i.e. 70/10/20. src/training/decoding.py:60-61 and :188-190: BaselineScorer(train_frame) only. src/training/baseline_cache.py:135-140 fits on self._train_frame. src/training/pretraining.py:52 and :93 use the validation frame. ADR 0016:183-185: extra rows move missForest by up to 0.016 and LightGBM by up to 0.067 on small or categorical tables.
finding.impact: Small but in the model's favour, concentrated on the small tables. In the probe, thin margins include credit-g_20nan vs missForest (-0.016, no verdict), kr-vs-kp_20nan vs bar (-0.019) and kr-vs-kp_40nan (-0.008).
finding.cheap_check: Build BaselineScorer with pd.concat([train_frame, validation_frame]) on fold 1 of credit-g_20nan and kr-vs-kp_20nan and score the same induced cells with cache_dir=None, about 15-60 s each. Defer until the CPU probe ends.
finding.suggested_fix: Fit baselines on train ∪ validation. If they get tuned (see the tuning-asymmetry finding), tune on validation, then refit on both.

verdicts.reasoning:
The asymmetry in the code is real. Under 5-fold CV the split is 70/10/20, the model's gradients come from the training rows only, and the baselines are fit on those same training rows and nothing more. The validation rows are never offered to the baselines. Beyond that, the finding overstates both how the model uses those rows and how much harm it does, so I downgrade it from medium to low.

(1) The model does not learn from the validation 10%. Every optimizer step in pre-training and in decoding runs over train_frame only, so on learning budget both sides have exactly the same 70%. The validation rows are a selection holdout, which is the usual benchmark protocol.

(2) Two of the three uses the finding lists do nothing under the imputation defaults (cosine LR, decode_checkpoint=induced, decode_patience=0):
- Pre-training's validation loss is only logged, because only the plateau scheduler reads it.
- The decode loss on the fixed validation mask picks best_state, but by_gaps discards that state.
- No early stopping runs.
What is left is ADR 0015: choosing one of 450 decode checkpoints on the validation gaps' truth. That is information the baselines could not get even if they were fit on train plus validation, because they only fit observed cells.

(3) The arithmetic is wrong. 70% against 80% is 12.5% fewer rows; 14.3% is the extra share that train plus validation would add.

(4) The cited impact evidence does not support "in the model's favour". ADR 0016 refit on the test rows plus training rows, about 29% more rows, which is twice the validation increment. missForest moved by at most 0.016 with no consistent direction. On credit-g_20nan induced, the finding's own example, more rows made missForest worse (0.855 to 0.869), and that comparison already has no verdict. The 0.067 LightGBM gain belongs to missforest_lgbm, an iterated transductive imputer that is withdrawn and never set the bar. It is not the single-pass lgbm that is in the bar.

(5) The project already partly mitigates this for missForest. ADR 0017 reads induced wins inside the 0.016 band as ties, and that band was measured on a larger row increment than the validation rows. For the bar members (knn, hgb, lgbm) nobody has measured it. kr-vs-kp_20nan's margin of -0.019 to -0.022 is larger than any plausible effect of +14% rows. kr-vs-kp_40nan's margin of -0.006 to -0.008 is within reach, so only that one could flip, and the cheap check is still worth running once the CPU is free.

No prior review records this validation-row asymmetry (CONSOLIDATED.md, the 2026-10-07 review, BACKLOG.md), so the status stays new.

The core defect holds at HEAD. All 14 *_report.py scripts still take "best baseline" as the minimum over ("mean_mode", "knn5", "knn10", "hgb"). Under ADR 0017 decision 1, the store's bar is every baseline not in summary.OUTSIDE_THE_BAR, so it includes lgbm. No guard elsewhere reconciles the two, and review finding 6 is still unchecked. 1. **The 15 early E38 CSVs are not why the bar is wrong.** Both live reports compute the bar from the reference cells, not from the arm cells: architecture_size_report.py:161 uses `_best_baseline(r)` and retune_report.py:173-174 uses `present["F"]`. Those reference cells are E34's (selection-2026-10-03). All 63 E34 raw_fold_metrics.csv files carry only the four ADR 0007 columns. Adding lgbm to the tuple would therefore raise a KeyError on every reference cell. The bar can only come from the store, which is what finding 6 already said. "Wider than reported" overstates what is new.

2. **Twelve of the 14 scripts are frozen analyses, not live defects.** They analyse experiments pre-registered and concluded under ADR 0007's bar of four, and their reference CSVs have no lgbm column. Only architecture_size_report (E38) and retune_report (E39) are read under ADR 0017.

Both live helpers hard-code `impute/induced/` (architecture_size_report.py:143, retune_report.py:156), so the masked gap (0.016 on kr-vs-kp_20nan) never reaches them. On the reference seeds 101/202/303, the reports' per-seed bar of four sits above the store's `baseline/best` on 7 of 21 variants, by 0.0004 to 0.0059:

finding.title: The hgb training copy doubles the rows, switches on leaky early stopping and fixes a 20% hide rate
finding.claim: Each column's booster trains on its observed rows plus a copy with 20% of the feature cells hidden. On pendigits (about 6,150 observed rows per column at 20nan) the doubling crosses scikit-learn's auto early-stopping threshold of more than 10,000 samples, which would otherwise stay off. letter and electricity are over it anyway. The internal validation split is drawn from the stacked original-plus-copy matrix, so near-duplicates sit on both sides and early stopping is optimistic. The 20% rate is a constant tied to EVAL_MASK_RATE, not to the variant's missingness. Neither is tuned. The mechanism itself (teaching the booster where gaps go) is sound.
finding.evidence: src/training/imputation_baselines.py:51 _TRAINING_HIDE_RATE=0.2; :241-244 vstack of features and the hidden copy, target duplicated. .venv/Lib/site-packages/sklearn/ensemble/_hist_gradient_boosting/gradient_boosting.py:533-534 do_early_stopping_ = n_samples > 10_000; :556 train_test_split for the validation fraction. ADR 0017 decision 3 notes hgb stops early on large tables while lgbm trains all 100 rounds.
finding.impact: Negligible for verdicts. On the large tables the bar is knn10 (pendigits, letter) or hgb on electricity, where the bar already beats the model. lgbm, without early stopping, lands within 0.006 of hgb.
finding.cheap_check: On one pendigits_20nan fold, refit hgb with early_stopping=False and with the copy excluded from the early-stopping split. Compare induced impute_score.
finding.suggested_fix: Pass early_stopping=False, or split validation by original row before stacking the copy. Optionally draw the hide rate from the observed missingness.

verdicts.reasoning:
Not refuted on the code: the mechanics are exactly as cited. Each column's booster stacks its observed rows with a copy that has 20% of the feature cells hidden, and duplicates the target (imputation_baselines.py:241-244, rate at :51). _fit_one never passes early_stopping (:268-275), and nothing on the caller path overrides it (decoding.py:188 -> BaselineScorer -> fit_baseline_imputers :317-333). That leaves sklearn 1.9.0's "auto" setting in force, which turns early stopping on above 10,000 samples (gradient_boosting.py:533-534) and draws the validation split from the stacked matrix (:556). Row counts check out: pendigits has 6,132-6,197 observed rows per column in the training fold and 12,264-12,394 after stacking, so the copy is what pushes it over 10,000. letter (about 11.2k observed) and electricity (about 25.4k) are over the threshold anyway. Twins of the same row do land on both sides of the internal split.

The substance is overstated, though. I ran the finding's own cheap check on fold 0, seed 42, single thread, and it came out null:
(1) Early stopping is switched on for all 41 columns of the three large tables (16 pendigits, 16 letter, 8 electricity numeric, plus electricity's categorical `day`, fitted as a classifier) but fires on only one: electricity `vicprice`, at 15 rounds. Every pendigits and letter model ran the full max_iter=100, so on pendigits the threshold crossing only holds out 10% of the stacked rows. The effect on mean column nRMSE is 0.3437 with early stopping on versus 0.3422 with it off, and letter gives 0.4947 versus 0.4939. Those are noise-level gaps, on tables where knn10 sets the bar anyway (ADR 0017:158-159).
(2) The leak's optimism is real in direction but tiny. On vicprice, the stacked split stopped at 15 rounds and a split by original row at 13. The stacked version scored better (0.461 vs 0.564).
(3) The suggested fix early_stopping=False is harmful. vicprice goes from 0.461 to 1.363 nRMSE, worse than the mean fill, on electricity, the one large table where hgb is the bar (ADR 0017:151, hgb 0.606 against the model's 0.618). Early stopping helps there, so the fix would weaken the bar exactly where it binds. The bar falls back to lgbm (0.612) anyway, so no verdict would move.
(4) "Not tied to the variant's missingness" is misframed. The training features already carry the variant's own gaps, because the copy is made from a matrix that already has NaN at the variant's rate (:228, :239-242). The original rows therefore match the induced population, and the extra 20% matches the masked population's EVAL_MASK_RATE default of 0.2 (types.py:235). (5) "Neither is tuned" is documented policy, not an oversight. :36-38 says a baseline is a fixed bar rather than something a run tunes, and :47-51 ties the rate to ADR 0004 on purpose.

Status is new. Grepping CONSOLIDATED.md, the 2026-10-07 review and BACKLOG.md finds only decoder early stopping. finding.title: C1: the scaler and vocabularies are fit on the whole table, which helps only the model, and negligibly
finding.claim: Still open at HEAD (protected in BACKLOG). impute_score is exactly invariant to it, as CONSOLIDATED §3.11 verified. Tree baselines (hgb, lgbm, missForest) and mean/mode are invariant to per-column affine scaling. KNN distances use the same globally scaled columns as everyone, a 1-3% column-weight difference with no consistent direction. The only one-sided effects favour the model: its input normalisation includes test-row statistics, and its vocabulary includes categories seen only in validation or test rows, which baselines can never answer (ADR 0007 decision 2: one cell on kr-vs-kp's spcop).
finding.evidence: src/training/data.py:67-71 StandardScaler.fit_transform on the whole frame before build_folds. src/training/pretraining.py:53-55 TabularEmbedder(df=feature_frame). src/embedder.py:149-158 vocabulary from np.unique over the whole column, including 'nan' (C2, also open). src/training/decoding.py:419-423 pushes the sibling's truth through the same scaler.
finding.impact: No verdict or thesis claim at risk. Mention it in the methods as a deliberate transductive preprocessing step.
finding.cheap_check: None needed for fairness. Optionally refit the scaler on the training fold for one credit-g run and confirm impute_score is unchanged to six decimals.
finding.suggested_fix: State it in the thesis. If the pipeline is ever made per-fold, fit the scaler and vocabularies on train ∪ validation.

verdicts.reasoning:
The defect is real at HEAD (b2b50fd), in the place the finding names, and BACKLOG C1 still lists it as open and protected. Its low severity holds. But four of the finding's supporting claims fail when I re-read the code and run a probe, and they should be corrected before anyone repeats them.

What holds:
- prepare_dataset fits StandardScaler on the whole frame (data.py:70-73). build_folds runs only afterwards (runner.py:75 then :93).
- The embedder gets the whole feature_frame (pretraining.py:50, :54-55) and builds each vocabulary with np.unique over the full column (embedder.py:153-158).
- The sibling's truth goes through the same scaler (decoding.py:419-423).
- AGENTS.md:7 protects the split/scaling order.
- Pre-training trains only on train rows (pretraining.py:51, :92-118). Every baseline is fit on the train fold only (imputation_baselines.py:317-333, missforest.py:262-270), with a vocabulary from that fold alone.

Corrections:
1. "impute_score is exactly invariant" is false. score_cells pools z-RMSE across all numerical columns (imputation_metrics.py:49-52), so each column's weight depends on its sigma. Changing the scaler changes those weights. I held the raw predictions fixed (a train-fold median imputer) and swapped the whole-table scaler for a train-fold one: the ratio moved at the third decimal, by up to 0.0033. The §3.11 check could not catch this. "Scaled RMSE equals raw RMSE over sigma" is true by definition and never compares a global sigma with a train-fold sigma.
2. The cheap_check would fail. impute_score will not be "unchanged to six decimals", even with predictions fixed. The model would also retrain under a per-fold scaler.
3. "A 1-3% column-weight difference" understates it. The largest |sigma_train/sigma_global - 1| per fold is 2-10% on credit-g and 19-77% on biodeg_60nan. The 3% in §3.11 is a different quantity: one column's sigma compared across the missingness ladder.
4. "Helps only the model" has the wrong mechanism. KNN reads the already-scaled frame (imputation_baselines.py:107, :152-153), so its distance weights depend on test-row statistics too. In my probe, KNN5 on the numerical columns moved by up to 0.025 per fold and about ±0.003 averaged over folds, with no consistent sign. On credit-g the repo's KNN also has one-hot blocks (imputation_baselines.py:154-159), which dilute the effect, so those credit-g numbers are an upper bound.

The vocabulary effect is negligible in both directions. The decoder excludes only [MASK], [NULL] and "nan" (models.py:12, :158-173), so a category seen only in the test fold is in its output space. But it is never a training target, so its logit is only ever pushed down and the model in effect cannot produce it. In the other direction, an observed category seen only in the test fold reaches the model as an embedding that never received a gradient. The baselines treat that value as a gap (imputation_baselines.py:285-290, missforest.py:251-256), so this one works slightly against the model.

Smaller points:
- mean_mode is invariant only because its ratio is exactly 1 (numerator equals denominator), not because of affine invariance.
- The tree baselines are approximately, not exactly, invariant. HGB's early-stopping loss on tables over 10000 rows and missForest's stopping statistic (missforest.py:234-236) are both computed in scaled units.
- C2 is mitigated for imputation, not fully open. "nan" is still in the vocabulary (embedder.py:153), but it is excluded from the decoder's output space (models.py:12, :158-173).
- ADR 0016 measured an analogous inductive-versus-transductive swap at 0.016 at most, with no consistent direction.

None of this endangers a verdict built on paired fold differences, because the model and the bar are scored in the same units on the same cells. Low severity stands. The thesis wording should drop the claims of exact invariance and of one-sided help.

dims.summary:
I checked the hyperparameter-optimization methodology at HEAD b2b50fd (read-only). I read opt.py, types.py, config.py, the decoding, finetuning and data code, ADRs 0005, 0007, 0008 and 0013-0018, the optuna-full and retune tickets, EXPERIMENTATION_LOG E02-E39, and the prior reviews (CONSOLIDATED, ADDENDUM, the 2026-10-07 review, BACKLOG, TASKS). I also ran small read-only probes against mlflow.db (mode=ro) and the split files. The scripts are in the scratchpad: hpo_overlap.py, hpo_e39_trials.py, hpo_e39_means.py.

**Bottom line.** The imputation search itself never reads test data. Its objective is validation-only, it is seeded, and since E21 every study has been pre-registered. The trouble is the protocol around it, not the code:
- **Benchmark reuse.** Every default-changing decision (ADRs 0013, 0014, 0015, 0018) and every per-variant file decision was taken on the same 21 variants. Those are also the variants the headline comparison with the baselines uses.
- **Fresh seeds do not give fresh cells.** A new seed re-splits the folds and redraws the masks. The induced cells are fixed by each CSV, so every replication re-scores the same cells. All six seeds in the record have now fed a decision.
- **Baselines get no tuning budget.** By ADR 0007 decision 5 they run at library defaults. A k=20 KNN that E20 measured as stronger at 40% missingness or more is left out of the bar.
- **Classification still ranks trials on test macro-F1.** Per the owner, the paper's TRIDENT numbers came from that mode.
- **The induced objective adds a small leak.** Under `--search_objective induced`, the search scores the exact cells (same truth) that later sit in the confirmation test folds: about 10% of each fold.
- **The objective is biased, and the bias is not the same for every trial.** It is a minimum over 450 epochs on the same cells that choose the checkpoint. On the E39 studies its optimism tracks LR_DECODE, which contradicts the ticket's "common to every trial". The "effective filter, useless ranker" pattern persists even without ties.
- **E39 is complete in the store** (30 of 30 cells FINISHED), but the pre-registered tally has not been run. Preliminary per-seed means show the re-tuned winner no better than the defaults; on spambase_20nan it is worse on all three seeds.

**Proposed protocol:**
1. Use validation-only objectives for both tasks. For classification, take macro-F1 on the validation rows at the restored checkpoint, which finetuning.py:163-168 already computes every epoch.
2. Use disjoint validation rows or masks for checkpoint selection and for the search objective (T08).
3. Score each trial on an inner k-fold or several splits, or run nested CV with the search inside each outer training portion (T09).
4. Give each baseline family an equal, declared budget, selected on the same validation induced gaps.
5. Build one untouched confirmation set: new MCAR draws written to a separate suffix (generate_splits.py overwrites in place at seed 42), seeds never used, and ideally 2-3 new OpenML tables. Read it once, for the thesis headline.
6. Gate promotion in code: promote a winner only if it beats the defaults on seeds and rows the study never saw (E39's arm design, built in). Retire any seed set once it has decided something.
7. Report the existing 21-variant results as development-set results.
sound: The imputation search objective is validation-only. TaskSpec imputation ranks by validation/impute/{masked,induced}/impute_score (src/training/types.py:97-104, 139-145), which decoding.py:345-363 scores on fold.validation_indices only. No test or cv/test key ranks an imputation trial, and ADR 0008 explicitly refuses ranking by the induced test cells (docs/adr/0008-selectable-search-objective-population.md:71-72).

Trials are seeded and failures are not scored. TPESampler(seed=args.seed) (opt.py:483), and a crash raises TrialPruned instead of returning 0.0 (opt.py:314-321), which would have been the best score under minimisation.

Configuration flags reach every trial (opt.py:238-239, CONFIGURATION_FLAGS at src/training/config.py:33-36). Held knobs take today's task defaults through the override path (config.py:95-97), so E39's trials and its T/D arms train the same system. The E39 ticket's check 1 confirmed this to the last digit.

E39's confirmation design is sound in the respects that bias a verdict, apart from the overlap finding. Arms run on seeds 101/202/303, which the study (seed 42) never trained on; pairs share folds and masks; the rule was pre-registered; there is no --promote_best or --retrain_best. All 30 T/D cells are FINISHED in mlflow.db (read-only count by tags experiment=retune-2026-10-15, is_mirror=false).

The induced objective removed the tie problem. Each of E39's five studies has exactly one trial at the best objective, against two tied trials in each cosine kr-vs-kp study under the masked objective. Winner ranks on test induced improved to 12, 6, 10, 14, 4 of 40 (mean 9.2), against 15-17 in the masked era (ADDENDUM §2).

No classification promoted file exists at HEAD. find datasets/hiperparams lists only seven *.imputation.json files, so the fork's classification default sweep did not read a test-tuned configuration and the F-07-4 fallback is not live today.
Promoted files are now tracked in git (git ls-files datasets/hiperparams lists all seven; history goes back to fcaadfb), so F-12-3, 'untracked and one git clean from gone', is fixed.

E18's 'best-induced trial' control used the test score only as an explicitly labelled oracle control, and nothing was promoted from it (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:453-468; ADDENDUM §8.8, line 458, says selecting on the induced test score would be leakage).

Baselines are fit on the training split of the same fold and scored on exactly the model's cells, with the same naive denominators (decoding.py:183-189; ADR 0007). The bar is chosen once per run on the CV mean, never per metric or per fold (summary.py:95-108), which if anything favours the baselines.

Pre-registration discipline holds from E21 on (tickets in imputation-optuna-full/ and imputation-retune/ were committed before launch, with stopping rules). Deviations are recorded rather than hidden: E17's fourth seed was added past the stopping point, and E38's adoption was narrowed to two variants.

The overlap measurement agrees with the stored cell counts: credit-g_40nan validation rows hold 777 induced cells against the 771 the critique recorded. Splits are 800/100/100, 2556/320/320 and 3679/461/461, matching CONSOLIDATED §3.3 (scratchpad/hpo_overlap.py).

finding.title: Imputation defaults were tuned step by step on the evaluation benchmark; no untouched confirmation set exists
finding.claim: Each default-changing ADR was adopted from studies on the same 21 variants that later produce the headline model-vs-bar counts: E30 led to ADR 0013, E32/E33 to ADR 0014, E34/E35 to ADR 0015 and E37/E38 to ADR 0018. The per-variant file decisions (E17, E39) used the same benchmark. Fresh seeds re-split the folds, redraw the masks and re-initialise the model. But the induced population is a fixed set of cells, set by the fixed MCAR seeds of each CSV, so every replication re-scores the same 21 cell sets against the same truth. Every seed in the record has now served an adoption or file decision: 42/7/13 (E30, E32, E35, E36, E37) and 101/202/303 (E33, E34 -> ADR 0015 before its replication, E38, E39). The baselines went through no comparable selection. Counterweights, which belong in the claim: each step was pre-registered with a 'no variant worse' rule; the adopted effects (E32/E33 mean -0.02 to -0.05, E38 -3.8%/-5.6%) are far above the seed SD of E12 (0.007-0.014); and the bar itself is picked on test CV means. So no single ADR is likely a false positive. What is at risk is the reported level, the headline counts (for example 'below the best baseline on 19 of 21', E35/E36), and any small per-variant margin.
finding.evidence: docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:869-870 (E30: 21 variants, seeds 42/7/13), :969-977 (E32 -> ADR 0014), :986-988 (E33 on 101/202/303), :1039-1043 (E34 -> ADR 0015 adopted before E35), :1067-1075 (E35 on 42/7/13), :1150-1173 (E38 -> ADR 0018), :1072-1073 and :1101-1102 (below the best baseline on 19 of 21); datasets/generate_splits.py:16,202 (fixed MCAR seeds, so fixed induced cells, written in place to processed_datasets); src/training/types.py:159-168 (today's defaults are the product of those decisions); src/training/summary.py:95-108 (bar chosen on test CV means, a partial offset)
finding.impact: Favours the model. It threatens the RQ1 thesis claim of how often, and by how much, TRIDENT beats the baseline bar, and any generalisation to new tables or new missingness draws (and, more so, to the MNAR settings of RQ2/RQ4). The individual ADR decisions are probably robust given their effect sizes.
finding.cheap_check: Read-only first: per variant, compare the latest gap_to_best_baseline (mean and CI) with the E12 seed SD. Variants whose margin is within about one SD are the ones a held-out draw could flip. Then one pre-registered run: regenerate the MCAR draws with a new base seed into a separate directory or variant suffix (never overwrite the benchmark), on seeds never used (for example 404/505/606). Score the frozen configuration and all baselines once.
finding.suggested_fix: Freeze the configuration space. Declare a confirmation benchmark that no decision may read until the thesis headline: new MCAR draws of the 9 tables, 2-3 new OpenML tables and unused seeds. Label the 21-variant numbers as development-set results in the thesis.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core claim survives a re-read. Every default-changing decision was adopted on the same 21 variants that then produce the headline. The induced cell set is fixed per CSV, and every seed in the record has served a decision. No document declares a held-out set. Each citation checks out at HEAD:
- E30 used 42/7/13.
- E32 led to ADR 0014 and was replicated by E33 on 101/202/303.
- E34 led to ADR 0015, adopted before E35 replicated it.
- E38 led to ADR 0018.
- The log records 19 of 21 below the bar at :1073 and :1102.
- The MCAR seed is 42+pct at generate_splits.py:16,202.
- The CV folds are a shuffled KFold (data.py:218-221), so the union of the test folds is every gap in the variant at every seed.

Nothing in the known reviews covers it. CONSOLIDATED §3.x (F-07-2, F-07-6, F-08-3) covers Optuna's winner's curse and leakage of the predefined split, not the sequential adoption of ADRs. Neither BACKLOG, TASKS.md, the 2026-10-07 code review nor the wiki pages mention a confirmation set. So the status is new.

I downgrade it from high to medium, for four reasons:

1. **The fixed-cells mechanism is weaker than stated.** The benchmark already holds independent MCAR draws of the same tables: four each for credit-g, kr-vs-kp and spambase, and two each for vehicle, biodeg and kc2. inject_nans gets a separate RNG for each rate and draws from the complete frame each time, so the levels are not nested. Every adoption rule required "no variant worse" across all 21. A gain tied to one draw would have had to hold on several independent draws of the same table. What is truly untested is generalisation to new tables, which is a limit of scope.

2. **"No untouched confirmation set exists" is overstated.** Fifteen non-benchmark variants of the same nine tables exist on disk, each an independent MCAR draw: vehicle, biodeg and kc2 at 40/80nan, and pendigits, letter and electricity at 40/60/80nan. A read-only query of mlflow.db finds zero imputation runs on 14 of them. electricity_40nan has only 2 FAILED runs from 2026-09-11. So a draw-level confirmation is possible today without regenerating any CSV. Only the table-level holdout and the unused seeds are missing.

3. **The size of the effect on the headline is small, and mostly noise, not selection.** The per-variant table in ADR 0017 (E35 K readout) shows the model ahead of the bar by 0.013 to 0.145 on 16 of the 19 variants. Only three margins sit inside about one E12 seed SD: credit-g_40nan (0.008), credit-g_60nan (0.008) and kr-vs-kp_40nan (0.006). The worst case is therefore about 16 of 21, not a reversal. Those three are sensitive to any redraw, whether or not there was selection. Each adoption step chose among two to four arms and was replicated on a second seed set. With effects of that size, winner's-curse optimism on the level should be small.

4. **The baselines claim needs a nuance.** The bar's own composition was re-decided on this benchmark. ADR 0017 moved missForest out of the bar after it set the bar on 11 of 21. This barely changes the counts: the model is still below missForest on 20 of 21 induced, and ADR 0016 reported 18 of 21 against a bar that included it. The baselines' own hyperparameters were never tuned, at library defaults (ADR 0017 decision 3). That asymmetry does favour the model, as the finding says.

Net: a real but standard development-set limitation, worth labelling in the thesis and checking cheaply on the 15 untouched variants. It is not a high-severity threat to RQ1.

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts in the finding check out, so it is not refuted. It is downgraded from high to medium because the mechanism it names, a fixed set of induced cells, can do almost no harm. What actually limits the results is the fixed set of tables and the untuned baselines. That is a labelling and external-validity caveat for the thesis; no ADR or verdict changes.

What holds:
- The MCAR draws are fixed: each level uses seed 42 + pct and the files are written in place. A fresh seed therefore re-scores the same cells against the same truth.
- Every seed set has served a decision. ADR 0015 was adopted on 101/202/303 alone, before E35. E33 called those seeds "unused".
- The defaults at HEAD are the product of that sequence of decisions.
- No prior review files this: it is absent from CONSOLIDATED.md, the 10-07 review, BACKLOG and TASKS, and from the wiki's projects/trident pages. F-11-1 (Optuna trials log test scores) and F-07-6 (the predefined validation rows reappear in the CV test folds) are adjacent but narrower.

Why the fixed-cell mechanism is weak:
1. The model never sees the truth of the induced cells; it comes from _00nan only at scoring time.
2. Each variant has hundreds to tens of thousands of cells, so the draw-to-draw variance of a mean is small.
3. The bar is scored on exactly the same cells (ADR 0007), so a new draw moves both sides of the model-vs-bar gap together.
4. The five decisions are generic structural choices, and the global ones were made on verdict counts over 21 variants under rules fixed in advance. Their winning margins (E30 9/0, E32 11/0, E33 13/0, E35 6/0 with the mean negative on 19 of 21) mean adoption barely depended on any variant's draw, so the expected optimism in the level is close to zero.
5. ADR 0018 is the one per-table choice. Its gains (-3.8% and -5.6%) sit far above pendigits' own CI (about ±0.001), and pendigits and letter were already below the bar before it, so it does not change the count.
6. The bar is min-of-5 on test CV means, a winner's curse in the bar's favour that pulls the opposite way.
7. One per-variant file decision runs against the model. On credit-g_40nan, the variant with one of the thinnest margins (-0.008), E17 kept a promoted file that was worse than the defaults (+0.018, paired +0.023) "on hold", and E39 still lists it as the current file.

The finding's cheap_check (regenerate the MCAR draws with a new seed) therefore tests the wrong thing. Only the "2-3 new OpenML tables" part of the suggested fix addresses the real risk: overfitting to these 9 tables, plus the tuning asymmetry against untuned baselines.

Rough size, from the E35 table (K against the best baseline):
- Thin margins: credit-g_40nan -0.008, credit-g_60nan -0.008, spambase_80nan -0.013, kr-vs-kp_40nan -0.014, and kc2_20nan -0.025 with a very wide CI (K - H -0.036, CI -0.107 to +0.034).
- The yardstick: E12's seed SD of 0.007-0.014 was measured on credit-g only, so a 3-seed mean has an SE of about 0.004-0.008.

"Below the best baseline on 19 of 21" is a count of point estimates. It could read about 15-17 on new tables or draws, but mostly through ordinary noise, which a CI-based count should report anyway, not through bias from adaptive selection. That is a few variants crossing the bar, not a sign change for RQ1.

Status update on F-07-6: its third dampener in CONSOLIDATED.md:688 says the search "never touched" the induced population. That stops holding for E39. Its reduced studies use the induced objective on the predefined split (opt.py:210, no cv_folds), whose validation rows make up 8.5-13% of the CV test folds. Any file E39 adopts carries a small optimism, roughly the min-of-40 winner's curse on the validation score times about 10% overlap, a few thousandths. E39 is in progress, so no decision has used it yet.

The remedy keeps its value. Label the 21-variant numbers as development-set results. Report the bar comparison as a count of CI-backed verdicts rather than point estimates. Add a few new tables that no decision reads, with an untouched missing-value draw on each of them. A new MCAR draw on the existing 9 tables on its own is low value.

finding.title: Classification Optuna still ranks trials by test macro-F1; the paper's TRIDENT numbers came from that mode
finding.claim: Confirmed at HEAD. TaskSpec('classification', 'f1_macro', ..., 'f1_macro') makes the search objective the fold's f1_macro. The trial namespace sets no cv_folds, so build_folds loads the fixed per-base predefined split. The fine-tuning stage restores the validation-loss checkpoint and then scores only the test rows, and run_from_namespace returns that single fold's metrics, so opt.py ranks trials by macro-F1 on the predefined test rows. --promote_best writes the shared <dataset>.json. Every classification run reads that file, including CV runs whose test folds contain those same rows, and imputation runs fall back to it when they have no file of their own (F-07-4). Per the owner, the paper's TRIDENT numbers came from this mode while its baselines were tuned on validation. The fork's classification path is clean today only because no shared file exists: datasets/hiperparams holds only *.imputation.json.
finding.evidence: src/training/types.py:138; opt.py:209-242 (no cv_folds), :285 (score = metrics[search_objective]), :577-581 (promotion); src/training/config.py:104-106 (imputation falls back to the classification file), :119-127, :200; src/training/data.py:50, 186-201 (per-base split, seed-independent); src/training/finetuning.py:180-198 (test-only fold metrics); src/training/cli.py:21-26; Wiki references/trident-paper.md:206; Wiki projects/trident/thesis-goals.md:152
finding.impact: Favours paper TRIDENT over its baselines. The fork sweep (0.858/0.799/0.742/0.661/0.531) and the paper (0.843/0.813/0.756/0.711/0.581) differ in three ways: untuned defaults against per-dataset test-tuned configurations, 3-fold CV against the single predefined split, and no test selection against test selection. The fork's shortfall at 20-80% therefore cannot be read as a replication failure, and an unknown part of it is the paper's optimism. Running opt.py for classification to reproduce the paper would reproduce the leak, and through the shared file it would contaminate later CV and imputation runs.
finding.cheap_check: Read-only: list any stored classification Optuna trials (is_optuna=true, task=classification, is_mirror=false). If there are any, compare each study's best objective with that trial's finetune/val_f1_macro and with a 5-fold CV run of the winner on a seed other than 42. The drop estimates the test-selection optimism.
finding.suggested_fix: Make the classification search objective validation macro-F1 at the restored checkpoint, which finetuning.py:163-168 already computes every epoch. Refuse --promote_best for classification until that change lands. For the paper replication, retune TRIDENT and the baselines on validation inside each outer fold (nested CV) with the same budget, as thesis-goals.md:152 plans.

verdicts.reasoning:
The defect holds at HEAD (b2b50fd), and every cited line checks out. I found no guard that neutralizes it.

1. A classification trial ranks by test macro-F1. The classification TaskSpec sets search_objective='f1_macro'. opt.py builds the trial's Args by hand, with no cv_folds attribute. CONFIGURATION_FLAGS does not include cv_folds either, so even `--cv_folds` passed to `main.py --use_optuna` never reaches a trial. As a result config.py:200 yields None and build_folds loads the fixed per-base predefined split. finetuning.py restores the best checkpoint by validation loss (:181), then scores only the test rows (:184-191). cli.py:25-26 returns that fold's metrics, and opt.py:285 ranks by them. score_search_objective is set only for imputation (opt.py:233). No guard in main.py or opt.py refuses a classification study or `--promote_best` for classification.
2. Promotion and fallback are as claimed. hyperparameter_file(dataset, 'classification') resolves to the shared <dataset>.json (DEFAULT_TASK='classification', types.py:83). Every classification run reads it whatever its cv_folds, and imputation falls back to it (config.py:104-106).

I downgrade the severity from high to medium for four reasons:
(a) Nothing at HEAD is contaminated. A read-only query of mlflow.db finds 0 Optuna runs not tagged imputation (all 2,953 Optuna study/trial runs are imputation). datasets/hiperparams holds only *.imputation.json, and git history never tracked a shared classification file. The fork's 0.858/0.799/... classification sweep is untuned defaults, so this defect does not bias it.
(b) The leak needs two explicit actions: an Optuna study run with --task classification, and --promote_best (opt-in, opt.py:577).
(c) The project already knows about it and chose to keep it. ADR 0005 decision 3 (docs/adr/0005-reduced-optuna-search-for-imputation.md:160-163) says the classification objective "spells out today's test-split behaviour rather than changing it". Ticket 02 (docs/tickets/imputation-optuna-reduced/issues/02-validation-search-objective.md:11) and map.md:154 say classification "keeps ranking by f1_macro on the test split".
(d) The impact on reading the paper (paper TRIDENT tuned on test, baselines on validation) is about upstream code and an owner statement, not a fork defect. The Wiki already records it, at references/trident-paper.md:206 and in thesis-goals.md:152, together with the planned remedy (retune on validation with the baselines' budget).

Classification is also secondary to the imputation focus. The "high" impact applies only if the owner uses opt.py as-is for the step-zero replication. That is a real hazard and the fix is cheap, so medium rather than low.

Side note: the fallback path has been exercised before. Six imputation parent runs on 2026-09-11 logged config_source=datasets/hiperparams/electricity/electricity_{20,40}nan.json, an untracked classification file that is gone now (F-07-4 history). They do not bear on test selection.

finding.title: Baselines get no tuning budget, and a measured stronger KNN bar (k=20) was left out
finding.claim: ADR 0007 decision 5 fixes the baselines as constants ('a baseline is a fixed bar; a tunable one would be a second model'). KNNImputer runs at k in {5,10}, uniform weights; HistGradientBoosting and LightGBM run at library defaults; missForest is external with a fixed tree count. TRIDENT meanwhile received over 25 Optuna studies of 40 trials and about 20 configuration experiments. E20 measured k=20 below k=10 wherever missingness is 40% or more (credit-g_20nan 0.955 -> 0.938, kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.883 -> 0.850, pendigits 0.358 -> 0.348), yet the bar kept {5,10}. That is a known stronger baseline left out by decision, on the variants where the model's standing is marginal. Partial offset: the bar is the minimum over five baselines chosen on the test CV mean, an oracle selection in the baselines' favour.
finding.evidence: docs/adr/0007-baseline-imputers-scored-on-the-decoders-cells.md:119-122 (decision 5), :352-358 (k=20 lower at 40% missingness or more); src/training/imputation_baselines.py:144-145, 270-274, 326; src/training/lightgbm_baseline.py:52-57; src/training/missforest.py:209-221; src/training/summary.py:95-108 (bar = min over test CV means)
finding.impact: Favours the model, most on the 40-80nan variants. It could change the 'below the bar on N of 21' counts and per-variant RQ1 claims. The net sign against the oracle bar selection is unmeasured, but the equal-budget principle is violated.
finding.cheap_check: Scoring only, as E20 did: on the cached folds and cells of the E35 or E39-D runs, add knn20 and knn50 plus a small hgb/lgbm grid (learning rate, leaves, iterations). Pick each setting on the validation rows' own gaps, never on test, then recompute the bar and the below-bar count.
finding.suggested_fix: Give each baseline family a declared validation-only budget comparable to a reduced study, chosen per fold on the validation induced gaps, and log the chosen settings. Keep the current untuned bar as a secondary reference row.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding has three parts. I checked each one against the code at HEAD (b2b50fd) and the MLflow store, which I opened read-only.

1) The headline claim fails: "a measured stronger KNN bar (k=20) was left out, on the variants where the model's standing is marginal." E20 ran before hgb and lgbm joined the bar. On the same seed-42 runs E20 scored, the current five-baseline bar is already below every k=20 value E20 reports. So knn20 would not set the bar on any variant the finding cites, and it changes no below-bar count. The finding also misreads its pendigits number. "pendigits 0.358 -> 0.348" is knn5 -> knn10, not k10 -> k20. E20 never reports a k=20 value for pendigits, and its own "40% or more" clause excludes a 20nan table anyway. That clause is contradicted by two of E20's examples, which are 20nan variants (credit-g_20nan, spambase_20nan). The finding repeats that contradiction without noticing it.

2) What remains of the KNN point can't be closed read-only, but it can be bounded. k=20 was never measured at 60nan or 80nan. There the bar is mean_mode at 1.000 and the model is marginal (E35: kr-vs-kp_80nan 0.976, spambase_80nan 0.987, credit-g_80nan 1.008, credit-g_60nan 0.992). At those levels knn10 scores 1.047-1.063. Just reaching mean_mode parity would take a drop of 0.047-0.063, and the largest k10 -> k20 drop E20 ever measured is 0.033 (kr-vs-kp_40nan). As k grows, KNN tends toward the mean/mode fill, which is already in the bar. So a larger k displacing the bar at 80nan is implausible, though unmeasured.

3) The equal-budget point is true as a fact. The baselines are constants: KNN at k in {5,10} with uniform weights, hgb and lgbm at library defaults, and missForest with 100 trees over 10 rounds. ADR 0007 decision 5 records this as a deliberate choice. Two things offset it:
- The bar is the minimum over five baselines, chosen on the test CV mean, an oracle selection in the baselines' favour.
- The strongest imputer, missForest, is reported on its own with gap_to_missforest. The model is below missForest on 20 of 21 induced variants, and 6 of those are ties within the 0.016 band.

So the bar is not weak by construction. Not measured: whether a validation-tuned hgb/lgbm would flip the few marginal variants where the model leads the bar by under 0.01 (kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.758 vs 0.764, credit-g_40nan 0.956 vs 0.964, credit-g_60nan 0.992 vs 1.000). That is a small residual risk, not a demonstrated defect. Also, on the model side, the Optuna tuning budget bought nothing measurable: E03, E10, E12 and E17 found tuned within noise of the defaults, and in E17 credit-g_20nan's promoted file was worse. The real asymmetry is in the design experiments, not in the "25 studies".

Status: none of CONSOLIDATED.md, BACKLOG.md or the 2026-10-07 review tracks a baseline tuning budget. The design is documented in ADR 0007 and offset by the five-baseline bar plus the external missForest, so I record it as known-mitigated, not as known-open or new.

Severity goes from high to low. The worthwhile part of the finding's cheap check is a validation-chosen hgb/lgbm grid on the few variants where the model leads the bar by under 0.01. Adding knn20 or knn50 would not change the bar.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding has two halves. They fail differently, and only one survives.

(1) The KNN k=20 half is wrong and immaterial. The "pendigits 0.358 -> 0.348" example is the k=5 -> k=10 step (ADR 0007:314), not k=10 -> k=20. E20 also states no k=20 value for pendigits. I re-scored KNN on the runs' own folds and induced cells; the script reproduces the ADR's seed-42 knn5/knn10 values exactly (credit-g_40nan 1.043/0.987). k=20 sets the bar on none of the 21 variants. On the two variants where KNN is the bar it is worse than k=10: pendigits 0.348 -> 0.360, letter 0.473 -> 0.485. Everywhere else it stays above hgb/lgbm, for example kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.850 against 0.764 and spambase_20nan 0.925 against 0.865. At 60-80nan, larger k only drifts back toward the mean/mode fill, which is already in the bar. The one exception is k=50 on credit-g_60nan: over 3 seeds it scores 0.987 against the model's 0.992. That flips the variant by mean only, with no verdict (CI [-0.002, +0.013]), and the k was picked after seeing test.

(2) The tuning-budget half holds, and the effect is bigger than the oracle min-over-5 offset. That offset is bounded by the hgb-lgbm spread, at most 0.009 per ADR 0017. I scored hgb's own recipe with one alternative setting: learning rate 0.05, 200 iterations, max depth 3. It lowers the bar by 0.010-0.035 on 4 of the 6 variants checked.
- kr-vs-kp_40nan: bar 0.764 -> 0.745. Model minus bar goes from no verdict (mean -0.006, CI [-0.016, +0.004]) to a baseline win by the project's own rule (+0.014, CI [+0.005, +0.022], all three seeds positive).
- kr-vs-kp_60nan: the model's verdict win (-0.038) becomes no verdict (-0.004).
- spambase_20nan: the model's verdict win (-0.018) becomes no verdict (-0.007).
- credit-g_40nan: the margin goes from -0.008 to +0.001, a tie.
- kr-vs-kp_20nan: unchanged.
Together with k=50 on credit-g_60nan, the RQ1 headline "below the bar on 19 of 21 induced" (ADR 0017 Outcome) drops to about 16 by mean. One per-variant standing turns into a measured loss, and two verdict wins disappear. Direction: the current bar favours the model, as the finding says. Size: about 0.01-0.035 impute_score on medium-missingness kr-vs-kp, credit-g and spambase. The large margins (vehicle, biodeg, kc2, the 60nan tables) are untouched.

Selection caveat: I picked the shallow setting from four after seeing seed-42 test scores on kr-vs-kp_40nan. I then applied it unchanged to seeds 7/13 and to other variants, and it was consistently better there, so it is more than selection noise. Still, it shows that a stronger bar exists; it is not the right measurement. The finding's validation-chosen per-fold grid is still needed.

Why medium, not high: no ADR decision reads the bar. ADRs 0013-0018 and the E35/E38/E39 primary rules are paired model-vs-model contrasts. missForest, reported separately, already tempers the claims at 40nan (credit-g_40nan 0.956 against 0.931). What is affected is the RQ1 headline count and a few per-variant RQ1 statements: real and bounded, not a reversal.

Why known-open: ADR 0007 d5 and ADR 0016 d7 record the fixed bar as a deliberate decision. No prior review (CONSOLIDATED, the 2026-10-07 code review, BACKLOG) raises baseline tuning. HEAD is unchanged.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding is half right. The first part of its title holds; the second part (k=20) falls apart when checked.

The first part holds. Re-reading the code confirms that no baseline gets any tuning:
- KNN runs at k in {5, 10} with uniform weights.
- HGB and LGBM run at library defaults, with only a seed set.
- missForest runs at the R package's defaults with 100 trees.
- The training-time hiding rate is a fixed constant.
- The bar is the lowest test-CV mean among the five baselines.

This is a deliberate choice, written down twice: ADR 0007 decision 5 ("a baseline is a fixed bar") and ADR 0016 decision 7 ("decision 5 stands"). None of the earlier reviews or backlog items treats it as a problem: CONSOLIDATED.md predates the baselines, the 2026-10-07 review's baseline items are about backfills and report tuples, and BACKLOG only has I3 (ReMasker). So it is known as a design decision but never acknowledged as a weakness. Nothing has been done about it, so 'known-open' stands, in that sense.

The k=20 part is refuted. On every variant the finding cites, k=20 beats k=10 but stays above the actual bar, which there is set by hgb or lgbm:
- credit-g_20nan: knn20 0.938 vs hgb 0.936 (seed 42); at E35 the hgb bar is 0.918.
- kr-vs-kp_40nan: knn20 0.850 vs hgb 0.772; at E35 the lgbm bar is 0.764.
- spambase_20nan: knn20 0.925 vs hgb 0.865 / lgbm 0.865.

A stronger KNN is not a stronger bar on any of them, so leaving k=20 out changes no verdict that is on record. The pendigits figure is also misread: '0.358 -> 0.348' is k=5 -> k=10 (ADR 0007 table: knn5 0.358, knn10 0.348). No k=20 value for pendigits or letter exists anywhere in the repo; a grep for knn20 finds only the ADR prose. The ADR's own sentence contradicts itself ('40% or more', then two 20nan examples), which probably caused the misquote.

KNN sets the bar on only three tables:
- kc2: k=5 already beats k=10, so k=20 would go the wrong way.
- pendigits and letter: at E35 the model leads knn10 by 0.018 and 0.014, and the bigger encoder of ADR 0018 widens those leads.

Mitigations the finding doesn't credit:
1. The oracle selection is the project's own stated argument, not a new observation: ADR 0007 'How to compare' says choosing the bar on test 'favours the baselines, so the bar errs against the model'.
2. missForest, a strong imputer from the literature, is logged with its own paired gap. The model is lower than it on 20 of 21 induced variants, and ADR 0016/0017 already label six of those wins ties inside the 0.016 inductive-vs-transductive band.
3. On the model side, the logged Optuna tuning mostly failed to beat the defaults (E03, E10, E17; E21 helped only pendigits and letter). The configuration experiments E24-E38 did improve the model, but each new default was replicated on fresh seeds (E33, E35, E38), which limits the selection-on-test bias. The difference in effort is real, and what it bought is documented. I did not verify the finding's 'over 25 studies of 40 trials' count.

What remains, and why the severity is medium rather than high: the real exposure is not KNN but the 60-80nan variants. There the default boosters score above 1.0:
- lgbm: 1.04-1.11 (ADR 0017).
- hgb: 1.113 on credit-g_80nan (seed 42).

So the bar falls back to mean/mode at exactly 1.0, while the model's leads are thin:
- credit-g_60nan: 0.992.
- spambase_80nan: 0.987.
- kr-vs-kp_80nan: 0.976.

A regularized booster, or one with a different hiding rate, chosen on validation gaps, could plausibly land between the two and flip one to three narrow wins. Thin leads over hgb/lgbm (kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.758 vs 0.764, spambase_20nan 0.848 vs 0.865) could also be exposed. This is unmeasured, and the paired gap_to_best_baseline intervals would show whether those wins are significant in the first place.

The cheap check is worth running, but aimed where it can bite:
- knn20 (and knn50) on pendigits and letter;
- a small regularization grid for hgb/lgbm (leaf size, iterations, learning rate) on the 60-80nan variants, selected on the validation gaps.

It is not worth running on the credit-g and kr-vs-kp 20-40nan variants the finding names, where hgb/lgbm already beat knn20 by 0.06 to 0.09.

finding.title: Which variants read a promoted file is decided on test folds, and the files on disk are stale or hand-pinned
finding.claim:
The contents of the five E02 files were chosen on masked validation cells, so they carry no direct leak. Their existence, though, is selected on test folds:
- credit-g_20nan's file was removed after it lost on CV test folds across seeds (E17).
- The other five were kept although no comparison showed them better (E03, E10, E17).
- E39's rule decides promote, remove or keep per variant on the test folds of seeds 101/202/303.
- ADR 0018 adopted the bigger encoder on pendigits_20nan and letter_20nan only. It left out electricity, part of E38's pre-registered large group, after its result was seen.

Of the seven files on disk, five are stale E02 outputs. kr-vs-kp_20nan still carries tie-broken trial 17's LR_DECODE 0.0017418753352176958 and PROB_MASCARA 0.2. These five also lack PRETRAIN_GAP_TOKEN and ENCODER_FINAL_NORM (2026-10-07 review item 12, still open: kr-vs-kp_20nan's file ends at DECODE_CHECKPOINT). The other two are hand-written ADR 0018 architecture pins with LR_DECODE 0.001, not Optuna outputs.

Latent risk: promote_best_configuration resolves through the override path, which ignores the variant's file. A future study promoted on pendigits or letter would therefore write task defaults over the ADR 0018 architecture.

The facts in the finding hold at HEAD. What does not hold is its main impact claim, that this "favours the model on those seven variants". It is also not new: every part except the framing is already written down by the owner or by an earlier review.

What holds (re-read at HEAD b2b50fd):
- Seven *.imputation.json files are on disk. The five E02 files end at DECODE_CHECKPOINT and lack PRETRAIN_GAP_TOKEN and ENCODER_FINAL_NORM. kr-vs-kp_20nan holds LR_DECODE 0.0017418753352176958 and PROB_MASCARA 0.2, the values of tie-broken trial 17 (F-07-1).
- The two ADR 0018 files hold the dataclass defaults (LR 0.001, WD 0.0019, mask rate 0.5) plus LAYERS 4, DIM_FEED 256 and final norm 'layer'.
- credit-g_20nan's file was removed on E17's CV test folds, which include headline seeds 7 and 42.
- electricity was left out of ADR 0018 after its result was seen, against the rule set in advance.
- E39 decides promote, remove or keep on the test folds of seeds 101/202/303.
- promote_best_configuration goes through the override path, which ignores the variant's file.

Why it is downgraded:
1. The direction of the bias is wrong for five of the seven variants. Keeping the five E02 files was a status-quo choice, and the test-fold evidence pointed against them:
   - E03: the promoted file was worse by point estimate on credit-g_40nan (0.968 vs 0.962), kr-vs-kp_40nan (0.778 vs 0.756) and spambase_40nan.
   - E17: credit-g_40nan's file was worse than the defaults across seeds (paired +0.0231, p≈0.033).
   Keeping files that the test folds disfavour does not make the model look better. If anything it makes it look slightly worse. Only three choices could favour the model:
   - credit-g_20nan's removal: about 0.016, on a variant where every arm overlaps hgb, so no verdict changes.
   - The pendigits/letter adoption: a −4.0% effect found on E37's seeds 42/7/13 and replicated on fresh seeds 101/202/303 under a rule set in advance. The pre-ADR encoder (R, 0.333 and 0.459) already sits below knn10 (about 0.348 and 0.473). So the knn10 win does not come from the selection; the selection only widens the margin.
   - Leaving electricity out: +0.3%, no verdict, negligible.
2. The parts are already documented:
   - The stale files are the stated reason for E39, which is running now (ticket 'Why' section).
   - The tie-break is F-07-1 in CONSOLIDATED.
   - The missing keys are item 12 of the 2026-10-07 review, still unchecked. At HEAD they have no effect: neither key is in _TASK_DEFAULTS['imputation'], and the dataclass defaults are null/none.
   - The credit-g_20nan removal and the electricity omission are both recorded in ADR 0005 and ADR 0018 themselves.
3. The promote_best 'latent risk' is mis-framed:
   - Trials also train through hyperparams_override (opt.py:234). A promoted file therefore matches exactly what the winning trial trained.
   - The real problem is that a reduced study on pendigits or letter trains the 2-layer encoder. ADR 0018 states this under Consequences, and E39 puts both variants out of scope for this reason.
   - The suggested fix ('start promote_best from the variant's file') would make the promoted file differ from what the winner trained, unless the trials changed too.

What remains is a real but small adaptive-selection issue on the benchmark cells: credit-g_20nan, the pendigits/letter adoption and E39's coming decision. It is a slice of the broader no-holdout reuse problem. It deserves a sentence in the write-up and a confirmation seed set to be retired, not a medium-severity finding.

finding.title: Under the induced objective, the search scores the exact induced cells that later sit in the confirmation test folds
finding.claim:
The predefined split is one file per base dataset, the same for every seed and variant, and trials never set cv_folds. Measured read-only, its validation rows hold 9.7-10.2% of each variant's induced cells:
- credit-g_40nan 777/8000
- kr-vs-kp_20nan 2296/23004
- kr-vs-kp_40nan 4579/46008
- spambase_20nan 5353/52440
- spambase_40nan 10483/104880
- credit-g_80nan 1583/16000
- pendigits_20nan 3519/35168
- letter_20nan 6464/64000

On seeds 101/202/303 they make up 5.8-13.1% of each 5-fold test fold's induced cells. With --search_objective induced (E22, E23, E39), those are the very cells, scored against the same _00nan truth, that ranked the trials. F-07-6/F-08-3 leaned on a dampener, that the headline population is induced and the search never touched it. Under the induced objective that dampener no longer holds, so the finding has worsened. The leak still passes only through four or five knobs and a retrained model.
finding.evidence: src/training/data.py:50, 186-201; opt.py:209-242 (no cv_folds in the trial namespace); src/training/decoding.py:356-363 (validation induced scored on fold.validation_indices); docs/reviews/imputation-critique/CONSOLIDATED.md:680-692 (the earlier dampener); scratchpad/hpo_overlap.py (the measurement above)
finding.impact: One-directional, in favour of the selected arm: E39's T, and E22/E23's induced winners against the masked winners and the defaults. A rough bound is 0.1 times the winner's optimism on those cells; with E39's median test-minus-objective of 0.03-0.08, that is at most about 0.003-0.008, comparable to the smallest verdicts in the record. Preliminary per-seed means in the store show E39's T not beating D, so no current verdict appears to rest on it.
finding.cheap_check: From the per-fold cell ledgers in the results/ tree (on the server for E39), recompute T-D and T-F with the predefined validation rows dropped from each test fold. If the verdicts do not change, record that in the E39 outcome.
finding.suggested_fix: Drop the search's validation rows from confirmation test folds, or draw search rows disjoint from the confirmation rows. Better still, nest the search inside each outer training portion (nested CV).

verdicts.reasoning:
The defect is real at HEAD, exactly as described. No guard removes it.

- **Trials always use the fixed split.** The trial namespace (opt.py:209-242) never sets cv_folds, and CONFIGURATION_FLAGS (src/training/config.py:33-36) doesn't carry it either. So build_folds takes the predefined branch, which reads one `{base}_split.json` per base dataset (src/training/data.py:50, 186-201).
- **The search scores the validation rows' own gaps.** Every trial scores them against the _00nan sibling (src/training/decoding.py:356-363). Under `--search_objective induced` that is the ranking key.
- **The confirmation reuses those cells.** It runs `cv_folds=5` (scripts/experiments/retune_run.py:79) with no exclusion of the predefined validation rows, and scores the test rows' gaps against the same sibling (decoding.py:246-247).
- **The overlap numbers reproduce.** Shares per test fold:
  - credit-g_40nan, seeds 101/202/303: 0.058-0.129
  - spambase_40nan: 0.083-0.117
  - E22/E23 at seed 42: credit-g_80nan 0.084-0.128, biodeg_20nan 0.082-0.117, kr-vs-kp_40nan 0.085-0.108, letter_20nan 0.095-0.105
- **The lost dampener is real.** "The search never touched the induced population" (CONSOLIDATED.md:680-692) does not hold for E22, E23 or E39.
- **Status is known-open.** Nothing was ever mitigated: ADR 0005 still lacks the overlap sentence that CONSOLIDATED.md:723/1492 recommended, ADR 0008 and the E39 ticket never mention it, and there is no nested or disjoint design.

**Why low rather than medium**

1. **E39 is finished in the local store, and no recommendation is within reach of the bound.** By the 15-pair, three-seed rule:
   - credit-g_40nan: T-F -0.050 [-0.060, -0.040], D-F -0.045, T-D -0.0046 [-0.0146, +0.0054] with mixed seeds. Recommendation: promote T.
   - kr-vs-kp_40nan: T-F -0.039 [-0.047, -0.032], T-D -0.0024 [-0.0117, +0.0068]. Recommendation: promote T.
   - spambase_40nan: D-F -0.0044 [-0.0081, -0.0007], all seeds negative. Recommendation: remove the file.
   - kr-vs-kp_20nan: everything level. Recommendation: keep F.
   - spambase_20nan: D beats T, +0.0096 [+0.0015, +0.0177], but D-F is level. Recommendation: keep F.

   The leak can only flatter T. Removing it would move T-D upward, and the two "promote T" calls flip only if T-D's lower bound rises above 0, a shift of more than 0.0146 or 0.0117. The finding's own upper bound is 0.003-0.008. The finding's line "T not beating D, so no verdict rests on it" was written on preliminary data and is incomplete: T-F verdicts do rest on leak-favoured contrasts, but with margins 5-10 times the bound.
2. **The finding's cheap check, run locally on the stored per-cell ledgers, finds no bias in the predicted direction.** The store keeps the best and worst fold's cell ledger per run (ADR 0002), and recomputing from them matches the logged impute_score to 1e-16. The estimate (T-D with the predefined validation rows dropped) minus (T-D on all cells) should be positive if the leak acts. It comes out at or below zero on all five variants:

   | variant | estimate |
   |---|---|
   | credit-g_40nan | -0.0033 |
   | kr-vs-kp_20nan | -0.0018 |
   | kr-vs-kp_40nan | -0.0064 |
   | spambase_20nan | -0.0072 |
   | spambase_40nan | -0.0002 |

   That is, T does relatively worse, not better, on the cells the search ranked it by. The same holds for E23 biodeg_20nan (folds 4 and 5, induced winner minus masked winner): -0.016/-0.027 becomes -0.017/-0.063 with those rows dropped. It also holds for E22 credit-g_80nan (fold 1): -0.184 becomes -0.196. Only 2 of 5 folds per run are stored, so this is a noisy sample, but it gives no sign of the bias.
3. **Corrections to the claim's scope.**
   - "Four or five knobs" holds only for E39's reduced profile (scripts/experiments/retune_report.py:48). E22/E23 used the full profile, about 13 knobs, so the channel was wider there.
   - "Seeds 101/202/303" applies only to E39. E22/E23 retrained at seed 42.
   - The one recorded verdict inside the bound is E23 biodeg_20nan "better" at -0.031 [-0.060, -0.002]. It is single-seed and exploratory, no decision rests on it, and the direct check moves it the other way.

What remains is a structural, one-directional contamination of the confirmation design. It deserves a sentence in ADR 0005 or ADR 0008 and a disjoint or nested design for future studies. It changes no current verdict.

finding.title: The induced objective is a minimum over 450 epochs on its own cells, and its optimism tracks LR_DECODE (contradicting E39's 'common to every trial')
finding.claim:
With DECODE_CHECKPOINT induced, the decode stage keeps the epoch with the lowest per-epoch score on the validation gaps. The induced search objective then re-scores the same gaps at that epoch, so the objective is the minimum of a 450-point noisy curve on fixed cells. The mechanism itself is known (ADR 0008 amendment, F-07-2). The E39 ticket asserts the bias is 'common to every trial, so the ranking survives'.

Read-only on E39's five finished studies (40 trials each): Spearman of (test induced on the predefined test rows minus objective) against log10 LR_DECODE is
- +0.45 on kr-vs-kp_20nan
- +0.39 on spambase_20nan
- +0.54 on spambase_40nan
- +0.14 on kr-vs-kp_40nan
- +0.03 on credit-g_40nan

The median of test minus objective is +0.081, +0.045, -0.007, +0.029 and +0.043 respectively. So the optimism is not uniform: trials with a higher decode rate read better on the objective than on held-out rows, and the winners sit at LR_DECODE 1.4e-3 to 5.6e-3.

The 'effective filter, useless ranker' pattern of E11 persists. Among the 20 best-by-objective trials, Spearman is 0.21, 0.18, 0.09, 0.08 and -0.02. The winners rank 12, 6, 10, 14 and 4 of 40 on test induced, better than the masked era's mean of 15-17, with no ties. These are five correlations at n=40: suggestive, not a demonstrated mis-ranking.
finding.evidence: src/training/types.py:166 (DECODE_CHECKPOINT induced by default); src/training/decoding.py:111-176 (checkpoint = argmin of the per-epoch gap score), :356-363 (objective = the same gaps at that epoch); docs/tickets/imputation-retune/01-retune-promoted-files.md:148-150; mlflow.db read-only, source study parents 167633dd, b71fd119, 054729b4, cf1a85cc, dd40c1d6 (is_mirror=false); scratchpad/hpo_e39_trials.py
finding.impact: It degrades selection, biasing it towards noisy, high-rate configurations. It does not bias E39's verdict, which is scored on fresh seeds. It helps explain why no reduced search has beaten the defaults, and argues that the next search must separate the cells that choose the checkpoint from the cells that score the objective.
finding.cheap_check: Same read-only query on E22/E23 (full-profile, induced objective, run before ADR 0015, so the checkpoint was chosen by loss). If the LR correlation vanishes there, the shared-cells mechanism is implicated.
finding.suggested_fix: Do T08: split the validation rows or masks into two disjoint halves, one choosing the checkpoint and one scoring the objective. Alternatively, score the objective at a fixed epoch budget. Correct the limit sentence in the E39 ticket.

verdicts.reasoning:
Not refuted on the facts. The code at HEAD does what the finding says, and every number reproduces. Downgraded to low and known-open on the interpretation, for four reasons.

(1) The mechanism is already documented and still open. The documented sources are ADR 0008's amendment, ADR 0015's Consequences and CONSOLIDATED F-07-2, which was settled at medium. The E39 ticket's own Known limits list it too. CONSOLIDATED even names the LR_DECODE channel as "plausible and unmeasured". The finding's only new contribution is the first measurement of that channel.

(2) A within-trial control undercuts the attribution to shared cells. Under DECODE_CHECKPOINT induced, the validation masked cells never choose the checkpoint, because kept_state = gap_state. So masked test-minus-validation measures an LR-dependent val/test shift with the shared-cells mechanism removed. On spambase_20nan and spambase_40nan that control shows almost the same LR correlation as the induced gap: +0.35 vs +0.39 and +0.40 vs +0.54. Those are two of the three correlations the finding relies on, and the only two besides kr-vs-kp_20nan above the n=40 noise floor. They are therefore a spambase-specific effect of LR on how well results carry from validation to test rows, not shared-cell optimism. Only kr-vs-kp_20nan isolates the mechanism cleanly: induced +0.45 against masked -0.31. The induced median offset is larger than the masked one by +0.09 on kr-vs-kp_20nan, but by no more than +0.013 on any other study, and is smaller on three of them (credit-g_40nan, kr-vs-kp_40nan, spambase_40nan).

(3) Where the mechanism is clean, the harm is not shown. On kr-vs-kp_20nan the test score also improves with LR (rho -0.31), and the winner at LR 5.6e-3 ranks 6/40 on test. The other winners sit at 1.4e-3 to 3.7e-3, on ADR 0005's plateau. So "biases selection towards noisy high-rate configurations" is unsupported.

(4) The cheap check comes out the finding's way but is confounded. On E22/E23 the correlation of (test - objective) with log LR vanishes (-0.22 to +0.02). However, those studies used the full profile with EPOCHS_DECODE sampled (rho of the gap with epochs -0.16 to -0.38), embedding pre-training and gaps shown as [NULL]. They are consistent with the mechanism but do not isolate it.

The "450-point noisy curve" channel cannot be checked from the store, because the Optuna trial runs carry no stepped metrics. The impact claim that this "helps explain why no reduced search beat the defaults" was not verified. The full-sample rho(objective, test induced) of 0.29 to 0.65 is no worse than the masked era's, and the drop in the top-20 correlation repeats E11's pattern; neither is new evidence of the shared cells.

E39's verdict is unaffected, as the finding itself says, because the arms run on fresh seeds 101/202/303. The ticket sentence "common to every trial, so the ranking survives" is imprecise: the median optimism ranges from -0.007 to +0.081, and on kr-vs-kp_20nan it tracks LR. Correcting its wording, and splitting the checkpoint cells from the objective cells (T08) in the next search, are reasonable low-cost actions.
