finding.title: Search protocol unchanged at HEAD: one fixed split, one seed, 40 trials, no held-out gate; winners still do not beat the defaults
finding.claim:
Each trial trains once on the predefined split at the study seed. T09 (k-fold inside the search) and T08 are still open. Forty seeded TPE trials, of which Optuna spends 10 as random startup, cover 4-5 dimensions in the reduced profile but 14-15 in the full one, which is close to random search.

The full profile samples EPOCHS_PRE and EPOCHS_DECODE in 20-60 against held defaults of 300 and now 450. The disjointness the addendum (§8.4) found has therefore widened. Full also cannot express ADR 0018's encoder: DIM_FEED is limited to 16-128 and ENCODER_FINAL_NORM is not sampled.

Track record: no reduced-profile winner has beaten the defaults on fresh evaluation (E03, E10, E16, E17). E39's preliminary per-seed store means, which are not the pre-registered tally, read spambase_20nan with T worse than D on all three seeds (+0.013, +0.005, +0.011) and the other variants mixed. E14 and E18 found about four fifths of the single-split advantage to be selection bias. E21's full-profile gains on pendigits and letter mix the search with a different budget and architecture.
finding.evidence: opt.py:125-141 (full ranges), :134, :144 (epochs 20-60), :209-242 (single split), :483 (TPESampler seeded); src/training/types.py:163 (EPOCHS_DECODE 450); docs/TASKS.md:124-128 (T08, T09 open); docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:386-402 (E14), :453-468 (E18); docs/reviews/imputation-critique/ADDENDUM-2026-09-15-optuna-results.md:368-392 (§8.4); mlflow.db read-only, experiment=retune-2026-10-15, cv/test/impute/induced/impute_score/mean per seed (scratchpad/hpo_e39_means.py)
finding.impact: Any promotion from a single-split study is more likely noise than gain, so a 'tuned' label in thesis text is unsupported. A reduced-against-full comparison measures the epoch budget, not the search space. Neither side is favoured directly; the cost is wasted budget and misleading 'tuned' claims.
finding.cheap_check: Run the owner's retune_report.py --tally on E39. Add the E14-style winner-rank table for E39's five studies to the outcome; it is already computed read-only (12, 6, 10, 14, 4 of 40).
finding.suggested_fix: Score each trial on repeated validation (3 inner folds, or 3 seeds sharing the outer fold). Gate promotion in opt.py on beating the defaults on seeds and rows the study never saw (E39's arms, made routine). Give the full profile epoch ranges that include the defaults, and let it reach the ADR 0018 architecture.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every factual part of the finding holds at HEAD (b2b50fd), so it is not refuted. Each trial trains once on the predefined split at the study seed: the trial namespace never sets cv_folds, and cv_folds is not in CONFIGURATION_FLAGS, so passing --cv_folds to opt.py would not reach trials either. The sampler is TPESampler(seed) with the default 10 startup trials. The full profile samples 14-15 dimensions, with both epoch counts in 20-60 against held values of 300 and 450. T08 and T09 are still open, and the owner's own E39 ticket lists the one-study, one-split limit in advance. Nothing in opt.py neutralises the selection noise.

Corrections that do not downgrade the finding:
(1) "ENCODER_FINAL_NORM is not sampled" is true but overstated. It is a CONFIGURATION_FLAG, so --encoder_final_norm layer overrides every trial and a full study can hold it. The only hard blocker for ADR 0018 in the full profile is DIM_FEED capped at 128 against the promoted 256.
(2) The same applies to EPOCHS_DECODE: --decode_epochs silently overrides the sampled value. The disjointness holds only when the flag is absent, and it always holds for EPOCHS_PRE.
(3) The reduced profile cannot express ADR 0018 either. A trial's override replaces the promoted file (config.py:98-100), so DIM_FEED is held at 32 and LAYERS at 2. This is why E39 excluded pendigits and letter. So the problem is wider than the finding states.

Why not "mitigated": the only guard is procedural. Promotion is opt-in (--promote_best), and the fresh-seed T/D/F arms plus a user ADR decide. That gate lives outside the code and is imperfect. The pre-registered rule (retune_report.py:131-153) promotes T when T beats any one arm and loses to none. The tally I ran read-only therefore says "promote T" on kr-vs-kp_40nan and credit-g_40nan, where T-D is "no detectable difference": T wins only because F loses to both T and D. That is the finding's impact actually happening: a file labelled tuned that cannot be told apart from the defaults.

Why not "low": classification's default profile is full (opt.py:451-454). It searches EPOCH_FINE and EPOCHS_PRE in 20-60 against held values of 150 and 300, across 14 dimensions in 40 trials, so "affects: both" holds.

The track record is confirmed and now pre-registered rather than preliminary. In E39, T-D shows no detectable difference on 4 of 5 variants, and D is better on spambase_20nan with T worse on all three seeds (+0.0132, +0.0050, +0.0106). Winner ranks are 12, 6, 10, 14 and 4 of 40. Their median of 10 beats E14's median of 18 against a chance level of 20.5, so the induced objective ranks somewhat better than the old masked one. This is consistent with E03, E10/E16, E17 and E18.

finding.title: opt.py plumbing at HEAD: most earlier findings still open, two mitigated, one fixed
finding.claim:
Status at HEAD of the earlier opt.py findings:
- Tie-break by trial number through study.best_trial: open, but mitigated (each of E39's five induced studies has a single trial at the best value).
- Promotion reads nothing held out (F-07-7): open, mitigated by process (E39 runs no --promote_best).
- A study cannot resume (F-07-9), because storage is timestamped and optimize has no catch=: open.
- The running-best file is named <dataset>.json, like classification's promoted file (F-07-10): open.
- temp_trials is rmtree'd, deleting every trial's cell ledger, the winner's included: open.
- Imputation falls back to the classification file (F-07-4): open.
- The hyperparameter path is CWD-relative: open.
- --retrain_best builds a namespace without cv_folds, so it retrains on the single split (the studies used separate 5-fold retrains).
- F-12-3 is fixed: git ls-files datasets/hiperparams lists all seven files.
finding.evidence: opt.py:535 (best_trial), :577-583 (promotion), :428-430 and :474-484 (timestamped storage), :526 (optimize without catch=), :336 (running-best name), :628-634 (rmtree), :590-614 (retrain namespace without cv_folds); src/training/config.py:104-106, :127; git ls-files datasets/hiperparams (7 files)
finding.impact: Mostly reproducibility and foot-gun risk. F-07-4, combined with a future classification --promote_best, could silently feed a test-tuned classification configuration into imputation runs. Neither side is favoured today.
finding.cheap_check: Greps at HEAD (done). Add a unit test that every promoted file's key set equals complete_configuration's, and one that an imputation run never reads <dataset>.json.
finding.suggested_fix: Tie-aware selection: log the number of trials within one quantum of the best and refuse promotion on ties. Add --study_dir and --resume, and catch= in optimize. Rename the running-best file (for example best_so_far.json). Keep the winner's ledger. Drop the classification fallback for imputation. Resolve the hiperparams path from the repository root. Pass cv_folds to the retrain.

verdicts.reasoning:
I re-read every cited line at HEAD (b2b50fd). The roll-up holds: no guard elsewhere neutralises any bullet, and low / known-open is the right call. It needs four wording corrections.

(1) The catch= half of F-07-9 is close to moot. opt.py:280-321 already catches Exception inside the objective and raises TrialPruned. In Optuna 4.9, KeyboardInterrupt propagates whatever catch= holds (_optimize.py:201-261; catch is typed tuple[type[Exception], ...]). Only failures outside that try, such as define_search_space at :201 or mlflow.start_run at :269, would get past it. The real defect is the timestamped storage, and the owner already documents it as a known limitation at run_retune_queue.sh:10-11.

(2) The tie-break mitigation is incidental, not structural. I queried all five E39 studies read-only, and each has exactly one trial at the best value. But the lattice from F-07-1 persists under the induced objective: kr-vs-kp_20nan has only 18 distinct values over 40 trials and kr-vs-kp_40nan has 29. On kr-vs-kp_20nan the best and second-best values (0.5298 vs 0.5321) are one lattice step apart.

(3) F-07-4 is open by a documented decision, not as an oversight. The comment at config.py:100-103 and the test at tests/unit/test_training_config.py:313 (test_an_imputation_run_prefers_its_own_configuration_and_falls_back_to_the_shared_one) pin the fallback. Its blast radius today is still zero: all seven files are .imputation.json, and no shared <dataset>.json exists.

(4) "F-12-3 fixed" is true for the tracking half: git ls-files lists 7 files, porcelain is clean, and the last commit is acb8c99. The versionless path per (dataset, task) remains, and the historical config_source pointers to the electricity_{20,40}nan files still dangle (the directory is empty); those pointers can't be fixed.

I also checked whether trials clobber one shared ledger, and they don't. ArtifactWriter roots each run at output_dir/dataset/<per-second timestamp> (artifacts.py:30-31), so every trial keeps its own ledger until the rmtree. OptunaTrialTracker never sends trial artifacts to MLflow, so the rmtree really does delete every trial's ledger. That is by design: the tracking.py docstring says --retrain_best produces the full record. E39's T-arm 5-fold runs log their own ledgers, which mitigates the loss.

The --retrain_best single-split retrain matches the trial it reproduces. The sharper foot-gun is that opt.py accepts --cv_folds through the shared parser and silently drops it for both the trials and the retrain: there is no guard in validate_parsed_args (config.py:214-260), and CONFIGURATION_FLAGS has no cv_folds.
verdicts.evidence:
Confirmed at HEAD:

- E39 never promotes or retrains: run_retune_queue.sh:72-74 runs opt.py without --promote_best or --retrain_best.

- opt.py:526 calls optimize without catch=, but :314-321 already turns Exception into TrialPruned, and Optuna's _optimize.py:211/261 re-raises KeyboardInterrupt anyway.
- opt.py:336 writes the running best as optuna_dir/<dataset>.json.
- opt.py:218-219 sends trial output to temp_trials, and artifacts.py:30-31 gives each run a timestamped subfolder. The ledger goes to <subfolder>/imputation/*_cells.csv (artifacts.py:214-234).

dims.summary:
STATISTICAL methodology of the imputation verdicts. I loaded 753 local raw_fold_metrics.csv files (E30-E38) read-only through mlflow.db?mode=ro. The loader reproduces every logged verdict count exactly (E30 M-A 9/0, P-A 7/2, P-M 0/3; E32 11/0; E33 13/0; E34 K 3/0, C 13/1; E35 K 6/0; E36 0/1; E37 ALL 3/0; E38 pendigits and letter), so the report scripts compute what the log says. I then re-ran each verdict under four alternatives: Holm across variants, the Nadeau-Bengio corrected resampled t, a seed-level t on the 3 seed means (df=2), and cross-table Wilcoxon/sign tests over the 9 base tables. Scripts are in C:\Users\DIOGON~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Diogo-Neiss-Documents-Mestrado-Wiki\f402d390-da5f-4f09-a187-282102e58959\scratchpad\ (stats_load.py, stats_reanalyse.py, stats_bar.py, stats_mc.py, stats_extra.py, stats_cross.py, stats_kc.py, stats_means.py).

Bottom line. The directions of the adopted ADRs are robust at the table level: 0013 M>A, 0014 G, 0015 K and 0018 all hold. The thesis direction (model below the baseline bar) also holds at the table level. What is weak is the counting and veto procedure that produced and reports them. Three numbers are not the right statistics for a thesis: the per-variant counts ("11 of 21", "13 of 21", "worse on none", "below the bar on 19 of 21"). They change two- to five-fold depending on which defensible test is used, and which variants carry a verdict changes too.

The rule has no multiplicity control and no practical margin, and the sign-agreement filter barely changes its error rate. Two decisions it produced read differently under a better analysis:
- **ADR 0015, calibration refusals.** C and KC lose on one or two variants by 0.003-0.012, yet win on 8-9 of 9 tables in both seed sets.
- **ADR 0013:120, refusal of P.** It flips to "recommend P" under Holm or N&B, while the table-level test backs M: right outcome, fragile reason.

The largest problem is structural. Every default was chosen on the same 21 variants' test folds (same rows, one MCAR draw each), and the headline comparison against untuned baselines is read on those same cells. Arm A (0.7929) sat above the bar (0.7781) before four test-selected adoptions brought the default to 0.7446. There is no held-out confirmation.

Classification side, outside this dimension: the 3-fold seed-42 sweep has no verdict procedure, and opt.py scores classification trials on test macro-F1, which is the same forking-paths problem in its purest form.
sound: The scripts compute what the log reports. A scratch loader over 753 local raw_fold_metrics.csv (mlflow.db?mode=ro, parent runs, mirrors excluded) reproduced every logged verdict count for E30-E38, to the variant (stats_reanalyse.py).

Pairing is real, so the unpaired-interval half of F-08-4 is fixed. The model-baseline gaps are paired per fold (src/training/summary.py:166-185), and every report script differences arms by fold and seed (scripts/experiments/confirmatory_report.py:113-117).

The ADR outcomes hold at the table level (stats_cross.py, Wilcoxon and sign tests over the 9 base tables): ADR 0013 M over A on 8/9 (p=0.0117) and M over P on 8/9 (p=0.0078); ADR 0014 G over M on 9/9 in both seed sets (p=0.0039); ADR 0015 K over H on 8/9 (p=0.0195, E34) and 9/9 (p=0.0039, E35). ADR 0018's pendigits and letter verdicts survive the naive rule, Holm, N&B (p<=1e-4) and seed-level t. E36's 'keep null' survives every test (cross-table p=0.43).
The thesis direction holds at the table level: the model is below every individual baseline on 8-9 of 9 tables, Holm-adjusted p=0.0156, the minimum n=9 allows (stats_extra.py).

The bar is chosen on the test-fold means (src/training/summary.py:95-108; the report scripts take the min over BASELINES). That selection favours the baselines, so it is conservative for the model's claim, not a leak.

For the conditional question the naive pooled rule is roughly calibrated: seed means vary less than iid predicts (ANOVA median F 0.65; 1.5% at p<0.05 over 272 contrasts), and the exact seed-level t gives similar totals.

Pre-registration is real. From E24 on, rules are fixed in tickets before launch (docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:9) and outcomes are read by those rules, unfavourable ones included (E36, E34's C). Integrity checks tie readouts to earlier cells to the last digit (E31, E34, E35, E36).
Within-run contrasts (E31, E34, E35) read two outputs of one trained model, so they are genuine common random numbers.
The single-seed scope limit from CONSOLIDATED §3.7 is mitigated: each cell has 3 seeds, and two seed sets exist.

docs/BACKLOG.md has no statistical item. The report findings in docs/reviews/2026-10-07-code-review-last-two-weeks.md are plumbing; finding 6, the four-baseline tuple in the report scripts, is known-open and does not change the conclusions above (ADR 0017 says lgbm moves no verdict).

finding.title: "Below the bar on 19 of 21" counts point estimates on one seed set; it is not a test and it changes with the seed set
finding.claim:
The thesis-level claim in ADR 0017 counts variants whose 3-seed mean is below the best of the baselines. It has no interval or test. It treats the 4 variants of credit-g, kr-vs-kp and spambase as independent evidence even though they share rows and the _00nan truth. It also depends on the seed set: 19/21 on seeds 42/7/13, but 17/21 on 101/202/303 and on today's default (ADR 0018 encoder on pendigits/letter).

With per-variant intervals the model is below on:
- naive rule: 16 below / 1 above (E35) and 15/2 (E34);
- N&B: 14/0 and 13/0;
- seed-level t: 14/0 and 14/0.

Across datasets:
- Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 9 base tables: p=0.012 (E35) and 0.020 (E34). The model is below on 8/9 tables; electricity is the exception (+0.012/+0.016).
- Pairwise, model vs each of the 4 baselines over 9 tables: below on 9/9, 9/9, 9/9 and 8/9 (vs hgb). Wilcoxon p = 0.0039, 0.0039, 0.0039, 0.0078, and Holm gives 0.0156 for all four. That is the floor n=9 can reach (2/512, x4), so it is the strongest statement possible, not a coincidence.
- Friedman over model + 4 baselines on 9 tables: chi2 24.1, p=7.7e-5. Mean ranks: model 1.11, hgb and knn10 2.78. The Nemenyi CD(0.05, k=5, N=9) is 2.03, larger than the 1.67 rank gap, so the Demsar post-hoc does NOT separate the model from hgb/knn10 at the table level. At N=21 (CD 1.33 < 1.62) it does, but only by treating the variants as independent.

Median relative gap to the bar: -3.95% (E35), -4.13% (today).
finding.evidence:
- docs/adr/0017-missforest-outside-the-bar.md:138-167: table of 3-seed means, E35 seeds only, and the 19/21 sentence at :167.
- Wiki projects/trident/fork-experiments.md:37 restates the verdict rule.
- stats_bar.py output: per-set counts, Wilcoxon over 21 and 9, pairwise Holm, Friedman/Nemenyi.
- The fold-level bar here uses 4 baselines because the selection runs' raw_fold_metrics.csv has no lgbm/missforest columns. ADR 0017:167-169 says lgbm moves no verdict (at most 0.009, on 6 variants). Same 4-name tuple as known-open finding 6 of docs/reviews/2026-10-07-code-review-last-two-weeks.md:123-133.
finding.impact: The RQ1 thesis claim (the decoder beats plain imputers). The direction survives every test. The count of 19 does not survive as a statistic: it is 14 with any interval and 17 on the other seed set. At the table level, the claim rests on n=9 at the resolution floor, and a mean-rank post-hoc fails. The selection bias in finding forking-paths-test-reuse favours the model on top of this.
finding.cheap_check: Rerun stats_bar.py (reads ro). To include lgbm/missforest at fold level, pull the parents' per-fold values from the ADR 0017 backfill, or rerun only the baselines on today's cells.
finding.suggested_fix: State the claim at the table level: "lower than the best of the baselines on 8 of 9 tables (Wilcoxon over tables p≈0.01; vs each baseline Holm p=0.016, the minimum attainable with 9 tables); median relative gap -4% [seed-level CI]; interval excludes zero on 14 of 21 variants; electricity the exception". Report both seed sets. Show a CD diagram, but rest inference on pairwise Wilcoxon or a Bayesian signed-rank test (Benavoli et al. 2016) over tables, not on variant counts. Read it on a held-out draw (next finding).

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts in the finding hold up, so it is not refuted. The cited sentence is at the cited line. It counts 3-seed means, uses no interval, and covers E35 only. I reran stats_bar.py read-only and every number in the finding came back the same: 19/21 on E35; 17/21 on E34 and on today's default; naive rule 16/1 and 15/2; N&B 14/0 and 13/0; seed-level 14/0 and 14/0; Wilcoxon over 9 tables p=0.0117 and 0.0195; pairwise p 0.0039 x3 and 0.0078; Friedman chi2 24.1, CD 2.03 against a 1.67 gap. The 17/21 does not depend on how the bar is defined: a per-seed bar and a bar of 3-seed means give the same count. On the E38 cells, the plain impute_score is the K readout, because the imputation default is DECODE_CHECKPOINT induced (types.py:166). So the 'today' set compares like with like.

The severity is overstated: high drops to low, for six reasons.
(1) It is not a code defect, and the ADR sentence is scoped and literally true. ADR 0017:139-141 says 'E35: seeds 42, 7 and 13 ... each cell the mean over the three seeds'. The sentence's job is to show that adding lgbm 'moves no verdict' on the same runs, and a point count is adequate for that.
(2) The repo's own protocol already registers 'best-baseline counts' as a Secondary measure (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:1031, :1066). The Primary verdicts are paired 15-fold-pair intervals plus the seed-sign rule. The repo never offered 19/21 as a test.
(3) The repo already documents the seed dependence. ADR 0015:26 says 'below the best baseline on 17 variants instead of 15' on E34 seeds, LOG:1036-1037 gives E34 as 15/18/17/18, and LOG:1073 gives E35 as 16/19/18/19. The finding presents 17/21 as a discovery; it is only missing from ADR 0017's sentence.
(4) The interval reading of a win already exists and is logged on every run: gap_to_best_baseline with 'ci95_upper below 0 is the paired reading of a win' (ADR 0007:153-159, :181-184). ADR 0007:185-187 also notes that picking the bar after seeing test scores favours the baselines, which partly offsets the forking-paths bias the impact cites.
(5) 'Thesis-level claim' overstates what exists at HEAD. A grep of the wiki finds no restatement of 19/21. thesis-goals.md:75 frames RQ1 against future dedicated imputers and makes no claim about the bar. The count appears only in ADR 0016:268 and 0017:167 and in the LOG's secondary counts.
(6) By the finding's own tests, the direction survives everywhere.

The finding's wording also needs two corrections:
(a) 'It is 14 with any interval' is false. The project's own verdict rule gives 16 below / 1 above (E35) and 15/2 (E34). 14 comes only from the N&B and seed-level methods.
(b) 'Variants share rows' is only half the story. CONSOLIDATED.md:986-988 measured that the _20nan and _40nan masks are independent draws: only 2459 of credit-g's 4000 cells missing at 20% are also missing at 40%. Collapsing to 9 tables is the conservative unit, not the only defensible one.

Caveat: the interval counts use a 4-baseline bar, because the selection runs' raw_fold_metrics.csv has no lgbm column. Adding lgbm can only lower the bar, so 16 and 14 are upper bounds for the 5-baseline bar.

Status stays new. This angle, a count of variants used as a statistic, is not in the prior reviews. Its parent theme is CONSOLIDATED §3.7 (:970-991, medium): 'cannot support a generalisation claim', 'six pairs are read simultaneously with no correction'. The facts in the finding are correct, but the issue does not matter much, so I am not refuting it and I am downgrading it from high to low.

What checks out:
- "19 of 21" counts 3-seed point means. ADR 0017:139-141 says each cell is "the mean over the three seeds", and no test is given at :167.
- On seeds 101/202/303 (E34), and on today's default, the count is 17/21.
- I reproduced every number: per-variant counts, Wilcoxon over the 9 tables, pairwise Holm, Friedman/Nemenyi.

Why it is not material:
1. **ADR 0017 does not rest on the count.** The decision is which baselines make up the bar. The 19/21 sentence sits in Outcome, and it answers one question: does adding lgbm change any variant's below/above status? That is a fixed comparison of means on the same runs and needs no test.
2. **The project already treats these counts as secondary.** The E35 plan lists "best-baseline counts" as Secondary (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:1065-1066, same for E36). Verdicts use the paired 15-fold rule on arm contrasts. The same count shows up only as a secondary number elsewhere (ADR 0016:268, ticket 05:108, ticket 06:135, log :1073 and :1102). No decision is based on it.
3. **No thesis claim uses it yet.** RQ1 is framed against dedicated imputers (ReMasker, CACTI, DiffPuter, TabImpute) at thesis-goals.md:75, not mean/KNN/hgb. No wiki page repeats 19/21, and no thesis text exists yet.
4. **The 19 vs 17 gap is two tied variants.** The variants that flip are credit-g_40nan and kc2_20nan. Their fold-level confidence intervals include zero on both seed sets, so the project's rule calls them ties either way.
5. **The direction holds under every test.**
   - The table-level analysis (8/9 tables, Holm at the floor) is reproduced.
   - Pooling all six seeds gives 16 below and 1 above.
   - The Nemenyi failure is not evidence against the model. Mean-rank post-hoc results depend on which methods are in the pool, and the finding itself says to rely on pairwise Wilcoxon instead.

Where the finding is wrong or overstated:
- "It is 14 with any interval" contradicts its own naive-rule counts (16/1 and 15/2). The project's actual verdict rule gives 16 on E35.
- "Thesis-level claim" overstates where the count sits.

What is real and should go into the wording later:
- "19 of 21" reads as two marginal losses. It hides credit-g_80nan, which is clearly above the bar on both seed sets.
- The honest picture is about 14-16 clear wins, 1 clear loss and 4-6 ties.
- The finding's suggested table-level wording is the right thing to use in the thesis.

The lgbm caveat (fold-level bar uses 4 baselines) changes no conclusion. ADR 0017:168-169 caps lgbm's effect at 0.009 on 6 variants. The only interval it could affect is kr-vs-kp_40nan (E35 CI [-0.0246, -0.0040]). Shifting it by +0.009 could make it include zero, so the naive count could become 15 instead of 16.

1. **It is not a thesis claim.** The wiki frames RQ1 against dedicated imputers (ReMasker, CACTI, DiffPuter, TabImpute), not plain imputers. "19 of 21" appears on no wiki page. In the fork it appears only in ADR 0017's Outcome and as a best-baseline count in E35, E36 and their tickets. The pre-registrations list those counts as Secondary measures; each experiment's verdict comes from its paired primary contrast.

2. **ADR 0017:167 does a different job than the finding gives it.** Read in full, the sentence checks that adding lgbm to the bar of 4 changes nothing on the same cells and seeds ("moves no verdict", lgbm lower by at most 0.009). For that job, point estimates on one seed set are the right tool.

3. **The seed-set dependence is already on record.** ADR 0015:26 gives 17 on seeds 101/202/303, ADR 0017:167 gives 19 on 42/7/13, and E35's log line gives 16/19/18/19 for its four readouts (H/K/C/KC). Its 17 equals E34's 17 because both swapped variants were below the bar either way, so "17 on 101/202/303 and on today's default" is one number counted twice.

4. **"It is 14 with any interval" is wrong.** Under the project's own verdict rule (15 paired folds, 95% CI excludes 0, all three seeds agree in sign; fork-experiments.md:37), the rerun gives 16 below / 1 above on E35 and 15 / 2 on E34. Only the Nadeau-Bengio correction and the seed-level t give 14, and the project has adopted neither.

5. **The variants are less dependent than claimed, and the dependence is already known.** Variants of one table share rows and the _00nan truth, but their MCAR masks are independent draws (2459 of credit-g's 4000 cells missing at 20% are observed at 40%), so each variant scores different cells. 6. **The interval tools exist.** ADR 0007's How to compare section defines `gap_to_best_baseline ci95_upper < 0` as the paired reading of a win, and E19 reported "never with disjoint intervals" next to its count. The thesis plan already commits to multiplicity control and enough datasets for critical-difference power (thesis-goals.md:154), and to paired deltas over repeated splits rather than overlapping intervals (thesis-goals.md:127, :135).

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts the finding cites hold at HEAD. The impact argument does not, so I'm keeping the finding and downgrading it from high to medium.

What holds:
(1) Every adoption verdict reads the test-fold induced score on one fixed cell set per variant. The induced cells come from fixed CSVs, made with one draw per rate. 5-fold CV puts every row in a test fold once, so every seed and every experiment scores the same cells.
(2) The baselines run at library defaults with no tuning: KNN at k=5/10, HGB at a fixed seed.
(3) No held-out draw, table or confirmatory read exists. Both seed sets are now spent on selection as well as replication: E34 and E38 selected on 101/202/303, E30, E32 and E37 on 42/7/13. E39 also runs on 101/202/303.

Why the impact is overstated:
(a) It compares the cumulative gain (0.7929 to 0.7446) with the gap to the bar, as if the whole gain were selection bias. Bias is only the noise the selection exploits, not the gain itself. The finding's own logic predicts the effects should shrink on fresh seeds. They didn't.
- E33, pre-registered on unused seeds, found G better on 13/21 against E32's 11/21, with larger effects at every level (60nan: -0.048 vs -0.036). Note that M itself read 0.0041 worse there.
- E35 replicated K on the other seed set: 6/21, worse on none, as did the pooled six seeds.
- E38 confirmed the bigger encoder on seeds E37 had not used.
- So the training-randomness and fold part of a winner's curse is ruled out empirically.
(b) The decisions followed rules fixed in advance, and those rules acted as vetoes rather than picking the lowest mean. The lowest-mean arms were rejected at least twice: E34's KC at 0.7412 (C and KC each lost spambase_20nan), and E31's column-wise scoring, superseded by E32. PG (E36) was not adopted either. That is not one-directional selection on the lowest mean.
(c) ADR 0012 (E29) was adopted on "no detectable difference", for cost, on 4 variants, not 21. It's not a score-selected adoption, so listing it overstates the selection count.
(d) The bar is itself picked on the same test cells: summary.py takes, per run and population, the baseline with the lowest CV-mean test score out of five. That oracle choice biases toward the baselines and partly offsets the model's dev-set advantage.
(e) E20 checked the bar's sensitivity to k. missForest, which per the ADR 0017 note quoted in summary.py would set the bar on most variants, is reported beside the bar as gap_to_missforest rather than hidden.
(f) ADR 0018 dropped electricity post hoc, but that arm gained nothing (+0.3%, no verdict), so the bias it adds to the 21-variant mean is about 0.0001.

What survives, at medium:
- Fresh seeds change the folds, masks and initialisation, but not the MCAR draw and not the 9 tables. Ticket 03 says so itself. Overfitting the design to these 9 tables and these draws is unmeasured.
- The model-vs-bar claim was never pre-registered as a confirmatory read.
- The finding's own cheap check, a fresh MCAR draw, would mainly test the draw. Only new tables test generalisation across tables. Its suggested fix (declare the 21 variants the development benchmark, then make one frozen confirmatory read on fresh draws or new tables) is still correct, as a thesis-level requirement rather than a code defect.

Why status is new: no prior review names serial reuse of test cells across experiments. Pieces of it are known:
- CONSOLIDATED states the single-draw scope ("this one missingness draw") and proposes the second draw as a repetition axis.
- F-08-3 / §3.3 (predefined validation rows are 8.5-13% of the CV test folds) is still open and applies to E39's seed-42 studies.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is real. There is one MCAR draw per (table, rate), and the seeds re-partition the same cells, so every adoption from E30 to E38 and the model-vs-bar read use the same induced cells. But the claimed impact does not hold up when I bound it. The finding treats the cumulative gain (0.7929 to 0.7446) as if it were selection optimism. It is not. Optimism is only the part of that gain that is noise tied to these particular cells, and here that part is small.

1. Each adoption is large compared with an upper bound on its cell-sampling noise. I took the pooled within-seed fold SD divided by sqrt(5). That bound also contains training noise, and seeds share cells, so it is not shrunk by sqrt(3). On the 21-variant mean:
   - M-A: -0.0184, SE <= 0.0041 (z -4.5)
   - G-M: -0.0203 / -0.0268, SE <= 0.0040 / 0.0046 (z -5.1 / -5.9)
   - K-H: -0.0073 / -0.0097, SE <= 0.0025 / 0.0034 (z about -2.9)
   - E38 adds only -0.0018 on a 21-variant mean (pendigits and letter).

   Every disjoint 2-fold subset of the cells shows the same sign for all five adopted contrasts. At z of 2.8 or more, the winner's-curse excess is a few percent of one SE. Even if every one of 10 tried options were null, keeping the best 5 of 10 gives about 3.7 sigma, roughly 0.015. The observed 0.048 is about three times that. A realistic optimism is 0.005 or less, against a gap to the bar of 0.0335 (-4.3%). Zeroing K entirely still leaves the model 3.1% below the bar.

2. The bar is selected on the same cells, but in the opposite direction. summary.py takes, per run, the minimum over the baselines of the CV test mean. When the bar is chosen out of sample it is 0.0011 to 0.0016 higher (worse), so the in-sample choice makes the comparison slightly harder for the model: gap -0.0330 against the in-sample bar versus -0.0346 out of sample.

3. Some held-out confirmation does exist. E30 tested M, found on 4 variants in E25/E26, on all 21: 8 of its 9 verdicts fall on variants outside the discovery set. Letter was not in the E37 screen and still gained 5.6% in E38. G and K were replicated on fresh seeds with the same or larger effects. Fresh seeds do not change the cells, but under MCAR the fold-to-fold spread over a fixed cell set is a first-order stand-in for draw-to-draw spread. A new draw would also change the observed training set, which the seeds do not capture.

4. Several statements in the finding are wrong or overstated:
   - E02 and E39 were selected on validation, not test: the Optuna objective ranks validation rows of a predefined split. Their only test contact is the known-open F-08-3 overlap of 8.5-13%.
   - E17 showed credit-g_20nan's promoted file was worse than defaults, the opposite of optimism.
   - Rejecting P, PG, C/KC or column-wise scoring cannot inflate the incumbent's number. C and KC even had better means and were still rejected.
   - E29 was adopted on "no difference".
   - BOOSTING_SEED is a seed, not a tuning knob.
   - "Never tuned" is overstated: E20 swept k (5/10/20, distance weighting), the bar takes the per-run best of knn5/knn10, and lgbm was added (ADR 0017).

finding.title: The verdict t pools 15 dependent fold pairs; counts and verdict variants change with the test, and the inferential target is never stated
finding.claim:
All 14 report scripts use the same interval(): a Student t on the 15 pooled fold differences with df=14, treating 5 folds x 3 seeds as iid. Within a seed, the folds partition the rows and share 75% of their training data. Across seeds, they score the same induced cells.

Empirical check, seeds as groups in a one-way ANOVA over 272 variant-contrasts: median F=0.65, and 1.5% reach p<0.05 against 5% nominal. Seed means vary LESS than iid predicts. So for the conditional question (these rows, this draw) the pooled t is roughly calibrated or conservative, and the exact seed-level t gives similar totals. For generalisation over row sampling, which is how statements such as "is a property of the method" read, the N&B correction (variance x (1/15 + 0.25); test 20%, train+val 80% per data.py:228-229) cuts counts sharply. N&B is likely over-conservative for paired arm differences and less apt still for within-run readouts (E31, E34, E35).

Counts per test, as (arm better / reference better):

| contrast | naive | Holm | N&B | seed-level t |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E30 M-A | 9/0 | 5/0 | 5/0 | 10/0 |
| E30 P-A | 7/2 | 5/0 | 3/0 | 4/0 |
| E30 P-M | 0/3 | 0/0 | 0/0 | 0/3 |
| E31 CW-mask | 5/6 | 1/3 | 1/1 | 2/3 |
| E32 G-M | 11/0 | 2/0 | 2/0 | 6/0 |
| E33 G-M | 13/0 | 9/0 | 7/0 | 9/0 |
| E34 K-H | 3/0 | 1/0 | 0/0 | 0/0 |
| E34 C-H | 13/1 | 10/0 | 5/0 | 7/1 |
| E35 K-H | 6/0 | 2/0 | 0/0 | 4/0 |
| E35 C-H | 13/1 | 10/0 | 7/0 | 7/0 |
| E37 ALL-R | 3/0 | 2/0 | 1/0 | 2/1 |
| E38 ALL-R | 3/4 | 2/1 | 2/0 | 3/2 |

Which variants get a verdict also changes. For E30 P-M, naive gives {biodeg_60nan, kc2_60nan, letter} and seed-level t gives {kr-vs-kp_40nan, spambase_20nan, spambase_60nan}: disjoint sets. The pooled rule also misses large consistent effects: spambase_60nan P-M is +0.069 with all seeds positive, naive p=0.074 (no verdict), seed-level p=0.012.

verdicts.reasoning:
The code fact holds. I re-ran the finding's reanalysis and every number in its table reproduces. Three parts of the finding are overstated, though, and they bring it down from high to medium.

1. **Seed-level t flips.** The seed-level t uses df=2, and most of its flips are a low-power artifact rather than better calibration. I fitted the model the finding itself recommends: a seed random effect, with the between-seed variance truncated at 0, using MSB with df=2 when F>1 and pooling when F<1. Under that model:
   - E30 P-M gives exactly the naive set {biodeg_60nan, kc2_60nan, letter_20nan}. The "disjoint sets" claim disappears.
   - E37 ALL-R stays at 2/0. biodeg_60nan has F=0.07 and no verdict, so ALL still advances. The claimed E37 flip is refuted.

2. **N&B.** The N&B column tests a target the repo explicitly disclaims: generalisation over row sampling (CONTEXT.md:16-20, ADR 0002:44-46). The finding itself concedes N&B is over-conservative for paired differences and within-run readouts.

3. **"Target never stated" is half true.** The general stance is documented: the internal CV interval measures within-run variability, not generalisation. The replication tickets also frame the question as "property of the change or of those draws", meaning the seeds. What is missing is narrower: no document defines what the pooled 15-pair verdict interval is an interval for.

**What survives:**
- The pooled t treats dependent pairs as iid. Where F>1 it is anti-conservative per variant. Example: E35 kr-vs-kp_80nan has F=1.85, naive p=0.0017, random-effects p=0.095.
- Three pre-registered readings sit right at their thresholds and change label even under the recommended random-effects model:
  - E31: supported becomes mixed (heavy 3/0, 6 no verdict).
  - E32: supported becomes mixed (heavy 4/0, 5 no verdict), so not "refuted" as claimed.
  - E35: replicated becomes "safe but weaker" (only spambase_80nan).
- ADR outcomes still survive. E33 under random effects is 10/0 with no M better, and E35 shows no H better.
- The wiki quotes the naive per-variant counts without naming the test (thesis-goals.md:86, trident.md:57, fork-experiments.md:76-82).

**Status against CONSOLIDATED §3.7 F-08-4:**
- The pairing half is fixed. All 14 scripts take paired arm-minus-reference differences per fold.
- The fold-overlap/dependence half is still open in code. For the ADR decisions it is mitigated by the fresh-seed replications (E33, E35) and by the rule that all three seeds must agree in sign.
- No BACKLOG or 2026-10-07 code-review item covers it.

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts in the finding hold up. All 14 report scripts use the same pooled 15-pair Student-t, and I reran stats_reanalyse.py and got exactly the table in the finding. Some per-variant counts and some pre-registered labels do change with the test. "High" severity does not hold, for five reasons.

(1) No ADR decision moves under any test. "Worse on none" holds under naive, Holm, N&B, seed-level t and a seed random-effects model, for every contrast that drove an ADR: E30 M-A (ADR 0013), E32/E33 G-M (ADR 0014), E34/E35 K-H (ADR 0015), and E38 ALL-R on pendigits and letter (ADR 0018, p ≤ 0.002 under every test).

(2) The project does state a target, as within-run: CONTEXT.md:16-20 says the interval "describes within-run variability, not independent test-set generalization". The replication tickets frame generalisation as being over seeds, not over row resampling ("a property of the change or of those draws", 03-replication-on-fresh-seeds.md:12-13; EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:984, 1052). So N&B is the wrong target by the project's own framing. The finding itself concedes N&B is over-conservative for paired differences and fits within-run readouts (E31, E34, E35) even less.

(3) For the declared conditional target, the pooled t is at or below nominal. The ANOVA gives median F 0.65, below the F(2,12) null median of about 0.73, and 1.5% of contrasts reach p<0.05 against 5% nominal. The near-null contrasts also behave: E36 PG-R gives 0/1 of 21 and E37 LN-R gives 0/1.

(4) Two of the finding's own sub-claims are wrong. First, seed-level t does not give "similar totals": it gives lower counts on most contrasts (E32 6/0 vs 11/0, E34 K-H 0/0 vs 3/0, E34 C-H 7/1 vs 13/1, E35 C-H 7/0 vs 13/1). That is power lost with df=2, not evidence the pooled test is off. Second, the E37 flip (ALL fails to advance) appears only under seed-level t (biodeg_60nan, p=0.043). Under the finding's own suggested fix, a seed random effect, biodeg_60nan does not flip: F ≤ 1 there, so the three seed means sit closer together than within-seed noise predicts, which is exactly where a df=2 t over-rejects. Under N&B and Holm, ALL still advances and wins the tie-break.

(5) The old §3.7 F-08-4 claimed fold overlap makes the interval understate how much the number moves "under a different partition". The new ANOVA points the other way: between-seed variance (seed = partition plus training draw) is at or below what iid predicts. The known concern is weaker than stated for the conditional question.

What survives, at medium. Under the conservative seed random-effects bound, counts drop about 20-30%: G-M goes 11→8 and 13→10, K-H 6→4 and 3→1, C-H 13/1→9/1 and 13/1→10/0, M-A 9→7. E35 changes from "replicated" to "safe but weaker" under N&B, seed-level t and the mixed model (1 or 0 of the three 80nan). That change is robust, but by the ticket's rule ADR 0015 still stands. The E31 and E32 heavy-gate labels drop to "mixed" under the mixed model and to "refuted" under N&B. E31 drove no ADR, and E32 was followed by E33, which is replicated naive, still replicated (5 heavy) under seed-level t, and safe but weaker under the mixed model.

The real open residue is reporting. The target in CONTEXT.md is never linked to the tickets, to the E30-E39 log entries or to the wiki. A grep for "internal CV" or "CONTEXT.md" in those places returns nothing. The wiki quotes bare counts (thesis-goals.md:86, trident.md:57, fork-experiments.md:76-82), and fork-experiments.md:37 names the rule but not its target. An examiner could challenge those counts, so this is not low; but no decision depends on it, so it is not high.

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts in the finding check out, so I'm not refuting it. I'm cutting its severity from high to medium and correcting one sub-claim.

What reproduces (HEAD b2b50fd): I reran the scratch reanalysis read-only, and it matches the finding's table cell for cell. All 14 *_report.py scripts use the same interval(): a pooled t with df = n-1 over the 15 fold pairs. confirmatory_report.py has not changed since commit 9298c52 (2026-10-01).

Why medium and not high:
1. **The dependence half is already known, at medium.** CONSOLIDATED.md:980-983 (§3.7, F-08-4) already says the five training sets overlap 75% pairwise and that a t-interval over folds understates partition variance. AUDIT.md:33 cut F-08-4 from high to medium. Since then only the pairing half has been fixed. The pre-registered tickets also flagged the approximation: imputation-pretraining/01:52-53 and 02:71-72 say "approximate: folds of one seed share training data".
2. **The finding's own ANOVA is the main point against "high".** Median F is 0.65, against 0.73 for iid F(2,12); 4 of 272 contrasts (1.5%) reach p<0.05. So seed means vary less than an iid model predicts, and for the conditional target the pooled t is calibrated or conservative. CONTEXT.md:16-20 defines exactly that target for the Internal CV interval: "within-run variability, not independent test-set generalization uncertainty". README.md:398 says the same. So "the inferential target is never stated" is wrong as written. The accurate version is narrower: the target is stated in the glossary and in the E24/E25 tickets, the "approximate" caveat is gone from the verdict-rule wording in later tickets (from E26, ticket 03-normalised, on), and EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:6 says "intervals are 95%" with no qualifier. The sign-agreement rule is a weak seed-level guard the project did reason about (ticket 07:57-59), which the finding doesn't credit. Ticket 03-replication:68-70 also notes that paired streams make the pairs tighter than independent draws.
3. **The dramatic flips come from tests the finding itself questions.**
   - Nadeau & Bengio's corrected t (N&B in the finding) is one the finding calls "likely over-conservative for paired arm differences". Example: E32 becomes "refuted" with 2 better, 7 no verdict. One more flip under N&B the finding missed: E30's reading would recommend P instead of M (both arms qualify, P-M 0/0).
   - The seed-level t has df=2 (critical value 4.30, low power).
   - For E30 P-M, all six variants in the two disjoint sets are borderline under both tests (p roughly 0.01 to 0.09). Two roughly calibrated tests disagreeing on borderline cases is expected noise, and both still give "M better than P" on 3, so the pre-registered E30 reading (M) is the same under seed-level t.
   - The tickets already flagged their verdicts at the threshold: 01-column-wise:143-146, 02-gaps-as-mask:180 and 03-replication:50-53.
4. **No decision changes under the tests the finding defends.**
   - The "worse on none" half of every wiki count is robust: the reference-better column is 0 for E32, E33 (G-M), E34 and E35 (K-H) under naive, Holm, N&B and seed-level t alike.
   - ADR 0014's adoption explicitly rests on that safety clause (03-replication:52-53).
   - E31 and E37 were screening steps superseded by follow-up studies (E32, E38) before any ADR.
   - ADR 0018's primary reading (E38: ALL better on pendigits and letter, R better on no large table) holds in every column.
   - Under seed-level t, E30 still yields M and E33 still "replicates" (5 of 9 heavy). E32 drops from supported to mixed (3 of 9), but E33 replicated it.

What stays open, and why this doesn't drop to low:
- **Test-dependence is new and correct.** The finding is the first to show that which variants get a verdict depends on the test: E30 P-M gives disjoint sets, and spambase_60nan's +0.069 (all three seeds positive, naive p=0.074) is missed.
- **The wiki quotes counts without the test or the target.** Affected lines: thesis-goals.md:86, trident.md:57, fork-experiments.md:76-82. "Better on 11 of 21" ranges from 2 to 11 across tests, and "13 of 21" from 7 to 13.
- **The scripts still apply no correction.**

The fix is documentation, not a change of decision: print the test name and the target next to each count, and add a seed-level or N&B sensitivity column. There is precedent in the repo: imputation-architecture/02:64 already uses (variant, seed) units for a secondary measure.

finding.title: Count-and-veto decision rule: error rate never calibrated, no practical margin; it refused calibration (ADR 0015) against 8-9 of 9 tables
finding.claim:
Decisions are tallies of per-variant verdicts, with a 'worse on none' veto and '>= k better' thresholds. There is no cross-dataset test, no multiplicity control and no smallest effect of interest.

Monte Carlo of the 3x5 design (stats_mc.py, 200k runs):
- Under iid, the false-verdict rate is 0.044 per test. The CI alone gives 0.050, so the all-seeds-agree filter removes only 0.006. One direction: 0.023.
- P(>=1 spurious 'worse' among 21 null variants): 0.38 iid, 0.89 at rho=0.1, 0.98 at rho=0.2.
- Expected spurious 'better' verdicts among 21: 0.48 iid, 3.4 at rho=0.2.
- A null arm passes E37's 5-variant advance rule with p≈0.09 iid, ≈0.27 at rho=0.2.
- The ticket's 'rarer than 1 in 20 per test' holds only under independence, and not because of the sign rule.

Decisions the veto made:
- **ADR 0015, calibration refused.** C-H is better on 9/9 tables in both seed sets (Wilcoxon9 p=0.0039 both). KC-K is better on 8/9 in both (p=0.0078 and 0.0117; median -0.4% relative). C was refused over spambase_20nan +0.0053 (E34). KC lost to K on spambase_20nan +0.005 (E34) and on kr-vs-kp_20nan +0.0115 and spambase_20nan +0.0033 (E35). Under N&B, KC qualifies and loses to neither in both E34 and E35.
- **ADR 0013:120, P refused.** This rests on two 'A better' verdicts at p=0.019 and 0.038 among 63 tests. Under Holm or N&B, P qualifies and the pre-stated rule ('P unless M better on >=3') recommends P. The table-level M-P comparison favours M on 8/9 (p=0.0078), so the outcome is right and the reason fragile.
- **E32.** 'Refuted if >=7 of 9 have no verdict' reads low power as evidence of absence.
- **E39.** It is being decided now with the same per-variant rule (retune_report.py:111-150).

- ADR 0013:120: the P decision has the right outcome for a fragile reason.

- More generally, the veto makes harmless candidates fail about 40% of the time under iid, while the '>=1 better' thresholds are cheap to meet by chance.

finding.suggested_fix:
- Primary test: a cross-table signed-rank or sign test on the relative effect, or a mixed model with table and seed random effects.
- Veto: an equivalence test (TOST) against a pre-stated SESOI (for example 1% relative), not 'no significant worse'.
- Holm across variants for any per-variant claim.
- State each gate's minimum detectable effect.
- Re-open the C/KC question with that reading.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's arithmetic is right. The conclusions drawn from it are not, and neither is the high severity.

1. **The code does what was pre-registered.** retune_report.py:113-152 implements the rule in the E39 ticket (01-retune-promoted-files.md:120-129) line for line. No code defect.

2. **The correlated Monte Carlo rows assume the wrong null.**
   - The iid rows reproduce: 0.022 one-direction per test, P(at least 1 spurious 'worse' of 21) = 0.37, expected 0.46.
   - The rho_b>0 rows (0.89 and 0.98; 3.4 spurious 'better'; E37 at 0.27) need seeds to be correlated given the variant. They are not: KFold/StratifiedKFold use random_state=seed (src/training/data.py:218,221), so each seed is an independent partition of the same table. A variant-level effect shared across seeds is a real effect on that variant, not noise.
   - I checked the within-seed clustering empirically: 189 variant-contrasts from E30, E34 and E35. The median between-seed F is 0.57 against 0.73 under the null, and only 2% exceed F.95(2,12), so there is no detectable positive clustering (implied rho_w about -0.05). The ticket's 'rarer than 1 in 20 per test' (01-column-wise-scoring.md:100) holds: 0.044.

3. **Veto census: no veto that changed a decision looks like chance.**
   - **E34/E35, C and KC (spambase_20nan).** The 'H better' vetoes on C-H and KC-K replicate in two independent seed sets: C-H at p=0.006 and 0.010, KC-K at p=0.0055 and 0.024, with 6/6 seeds positive in both contrasts. Under the null, the same variant being flagged twice happens about 1% of the time. The log names the mechanism: the model is already calibrated at 20nan (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:1077-1080).
   - **KC-K on kr-vs-kp_20nan.** +1.29% relative (E34, p=0.079, 3/3 seeds) and +1.96% (E35, p=0.006, 3/3 seeds). Both exceed the 1% SESOI the finding itself proposes, so the KC refusal survives its own suggested TOST fix. The harms (0.4-2.0% relative) are as large as or larger than the median gain (-0.4%).
   - **'Refused' overstates it.** C was routed to a refined pre-registered study (log :1041-1045, :1077-1080), not killed. ADR 0015 (:85-86) is about K and says nothing about calibration.
   - **E30, P (ADR 0013:120).** Both 'A better' vetoes are 3/3 seeds (kr-vs-kp_40nan p=0.019, spambase_40nan p=0.038). P is also +7.2% on spambase_60nan with 3/3 seeds. The cross-table reading favours M on 8/9 tables (p=0.0078).
   - **The finding's own fix would have got P wrong.** Under Holm(21) the two vetoes go to adjusted p of 0.27 and 0.49, and the three 'M better than P' verdicts to about 0.42, 0.42 and 0.59. P would then qualify and the rule would recommend it, which the finding's own cross-table test rejects. The finding concedes the outcome was right; it is the proposed remedy that is fragile.
   - **E36.** R better on electricity_20nan, one seed set. PG had zero 'better' verdicts and needed 3, so this veto was outcome-neutral.
   - **E37.** L4 and LN were vetoed, but ALL advanced on more 'better' verdicts anyway. E38 corroborates the depth harm on credit-g_20nan.
   - **E32 and E38.** The 'at least 7 no verdict' refutation clause never fired (E32 was supported), and no primary veto fired in E38.
   - **E39.** Each verdict decides one variant's file, so per-variant is the right unit. A false promotion swaps in an equivalent configuration, so the harm is bounded.

4. **What survives (low severity, new).** No prior review covers it. F-08-4 (08-experimentation-design.verdict.md:151-176) dealt with multiplicity in the September 12-pair design, which the seed-agreement rule later mitigated.
   - The 'worse on none' veto has no margin. A harmless candidate fails about 37% of the time across 21 variants under iid, and the docs don't say so.
   - No SESOI or MDE is stated. The per-variant MDE at 80% power is a median of about 0.7-1.0% relative for the within-run calibration contrasts and 2.2-2.6% for K-H and P-A, so the veto can fire on harms of about 0.5%.
   - Stating these operating characteristics, and a SESOI, is a documentation and design improvement. No adopted or refused decision is shown to be wrong.

verdicts.reasoning:
The arithmetic holds under iid: about 0.044 per test, 0.022 in one direction, and 0.38 for at least one spurious "worse" among 21 null variants. The material claims do not hold up.

1. **The high-correlation scenarios are refuted by the repo's own near-null experiment.** The alarming figures (0.89 and 0.98 for a spurious veto, 3.4 spurious "better" verdicts) all assume rho = 0.1 to 0.2. E36 (PG − R, paired random streams, level means within ±0.002) is the best null available.
   - Induced: one verdict among 21, the count the nominal rate predicts (0.92 expected). RMS of the 21 t statistics is 1.14 against about 1.08 under iid, which implies exchangeable rho ≈ 0.008.
   - Masked: no verdicts, RMS(t) 0.81, so rho ≤ 0.
   - The rule therefore runs near its nominal rate. The N&B factor 0.25 (equivalent to rho ≈ 0.2) is over-conservative for this design, and every "under N&B it reverses" counterfactual rests on it.

2. **ADR 0015: the veto fired on replicated harm, not on noise.** Seed means across both seed sets (101/202/303 and 42/7/13):
   - C − H on spambase_20nan is positive on 6 of 6 seeds (+0.0024 to +0.0099).
   - KC − K on spambase_20nan is positive on 6 of 6 (+0.0006 to +0.0069).
   - KC − K on kr-vs-kp_20nan is positive on 6 of 6 (+0.0033 to +0.015); E34 merely lacked the interval.

   A cross-table Wilcoxon asks "better on average"; the pre-registered rule asks "harms nowhere". Choosing the second is a policy choice, not a statistical error. E35's conclusion already names the follow-up: a calibration that leaves the 20nan tables alone. The stake is small: means 0.7446 → 0.7412 (E34) and → 0.7422 (E35), a median of about −0.4%. Not thesis-material.

3. **ADR 0013:120: the P refusal was overdetermined.** The E30 rule recommends P over M unless M is better than P on 3 or more variants, and M was better on exactly 3 (biodeg_60nan, kc2_60nan, letter). So M wins even if P had qualified. P was also worse than A on all three seeds of spambase_60nan (+0.070). Under Holm or N&B, those three M-over-P verdicts vanish (adjusted p 0.25 to 0.59), so the proposed fix would have recommended P. The finding itself concedes M is the better arm at table level (8 of 9). The correction would have made this decision worse.

4. **E32: the clause never fired.** "Refuted if 7 or more have no verdict" did not apply: G was better on 5 of the 9 heavy variants and M on none. E33 replicated it on fresh seeds.

5. **E37 was a screen, gated by a fresh-seed confirmation.** The p ≈ 0.09 chance of a null arm advancing only buys a confirmation. E38 ran that confirmation on seeds 101/202/303 and replicated the gain (pendigits −3.8%, letter −5.6%).

6. **E39 decides each variant on its own.** `recommendation()` decides each of the 5 files separately, over 3 contrasts each. Under the null, a spurious "promote T" or "remove file" swaps in a configuration that scores the same. The stake is low, and the pre-registered prior is "a small gain at most".

**Replication is the multiplicity control the finding does not credit.** Every adopted default was confirmed on an independent seed set: E32 by E33, E34 by E35, E37 by E38.

**Status:** CONSOLIDATED §3.7 (F-08-4) already flagged that the comparisons were read "simultaneously with no correction" and asked for paired differences and a stated family. Both landed: fold-pair intervals and the stated family of 21 (ticket 01:99-100). FWER is controlled de facto through fresh-seed replication, so this is known-mitigated.

**Genuine residue (low):**
- No smallest effect of interest and no stated detectable effect for the veto.
- Under a global null over 21 variants, the veto blocks a harmless candidate about 38% of the time.
- The ticket's "rarer than 1 in 20" is literally true at 0.044, but the seed-sign rule contributes only about 0.006 of it.
- A zero-cost improvement is to print N&B and seed-level-t columns beside the naive verdict in E39's report. None of this changes any decision made so far.

verdicts.reasoning:
The description of the rule is accurate. The claimed decision errors are not, so I refute the finding as stated and downgrade it from high/new to medium/known-mitigated.

What stands:
- Decisions are per-variant tallies with a "worse on none" veto.
- There is no family-wise control, no SESOI or equivalence test, and no cross-table test.
- The interval is a Student-t over 15 pooled fold pairs, so it ignores seed clustering (retune_report.py:100-103,121-122).
- Under iid, a harmless candidate fails a 21-variant veto about 38% of the time.
- The tickets' "rarer than 1 in 20 per test" is literally true (0.044), but the sign rule adds only 0.006 of that.

Why the headline impact fails:

1. **The ADR 0015 veto was not a chance casualty. It replicated.**
   - C-H on spambase_20nan is +0.0053 [+0.0018, +0.0088] on seeds 101/202/303 and +0.0055 [+0.0015, +0.0095] on seeds 42/7/13. All six seed means are positive (0.0059, 0.0045, 0.0056, 0.0042, 0.0024, 0.0099), with 12/15 folds positive in each set.
   - KC-K on spambase_20nan is +0.0050 and +0.0033, also positive on all six seeds.
   - Under iid, a same-variant, same-direction false verdict on two independent seed sets has probability about 0.0005, or about 0.011 for any of 21 variants.
   - Fisher-combined p for C-H spambase_20nan is about 0.0007. That survives Holm over 21 tests (0.05/21 = 0.0024), although neither seed set alone survives Holm or N&B.
   - So the veto detected a real, reproducible, small loss. Wanting to trade it for a cross-table mean gain (median -0.4%) is a policy preference (worst case versus mean), not a statistical error.
   - The project already reads it this way: E34 and E35 treat the loss as real and propose a calibration that spares the 20nan tables as the next study. That is a deferral, not a refusal.
   - ADR 0015 itself never rules on calibration. Only the log does.

2. **The rho>0 Monte Carlo rows are misread.**
   - stats_mc.py sets rho_w = rho_b (compound symmetry). That is one component shared by all 15 fold pairs of a variant: a real variant-level effect that would replicate, not noise. Calling those detections "spurious" assumes the estimand is the cross-variant mean, while the veto's estimand is per variant.
   - Pure seed noise (rho_w > rho_b) does inflate the rate: my MC gives 0.117 at seed variance 0.25 and 0.157 at 0.5.
   - The only near-null contrast, E36 PG-R, gave 1 verdict in 21. The iid rule predicts about 0.9, so the data fit the iid regime, not rho = 0.2.

3. **Spurious "better" verdicts are mitigated by practice, which the finding omits.** Every adopted default was replicated on fresh seeds before or after its ADR:
   - ADR 0014: E32, replicated by E33.
   - ADR 0015: E34, replicated by E35.
   - ADR 0018: the E37 screen was confirmed by the separate E38 study.

4. **ADR 0013 P: the finding concedes the outcome is right, and the reason is less fragile than claimed.**
   - P was worse than A on spambase_60nan by +0.070, with all three seeds positive (0.061, 0.039, 0.110).
   - M beat P on 3 variants.
   - P's "A better" verdicts have all seeds positive: kr-vs-kp_40nan (0.003, 0.010, 0.030) and spambase_40nan (0.024, 0.011, 0.007).

5. **E32's low-power "refuted" branch never fired** (G was better on 11 of 21 and replicated in E33). So no decision rests on it.

6. **E39 is a per-file decision with "keep F" as the status quo.**
   - The cross-table veto does not apply, which the finding's own cheap_check concedes.
   - E39 is pre-registered and in progress (EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:1177-1209), so it is prospective and cannot be faulted yet.
   - Printing seed-level and N&B calls beside the naive call is a useful report addition, not a defect.

Status:
- **Multiplicity.** CONSOLIDATED §3.7 / F-08-4 (medium) flagged uncorrected simultaneous reads and the missing paired quantity. Every ticket since E30 declares multiplicity as a known limit, and ticket 07 warns that a lone verdict deserves less weight. The paired 15-pair, 3-seed design plus fresh-seed replication is the mitigation.
- **Still open:**
  - no family-wise correction;
  - no SESOI or equivalence margin;
  - no cross-dataset test of the kind ML benchmark papers report (Wilcoxon or Friedman over tables);
  - the t-interval ignores seed clustering;
  - the "1 in 20" sentence credits the sign rule.
- **Why medium:** these weaken how the thesis can phrase generalisation claims and are cheap to add beside the tallies. None of them reverses an adopted decision.

finding.title: Multiplicity: family sizes are stated, never corrected
finding.claim:
The tickets count their families: 21, 20, 42 and 15 primary tests. No correction is applied. The masked population is read with the same rule, and the 39 sequential experiments have no overall budget.

Holm within each 21-variant family, on the naive p-values:

- E31: 5/6 to 1/3.
- E32: 11 to 2. E33: 13 to 9.
- E34: K 3 to 1; C 13/1 to 10/0.
- E35: K 6 to 2; C 13/1 to 10/0.
- E36: 0/1 to 0/0.

verdicts.reasoning:
I re-read the code and could not refute the finding. Every verdict function in scripts/experiments/*_report.py uses a fixed two-sided t.ppf(0.975, n-1) interval over the 15 pooled fold pairs and then requires the three seeds to agree in sign. No report applies Holm, Bonferroni or BH; grepping .py files finds none. The four family sizes appear at the cited ticket lines. All Holm recounts in the claim reproduce exactly from stats_reanalyse.py, including E30 M-A 9 to 5, E32 11 to 2 and E34 C 13/1 to 10/0.

Nothing elsewhere neutralises the problem. The tickets say that with the seed-agreement rule "a false verdict is rarer than 1 in 20 per test". A null simulation (iid folds, 3 seeds of 5) confirms that is literally true, but the rule only takes the per-test false-verdict rate from 5% to about 4.45%. That leaves a family-wise error of about 0.62 across 21 tests and 0.85 across 42, with roughly 0.9 false verdicts expected per 21-variant family. So the rule is not a multiplicity control.

The fresh-seed replications (E33, E35) guard against a lucky seed draw, but they do not settle the multiplicity question. ADR 0013 (E30) and ADR 0018 have no replication at all.

The impact is somewhat stronger than "inflated tallies", because pre-registered readings change under Holm:
- **E30:** both "A better than P" vetoes disappear (adjusted p 0.27 and 0.49), and M-better-than-P falls from 3 to 0. Under rule 2, P (the cheaper arm) would then be recommended instead of M. This is only a formal flip: the user took the decision, and P's near-failure on spambase_60nan is invisible to either rule.
- **E32:** the heavy-9 count of "G better" falls from 5 to 2, below the pre-registered threshold of 5. The reading becomes "mixed", not "supported". In the E33 replication it falls from 6 to 4, which is "safe, weaker". The safety clause (no variant worse) holds either way, so the ADR 0014 default still stands.
- **E34:** C's only veto (spambase_20nan, p 0.006, adjusted 0.062) disappears, so C would also qualify. But that veto replicates in E35 (p 0.010, the same sign on all six seeds), so calling it "spurious" is weak there. It is a real, small harm that Holm on one family cannot see.

The finding overstates a few points, which keeps it at medium rather than raising it:
- **E38's primary family:** the claim treats E38 as a 21-variant family, but its pre-registered primary is only the 3 large variants. pendigits and letter survive Holm (adjusted p about 0), so ADR 0018 is unaffected.
- **Masked population:** it is scored with the same verdict function, but every ticket and report already labels it secondary and does not rule on it ("The rule is on induced cells only"). That part of the suggested fix is already in place.
- **CONSOLIDATED.md:983:** this line refers to ADR 0005's six single-seed pairs (F-08-4), not to E30-E38. It shows the issue was raised before, but for a different family.
- **Direction of the error:** veto-direction errors push toward not adopting, which is conservative. Every rule was pre-registered with its family size stated.

The status is known-open. The tickets list multiplicity under "Known limits, stated in advance", and E30's ticket adds that a lone verdict among many nulls deserves less weight. Nothing at HEAD corrects for it, and BACKLOG and the 2026-10-07 review do not track it. E39's 15 primary verdicts use the same uncorrected rule (retune_report.py:113-127). I did not reanalyse E39 because its cells are not in stats_cells.pkl.

finding.title: 'Fresh-seed' replications refresh only partition and initialisation, and the seed sets were reused
finding.claim:
E33, E35 and E38 replicate across seeds. That changes the fold partition, the initialisation and the evaluation and corruption streams. It does not change the rows, the induced cells or their truth: there is one MCAR draw per (table, rate). Each seed set scores every induced cell 3 times, so a 'replication' cannot detect a result specific to the draw.

The seed sets are also not fresh across experiments:
- 101/202/303 were 'unused by any earlier imputation study' at E33. They were then reused by E34 (which decided ADR 0015), by E38 (whose reference is E34's K readout) and by E39.
- 42/7/13 served E30, E31, E32, E35, E36 and E37.

The second missingness draw that CONSOLIDATED §3.7 proposed as a repetition axis is still unused. The _20nan and _40nan masks are independent draws, but confounded with the rate.

- CONSOLIDATED.md:986-990 (fix direction, not done).

finding.suggested_fix: Name the axis in every replication ('seed replication on a fixed draw'). Add a draw-replication arm for the decisions the thesis cites.

verdicts.reasoning:
The facts in the finding are correct at HEAD, so I can't refute it. I'm downgrading it from medium to low because the impact it claims is overstated.

What holds:
(1) There is one MCAR draw per (table, rate). The injection seed is fixed at 42 + pct, and there is exactly one CSV per (table, rate).
(2) The run seed changes only the fold partition, the evaluation mask (seeded on (seed, fold)) and the global training stream. The truth comes from the fixed _00nan CSV, and the induced headline is scored on test rows only. So each induced cell is scored once per seed, 3 times per seed set.
(3) The seed-reuse history is as stated: 42/7/13 for E30, E31, E32, E35, E36 and E37; 101/202/303 for E33, E34, E38 and E39.
(4) No draw-replication arm exists anywhere. BACKLOG doesn't track one, and the fix direction in CONSOLIDATED §3.7 was never carried out. The status therefore stays known-open.

Why it's downgraded:
(a) The ADR-level claims are tallies over 21 variants, and each variant is its own MCAR draw on a different table or with a different injection seed (62/82/102/122). A result specific to one draw would have to repeat, in the same direction, across 13 independent draws (E33) or 6 (E35) to produce those tallies. "Cannot detect a result specific to the draw" is true of each variant's verdict, including the "worse on none" safety clause. It is not true of the method-level statements, so "limits ADR 0014 and 0015 as statements about the method" overstates the problem. What is tied to the draw is the per-variant claims, such as "K better on credit-g_80nan".
(b) The scope was partly stated before the run. E33's pre-registration says it replicates over seeds and keeps "same variants", which means the same draws. Its next phrase, though, says a fresh seed changes "the masks", which is ambiguous. E35's ticket, the log and the wiki say nothing about the draw being fixed, so the naming fix is not done in general.
(c) The seed reuse doesn't misstate freshness. Each "fresh" is qualified against the experiment that made the selection: at E33 the set was unused by any earlier study (true then), and at E38 it was "unused by E37". The sets also alternate (A, B, B, A, A, B), so ADR 0014, 0015 and 0018 were each chosen on one set and confirmed on the other, a two-set cross-replication. What remains: both seed sets now carry the whole sequential decision history, so no untouched seed set is left for a final confirmation. And because the folds depend only on the seed, every experiment on a set shares the same 15 partitions. ADR 0013 (E30) rests on 42/7/13 alone, a gap the finding doesn't mention.
(d) The finding itself admits that the _20nan/_40nan "second draw" is confounded with the rate, so it isn't a usable repetition axis. A real draw replication needs new CSVs.

Minor citation slips:
- CONSOLIDATED:986-990 is the observation; the fix direction is at 1039-1044.
- wiki fork-experiments.md:79 never says "replicated"; it says "E32 on fresh seeds" and "ADR 0014 stands".
- thesis-goals.md:86 is already limited to "imputation task under MCAR only".

The remaining problem is scope and wording, with a cheap fix: name the axis everywhere, and run one alternative draw for the decisions the thesis cites. That makes it low severity.

finding.title: Tallies weight negligible and large effects equally; no smallest effect of interest
finding.claim:
Of the 108 naive verdicts in E30-E38, 13% have |Δ|<0.005 and 17% are below 0.0066. Examples: letter -0.0014 (E32); letter +0.0013 and pendigits +0.0011 (E31, both counted as 'mask better'); pendigits and letter -0.0017 and credit-g_20nan -0.0016 (E34 C-H). Each of these counts the same as kc2_60nan -0.093.

The right noise floor for paired contrasts is the SD of the per-seed mean paired difference. Over 272 variant-contrasts its median is 0.0066 (IQR 0.003-0.0115), which happens to equal E12's unpaired 0.0066 on credit-g_20nan. E12 measured only single-arm, unpaired seed noise. No ticket defines an effect size of interest.
finding.evidence:

- EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:917-920 (E31's light variants) and 958-966 (E32).

finding.impact: Inflates the 'better/worse on k' counts in the wiki and, through the veto, lets a 0.5% effect decide (the ADR 0015 calibration).

finding.suggested_fix: Report the relative effect (%) with a seed-level interval per variant. Pre-register a SESOI and read the veto as an equivalence test.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding joins two claims. Only one of them holds.

Strand A holds: the tallies ignore magnitude and no smallest effect of interest exists. I recomputed this read-only from the pickles. There are 108 naive verdicts over 272 variant-contrasts, and the per-contrast tallies match the log exactly (E30 9/0, 7/2, 0/3; E31 5/6; E32 11/0; E33 13/0; E34 K 3/0, C 13/1; E35 K 6/0, C 13/1; E36 0/1; E38 3/4). Of those verdicts, 14 (13%) have |d|<0.005 and 18 (16.7%) have |d|<0.0066, and every example quoted in the finding reproduces. In relative terms, 12% of verdicts are under 0.5% of the reference score and 17.6% under 1%; the median is 2.2%. A grep of docs/ outside docs/reviews finds no SESOI, equivalence or non-inferiority margin in any ticket or ADR. So refuted=false, and status new: the nearest prior items differ. 08-experimentation-design.md:83 covers fold and seed variance plus family-wise error, and 2026-10-07-code-review:308 covers --tally paths that omit the verdict.

Strand B is refuted: the "noise floor" argument fails. The 0.0066 is a pooled median over 272 heterogeneous contrasts, and its IQR runs from 0.003 to 0.0115. It is not a floor for any one variant. The small verdicts the finding names sit on variants whose own seed-mean SD is 0.0001 to 0.0010. Measured against that, letter (E35 C-H) is 20x its own SD, letter (E34 C-H) 16.8x, pendigits (E34 C-H) 11.4x and letter (E31) 13.7x. The pendigits and letter C-H effects also replicate across both seed sets. These effects are tiny, not noisy. The match with E12's 0.0066 is a coincidence: E12 measured one variant, one arm and five seeds.

The impact is overstated. Every count in the log and the wiki sits next to its per-variant deltas and the mean by missing level, so magnitudes are visible. No adopted default turned on an effect under 1%:
- ADR 0013: M's smallest win is -0.012. Letter's +0.0018 P-M verdict was moot, because P had already failed on two A-better verdicts of +0.014.
- ADR 0014: letter's -0.0014 is a 20nan variant, outside the 5-of-9 heavy-variant rule.
- ADR 0015: K's smallest E34 win is -0.010 (1.0%).
- ADR 0018: the effects are -3.8% and -5.6%.
- E36 and E37: electricity's veto is +0.0105 (about 1.4%). ALL advances on its two wins of 1% or more, whatever happens to credit-g_80nan's -0.57%.

A sub-1% effect decided an outcome in one place only: the rejection of C and of KC over K in E34, on spambase_20nan (+0.0053, +0.62%). It replicated in E35 (+0.0055), and all six seeds are positive. That veto blocked a change rather than adopting one. The ticket explains the mechanism (the alpha of 0.83 shrinks guesses that were well calibrated) and names the follow-up. A SESOI would flip it only at a margin of 0.65% or more.

Some mitigation is already in place. E38 reports the mean relative change with a seed-level interval, which is half the suggested fix, and E29 flagged a 0.2% lean as negligible. This is a protocol-design gap: the zero-margin count rules were pre-registered on purpose. It is not a code defect. The suggested fix stays useful: a pre-registered SESOI, for example 1% relative read against the seed-level interval, would turn the C/KC call into an explicit equivalence decision. Severity goes from medium to low.

finding.title: Per-run t(df=4) logged as ci95; training corruption stream still unmatched between arms (F-12-2)
finding.claim:
Two separate issues.

First, summary.py logs a 5-fold Student t (df=4) as ci95_lower/ci95_upper for every metric, gap_to_best_baseline included. EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:6 says 'intervals are 95%', while CONTEXT.md:16-20 says the internal CV interval is within-run variability and tells writers to avoid 'confidence interval'.

Second, F-12-2 is still open:
- Training corruption draws from the global numpy stream (src/utils.py:75,89).
- The global seed is set once (src/training/runner.py:71).
- Only the evaluation mask is reseeded per (seed, fold) (src/training/data.py:176).

So 'pairs share their random stream' (06-pretraining-gaps-as-mask.md:78) holds only until the draw counts diverge. This adds variance to arm differences (conservative); it does not bias them.
finding.evidence:
- src/training/summary.py:166-185, 260-270
- CONTEXT.md:16-20
- docs/EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:6
- src/utils.py:75,89
- src/training/runner.py:71
- src/training/data.py:176
finding.impact: Wording in thesis tables; slightly wider paired intervals in cross-run contrasts (E30, E32, E33, E36-E38).
finding.cheap_check: grep ci95 in the thesis or wiki tables; compare cross-run vs within-run paired SDs from stats_reanalyse.py.
finding.suggested_fix: Label the per-run band 'internal CV interval (t, 4 df)' in write-ups. Seed corruption per (seed, fold, stage, epoch) behind a flag, as CONSOLIDATED §3.7 proposed.

verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism holds at HEAD (b2b50fd), with every cited line accurate. The finding overstates both the documentation conflict and the impact, so I am downgrading its scope but keeping the severity.

Part 1, interval naming.
- The code part is true. summary.py:260-270 builds the per-run band through _student_t_interval (summary.py:330-341), which uses t.ppf(0.975, df=n-1), so df=4 at 5 folds.
- The band is stored as ci95_lower/ci95_upper (types.py:465-478) and logged under those MLflow keys (tracking.py:443-444). _paired_gaps (summary.py:166-185) gives gap_to_best_baseline the same band.
- The claimed conflict in the docs does not exist:
  - EXPERIMENTATION_LOG.md:6 says "intervals are 95%", not "confidence interval".
  - CONTEXT.md:16-20 defines the internal CV interval as a 95% Student-t interval, so the log agrees with the glossary.
  - The log names t(4) explicitly at :353 and :356, and :166 warns that single-arm intervals are not a test of a difference.
- No ci95 appears in the wiki. thesis-goals.md:92,135 uses "95% CI" for a planned repeated-splits design, not for the per-run band. So the "wording in thesis tables" impact is nil today.
- What is left is cosmetic: the field names use "ci", which the glossary says to avoid, and log:6 covers both the per-run t(4) band and the 15-pair t(14) verdict band in one sentence without giving df.

Part 2, F-12-2.
- It is still open at HEAD:
  - Training corruption is drawn only from global numpy (utils.py:75, utils.py:89).
  - The seed is set once per run (runner.py:71).
  - Only evaluation_mask (data.py:174-179) and the preview sampler (artifacts.py:218) get their own stream.
- CONSOLIDATED §3.7 proposed two fixes; only the paired-difference one landed (_paired_gaps, and the 15-pair seed-agreement rule from E24 on). The per-(seed, fold, stage, epoch) stream flag was never added.
- The impact list is mostly wrong. For most of the named experiments the numpy stream is matched between arms by construction:
  - **E32, E33, E36:** gaps_as_mask is a pure tensor transform applied after the draw (pretraining.py:103-107, decoding.py:88,128), and decode_patience defaults to 0 (types.py:226). Each pair makes the same draws, in the same number, in every fold. So ticket 06:78's "pairs share their random stream" is literally true for E36, which tickets 02:175-176 and 06:36 state and verify.
  - **E37, E38:** an architecture change only touches torch (embedder.py:191-197 init, randperm at pretraining.py:110 and decoding.py:130). The numpy corruption masks stay identical; the torch drift is inherent to changing the architecture.
- The stream really diverges only where an arm changes draw counts:
  - E30: arm A decodes 150 epochs, M 450, P up to 450 with patience 50 (ticket 07:18-20). Folds 2-5 diverge.
  - E27: early stopping, already acknowledged in ticket 04:47-49.
  - E39 (in progress): PROB_MASCARA differs between arms, and the floor loop's choice count depends on the data, so draws diverge within fold 1, as the F-12-2 verdict measured.
- The finding is right that the effect is conservative: unmatched corruption adds noise to paired differences and does not bias them.

Net: the defect is real but small and already known, and its stated impact is overstated. Low and known-open stand.
